# LAYER_BOUNDARIES

This document separates the release into layers that must not be collapsed.

## 1. Active base layer

- Includes:
  - `BaseCore`
  - typed dynamics, rigidity, inverse-limit identity, operational-criterion grammar
- Does not include:
  - bridge confirmation
  - runtime validation
  - human comparators
- Valid assertions:
  - internal formal derivation inside stated assumptions
- Prohibited automatic inferences:
  - BaseCore in release -> runtime instantiation
  - BaseCore -> external validation

## 2. Downstream formal packages

- Includes:
  - Papers I-IX
  - downstream formal extensions, bridges, protocols, and burden stacks
- Does not include:
  - active base ownership
  - public empirical closure
- Valid assertions:
  - downstream formal extension under explicit dependence
- Prohibited automatic inferences:
  - downstream package -> active base layer
  - Paper IX -> bridge completion

## 3. Legacy and lineage material

- Includes:
  - canonical_core_legacy
  - historical frozen core PDFs
  - parallel lineages
  - NotebookLM mirrors and reconstructions
- Does not include:
  - active source-of-truth authority
- Valid assertions:
  - archival provenance and editorial traceability only
- Prohibited automatic inferences:
  - legacy or mirror -> current spine

## 4. Implementation / system

- Includes:
  - `QICN-SYSTEM`
  - runtime artifacts
  - support labels
  - export policies
- Does not include:
  - theorem closure
  - ontology
  - external validation
- Valid assertions:
  - operational support and governance only
- Prohibited automatic inferences:
  - implementation exists -> theory validated
  - runtime metrics -> phenomenological theorem confirmed

## 5. Interpretation / language

- Includes:
  - explanatory readings
  - controlled terminology
  - non-claim language policy
- Does not include:
  - theorem proofs
  - public validation
- Valid assertions:
  - disciplined restatement of what the formal layers may suggest
- Prohibited automatic inferences:
  - interpretation -> closed theorem
  - bridge language -> bridge support

## 6. External validation

- Includes:
  - independent replication
  - independent methodological review
  - external empirical confirmation
- Does not include:
  - local release bundles
  - local smoke suites
  - governance docs
- Valid assertions:
  - none are granted by this reconstruction alone
- Prohibited automatic inferences:
  - release sync -> external validation

## Bridge rules

- Allowed bridge: base layer -> downstream packages only through explicit dependency.
- Allowed bridge: corpus -> system only through explicit interface docs.
- Allowed bridge: implementation -> internal evidence only through policy-governed artifacts.
- Disallowed bridge: legacy -> active base.
- Disallowed bridge: mirror lineage -> source-of-truth.
- Disallowed bridge: internal evidence -> public claim closure.

# THEORY_SYSTEM_INTERFACE

This document fixes the explicit boundary between `QICN-RELEASE` and `QICN-SYSTEM`.

## Public corpus areas with an operational counterpart

- Paper IV
  - operational reflection: admissibility, baseline handling, comparator discipline, invalidation rules
- Paper V
  - operational reflection: invariant diagnostics, criterion-facing structure, rupture semantics, admissible support burdens
- Paper VI
  - operational reflection: prediction family diagnostics, downgrade logic, negative controls, internal support-status surfaces
- Paper VII
  - operational reflection: descriptor families and runtime-facing diagnostics for operational life, structural class, and subjecthood
- Paper VIII
  - operational reflection: self-index, ownership, continuity, perspective, valuation, intervention, reducibility, and internal gate diagnostics
- Paper IX
  - operational reflection: bridge predicate registries, provisional bridge surface modules, burden-stack alignment, and non-claim grammar only
- ROEO annexes and governance docs
  - operational reflection: export surfaces, terminology policy, controlled statements, surface policy

## What the system does not close

- BaseCore as real-world theorem confirmation
- external validation of Papers IV-IX
- bridge admissibility
- human consciousness, human subjectivity, or metaphysical subjecthood
- automatic promotion of runtime subjectivity or bridge surfaces into claim-facing release status

## What must not be inferred

- runtime metrics -> public theorem confirmation
- internal support labels -> external validation
- descriptor families -> current system is an operational subject
- provisional bridge surfaces -> phenomenal bridge support
- public release alignment -> phenomenality, human equivalence, or external adjudication

## Interface policy

- the interface remains explicit, limited, and one-way by default
- every bridge from corpus to system remains tagged as operational or governance-only unless external validation exists
- Paper IX may guide bridge-facing runtime architecture as public corpus material, but every runtime-facing bridge surface remains provisional and non-confirmatory

# GLOSSARY_CANONICAL.v1

## Scope

Canonical terminology and reading rules for the live public release trunk.

## Core package terms

- **BaseCore**: the active mathematical base layer and source-of-truth package
- **canonical_core_legacy**: preserved historical package, not the active base
- **downstream public package**: a released package that depends on BaseCore or earlier packages without becoming the base
- **mirror / reconstructed lineage**: preserved non-primary material kept for genealogy, comparison, or audit traceability

## Canonical operational term policy

- preferred technical term for non-human runtime-facing readouts: **readout interno operacional**
- not allowed as public technical claims:
  - human qualia
  - phenomenality proven
  - bridge confirmed
  - the system feels
  - subjectivity achieved

## Boundary

Terminology policy constrains release reading only. It does not authorize runtime-to-theory escalation, bridge confirmation, or human-equivalence claims.

papers.name: BaseCore
papers.role: fuente formal activa (source of truth); el resto depende de ella
papers.title: Mathematical Foundations for Controlled Projective Systems
papers.abstract: This document presents the foundational mathematical layer of the Rigid Identity Framework. It consolidates the core theorem-level apparatus on which downstream papers depend, without borrowing hypotheses from later application layers. Specifically, this base monograph proves contractive projection dynamics, typed computable witnesses, parameterwise non-collapse under explicit anti-constant assumptions, inverse-limit identity under non-finite-determination assumptions, conditional rigidity under admissible perturbation models, conditional obstruction to uniform response fidelity under a binary representation budget, and operational-criterion grammar together with explicit falsation and scope boundaries. The typed disk witness has an exact regular-point spectral classification. A compact Hilbert rotation-block model has infinitely many nonzero spectral values. Variational criteria certify non-collapse on partial convex intersections. A joint small-gain bound yields mesh-to-continuum equilibrium convergence with evolving coherence, energy and phase. A common invariant-subspace test obstructs differentiable product charts for controlled dynamics.

papers.name: Paper I
papers.role: identidad rígida y fundamentos (paquete derivado público)
papers.title: Projective Compatibility and Sectorial Deformation Resistance
papers.abstract: We introduce a formal framework for rigid identity as a mathematical object emerging from the dynamics of observable systems under minimal structural constraints. Identity is defined as an inverse limit over a family of locally corrupted states linked by retroinductive projection maps, yielding a globally invariant object despite persistent environmental perturbations. For a common metric tower, exact fiber lifts with bounded weighted amplification yield a Hausdorff bound. papers.abstract: We study structural assignments from inverse-limit histories into an abstract metric codomain. Exact equality of all finite readouts forces factorization through the first cut and is incompatible with the required non-factorization. We replace that equality by uniformly summable readout increments, retaining non-factorization as a separately checked condition. An explicit binary-prefix system with ternary readouts realizes both conditions. It gives uniform approximation, a global lower and upper readout bound, and an exact minimax error for each finite observation budget. Continuity follows from controlled approximation by continuous finite readouts. Cross-system fragmentation and invariance require typed comparison domains and audited transports; a scalar rigidity label alone does not imply them. Under those comparison hypotheses we derive loss and normalized protection statements, including uniform perturbation bounds for both functionals on compact comparison models. Phenomenal and normative interpretations require independent bridge premises.

papers.title: Witness-Relative Exclusion of Joint Null Readouts
papers.abstract: We introduce an abstract structural readout space $\E$ and a compatibility operator $\Phi: Z \to \E$ on a declared metric comparison domain. We define a null regime $\nullphi \in \E$ and prove a Phenomenological Instability Theorem: under a certified positive lower readout bound, two defined, separated witness values cannot both equal the null element. CCR is a possible application class and is not needed for this metric implication. Consequently, a CCR realization with such a witness induces a witness-relative non-null separation. The result is negative-structural: it does not posit experience; it forbids one typed joint-null configuration under stated hypotheses. We provide explicit coupling bounds in two canonical families (profinite and symbolic dynamics) and prove factorization on a faithful image and a finite-prefix approximation bound. We also prove countable metric--Polish consistency, a conditional channel--projection law and explicit noise margins connecting approximation to finite-budget and null-separation bounds. The results are metric, order-theoretic and representation-relative; physical interpretation requires additional evidence.

papers.abstract: This paper specifies a falsification-first protocol for evaluating QICN under strict forensic admissibility constraints. The design is intentionally claim-bounded: the target is comparative structural-functional support, not phenomenological proof. The protocol instantiates five core predictions, mandatory ablation baselines, fixed seeds, and pre-registered decision gates. Statistical inference is defined ex ante with primary-metric priority, effect-size thresholds, and multiplicity correction. To prevent post-hoc inflation, evidence is admissible only if packet integrity, replay consistency, and runtime budget constraints pass simultaneously. We introduce a version-frozen operational triple $(A, J, W)$ (actuator set, objective functional, workspace interface), and require semantic version bumps for incompatible changes. We further include latency invalidation criteria and baseline obligations (heuristic, planner-off, world-model-off) for all key experiments. The strongest admissible conclusion remains constrained comparative support for audited cognition-operational hypotheses. A typed external interface adds identification, sensory/motor calibration, matched sham/disconnection controls and design-conditional error and power bounds. No biological dataset or external experiment is supplied.

Instead, it defines a framework-internal class $\Cop$ and an associated family of certified response classes $\Qop(S)$ for admissible systems \[ S = (X,\Phi,C,R,\Gamma,U), \] where $X$ is state space, $\Phi$ is dynamics, $C$ is effective causal structure, $R$ is a readout family, $\Gamma$ is an admissibility bundle, and $U$ is the set of admissible interventions. The criterion is organized around six critical invariants: structural persistence, rigid identity, causal integration, operational continuity, non-null differentiation, and operational legibility. Each invariant is defined explicitly, tied to an upstream corpus dependency, and paired with a failure mode. On that basis the paper proves four framework-internal results: conditional membership given six jointly realized witnesses on admissible support, substrate invariance under exact structural equivalence, approximate stability under bounded admissible perturbations, and rupture under invariant loss. A further corollary establishes biological non-primacy: biology is not a primitive constitutive variable for the class under study, but one admissible realization among others provided the invariants are preserved. The criterion is not narrative. Every major claim is backed by a definition, a proposition, a theorem, a proof sketch, or an explicit dependency on the canonical corpus. The resulting paper adds a new role to the framework: it formalizes the level at which substrate ceases to be explanatorily primitive without reopening the ownership of the Core, Rigid Identity, Structural Assignment Regimes, Null-Regime Instability, or Forensic Predictions. The analytic risk, coverage, and Gaussian-comparison theorems are mathematical protocol results; no executed campaign results are reported. The protocol separates internal certificates from admissible human-comparator evidence, defines preregistration freeze and amendment rules, and specifies independent reviewer selection, blinding, matched interventions, negative controls, and coverage-aware decision rules. Explicit gates distinguish rehearsal, session zero, and the first admissible collection event. The article reports no human comparator results or external adjudication verdicts and makes no claim of human equivalence, superiority, inferiority, cross-substrate identity preservation, metaphysical subjecthood, or final comparative conclusions.

theorems.statement: [Why this witness does not certify H5] The image of T_u lies in the constant subspace mathcal I _ mathrm c . Therefore its fixed point is constant by construction. This witness is correct and useful for typing and state spectral analysis, but it cannot certify the parameterwise anti-constant hypothesis H5 from Section~ ref sec:parameterwise-noncollapse .

theorems.statement: [Separate Witness for H5] The family T_u^ mathrm ac _ u in U satisfies Hypotheses~ ref hyp:H1 -- ref hyp:H5 of Section~1.

BaseCore therefore distinguishes two roles cleanly: the Golden Mean witness certifies typed operator correctness and state contraction; the affine anti-collapse witness certifies the stronger H5 burden needed for parameterwise non-collapse.

theorems.title: Parameter-Family Persistence is not State Spectrum

theorems.title: What has been removed
theorems.statement: [What has been removed] The previous text incorrectly mixed strict contraction with a state-spectrum eigenvalue lambda =1 . BaseCore no longer does that. Any neutral or persistent mode must now be interpreted as a mode of variation across the parameter family, not as an eigenmode of the contractive state Jacobian.

theorems.title: Realization of the Three Regimes and Rank Ablation
theorems.statement: [Realization of the Three Regimes and Rank Ablation] For any unit v in mathcal N^ perp , the forcing Gamma (t)=tv-K_ infty P_ B_1 (tv) on 0 leq t leq 2 realizes the interior, sphere and exterior at t<1 , t=1 and t>1 , respectively. Its equilibrium is nonconstant for t>0 . Replacing K_ infty by the single block K_ mathrm mean f=qf_0 e_0 gives spectrum 0,q and a one-step annihilation of every nonconstant mode of the linear operator.

theorems.title: Projective System of State Spaces
theorems.statement: [Projective System of State Spaces] Let S_t _ t in mathbb N be a family of non-empty state spaces together with projection maps [ pi _ t+1 to t :S_ t+1 to S_t ] satisfying the compatibility rule [ pi _ t+1 to t circ pi _ t+2 to t+1 = pi _ t+2 to t qquad forall t in mathbb N . ]

theorems.title: Identity as Inverse Limit
theorems.statement: [Identity as Inverse Limit] The identity object associated with the projective system is [ Id := varprojlim S_t = left (x_t)_ t in mathbb N in prod _ t in mathbb N S_t ; middle | ; pi _ t+1 to t (x_ t+1 )=x_t forall t right . ]

theorems.title: Identity neutrality
theorems.statement: [Identity neutrality] In BaseCore, Id is a structural inverse-limit object only. It carries no automatic phenomenological, biological, or metaphysical interpretation.

theorems.label: hyp:topo
theorems.title: Topological Regularity
theorems.statement: [Topological Regularity] Each S_t is compact Hausdorff and each pi _ t+1 to t is continuous and surjective.

theorems.label: hyp:nfd
theorems.title: NFD: Non-Finite Determination
theorems.statement: [NFD: Non-Finite Determination] For every t in mathbb N , the canonical projection [ p_t: Id to S_t, qquad p_t((x_k)_k)=x_t ] is not injective. Equivalently, [ forall t exists x,y in Id quad x neq y quad text and quad p_t(x)=p_t(y). ]

theorems.title: Persistent future branching as an operational form of NFD
theorems.statement: [Persistent future branching as an operational form of NFD] A sufficient operational strengthening of Hypothesis~ ref hyp:nfd is: for every t there exists k>t and x_t in S_t such that the fiber of pi _ k to t over x_t contains at least two globally extendable compatible histories. BaseCore keeps the weaker NFD statement as the primary assumption because it is exactly what the non-locality theorem needs.

theorems.label: prop:nonlocality
theorems.title: Non-Locality of Identity under NFD
theorems.statement: [Non-Locality of Identity under NFD] Assume Hypotheses~ ref hyp:topo and ref hyp:nfd . Then no canonical finite-time observation determines identity. More precisely, for every t the canonical projection [ p_t: Id to S_t ] is not injective, so identity is not recoverable from any finite slice through the projective observation maps.

theorems.title: What is \emph{not} proved here
theorems.statement: [What is emph not proved here] BaseCore does not prove that no arbitrary set-theoretic injection Id to S_t can exist in every imaginable inverse system. It proves the narrower and correct claim that the canonical projective observations p_t are not injective under Hypothesis~ ref hyp:nfd .

theorems.label: thm:noprogressive
theorems.title: No Canonical Progressive Recovery under NFD
theorems.statement: [No Canonical Progressive Recovery under NFD] Assume Hypothesis~ ref hyp:nfd . No finite canonical prefix map determines the inverse-limit identity object.

theorems.label: ass:rig1
theorems.title: RIG-1: Common Metric Stages
theorems.statement: [RIG-1: Common Metric Stages] Both towers use the same nonempty complete metric stages (S_t,d_t) and continuous bonding maps. Use the weighted history metric below with w_t operatorname diam (S_t) to 0 . This fixes the ambient space used for both Hausdorff directions.

theorems.label: ass:rig2
theorems.title: RIG-2: Controlled Propagation
theorems.statement: [RIG-2: Controlled Propagation] For the fiber lifting constants K_t>0 of RIG-3 define q_t=w_ t+1 K_t/w_t . Require C= sup _ 0 leq k leq t< infty prod _ j=k ^t q_j< infty . In particular q_t leq 1 at each stage suffices.

theorems.label: ass:rig3
theorems.title: RIG-3: Exact Fiber Lifts in Both Towers
theorems.statement: [RIG-3: Exact Fiber Lifts in Both Towers] For each f in pi _t, widetilde pi _t , u in S_ t+1 and v in S_t , there exists u' in S_ t+1 with f(u')=v and d_ t+1 (u,u') leq K_t d_t(f(u),v) . The same K_t bounds both lifts. No continuous selection is required.

theorems.label: ass:rig4
theorems.title: RIG-4: Typed Projection Defects
theorems.statement: [RIG-4: Typed Projection Defects] Write pi _t= pi _ t+1 to t and widetilde pi _t= widetilde pi _ t+1 to t . Require sup _ u in S_ t+1 d_t( pi _t(u), widetilde pi _t(u)) leq epsilon _t< infty .

theorems.title: RIG-5: Summable Deformation
theorems.statement: [RIG-5: Summable Deformation] Require E_w= sum _ t geq 0 w_t epsilon _t< infty .

theorems.title: Weighted Deformation Size
theorems.statement: [Weighted Deformation Size] The weighted deformation size is | epsilon _ bullet |_w=E_w . When epsilon _t is the exact supremum projection defect this specifies a cost on the common-stage perturbations. An independently defined intervention cost needs its own quantitative relation to this sum.

theorems.label: def:weighted-metric
theorems.title: Weighted Product Metric

theorems.label: prop:weighted-history
theorems.title: Finiteness, Completeness and Compactness of Weighted Histories
theorems.statement: [Finiteness, Completeness and Compactness of Weighted Histories] The formula is finite on every pair in the full product exactly when the weighted diameters are bounded outside a finite set of stages. For finite-diameter stages this is equivalent to B= sup _t w_t operatorname diam (S_t)< infty . For any nonempty inverse limit I and b in I , it is finite on all of I exactly when I subseteq P_b . If the coordinate spaces are complete and the bonding maps continuous, P_b and I cap P_b are complete. If w_t operatorname diam (S_t) to 0 , the weighted metric induces the product topology and [ 0 leq d_w(x,y)- max _ 0 leq t leq N w_t d_t(x_t,y_t) leq sup _ t>N w_t operatorname diam (S_t). ] In this case compact coordinate spaces give a compact inverse limit. Surjective bonding maps give a compatib

theorems.label: ex:weighted-tail-failures
theorems.title: Two Distinct Tail Failures
theorems.statement: [Two Distinct Tail Failures] On S_t=[0,1] with identity bonding maps and w_t=2^ -t , choose d_t(s,u)=4^t|s-u| . The two constant histories 0 and 1 have distance + infty . For a different failure, take S_t= 0,1 ^t with prefix deletion and d_t=2^t times the discrete metric. With the same weights every distinct pair of histories has distance 1 . The inverse limit has a compact product topology and a noncompact discrete metric topology. Flipping a bit at successively later levels gives product convergence to the unflipped history while all the weighted distances remain 1 .

theorems.label: thm:rigidity
theorems.title: Conditional Stability of Inverse-Limit Identity
theorems.statement: [Conditional Stability of Inverse-Limit Identity] Under RIG-1 through RIG-5 the two limits I= Id and widetilde I= widetilde Id are nonempty. Every history in either limit has a compatible history in the other within distance C E_w . Thus d_H(I, widetilde I) leq C E_w .

theorems.title: Conditional Isomorphism Requires Extra Structure
theorems.statement: [Conditional Isomorphism Requires Extra Structure] The Hausdorff bound alone is a statement about the distance between sets. A homeomorphism follows under the commuting-bijection hypotheses below.

theorems.label: prop:coherent-history-transport
theorems.title: Transport by Commuting Coordinate Bijections
theorems.statement: [Transport by Commuting Coordinate Bijections] Suppose the weighted metric induces the product topology and homeomorphisms h_t:S_t to S_t satisfy widetilde pi _t h_ t+1 =h_t pi _t . Then H(x)_t=h_t(x_t) maps the limits homeomorphically, with inverse H^ -1 (y)_t=h_t^ -1 (y_t) . Its displacement in the common history space is at most sup _t w_t sup _ z in S_t d_t(z,h_t(z)) .

theorems.label: ex:coherent-rotation-tower
theorems.title: A Ramified Tower with Positive Deformation and Coherent Transport
theorems.statement: [A Ramified Tower with Positive Deformation and Coherent Transport] Take S_t=( mathbb R/ mathbb Z) times 0,1 ^ t with the maximum of the circle distance (circumference one) and the discrete prefix distance. Let pi _t keep the angle and delete the last bit, and take w_t=2^ -t . For an intervention at stage k with amplitude 0<a<1/2 , replace pi _k by prefix deletion and angle shift -a . Set h_t to the identity for t leq k and to angle shift a for t>k . The inverses shift by -a on those same levels. The squares commute at k by cancellation and at every other level by commutation with prefix deletion. Each limit has at least two histories over every finite cut, since a later bit may be flipped. All bonding maps are 1 -Lipschitz and satisfy the fiber estimate with K_t=1 : set the required angle

theorems.label: ex:hausdorff-not-isomorphism
theorems.title: Hausdorff Stability Without a Homeomorphism
theorems.statement: [Hausdorff Stability Without a Homeomorphism] Take S_t= 0, ldots ,2^t-1 with discrete distance scaled by r>0 , w_t=2^ -t , and pi _t(j)= lfloor j/2 rfloor . For t geq 1 , change only the image of j=1 to 1 , keeping widetilde pi _0= pi _0 . Both maps remain surjective and satisfy the fiber estimate with K_t=1 . The weighted intervention cost is r sum _ t geq 1 2^ -t =r . The all-zero history of the perturbed tower is isolated by the cylinder y_1=0 because each subsequent zero has exactly one lift. The original tower is the binary-prefix space and has no isolated histories. Thus the limits are not homeomorphic, even though the Hausdorff bound tends to zero with r . The perturbation hypotheses for the Hausdorff estimate all hold.

theorems.label: def:ontmass
theorems.title: Sectorial Deformation Resistance
theorems.statement: [Sectorial Deformation Resistance] Let E_w( delta ) denote the weighted energy of an admissible perturbation family delta . Define [ MO := inf left frac E_w( delta ) d_H( Id , widetilde Id _ delta ) ; middle | ; delta text admissible , d_H( Id , widetilde Id _ delta )>0 right , ] with the convention MO =+ infty if no admissible finite-energy perturbation yields positive deformation of the identity object.

theorems.title: Interpretation discipline
theorems.statement: [Interpretation discipline] MO is a deformation-resistance scalar, not a metaphysical substance. BaseCore uses it only as a conditional invariant attached to admissible perturbation models.

theorems.label: ass:ns1
theorems.title: NS-1: Target and Observable Family
theorems.statement: [NS-1: Target and Observable Family] Fix a nonempty set of compatible histories X subseteq Id , a family of queries J , and responses F_j:X to (Y_j, rho _j) . The query can specify an observable, a time horizon, or a declared intervention. All queries refer to the same encoded history. The intervention protocol and parameters are known to both parties and fixed independently of the history, except for information explicitly included in the encoded state. Non-finite determination and deformation resistance are separate properties of a target, measured using their own definitions.

theorems.label: ass:ns2
theorems.title: NS-2: Binary Representation Budget
theorems.statement: [NS-2: Binary Representation Budget] A deterministic encoder c:X to 0,1 ^B has at most 2^B possible representations. The budget includes all history-dependent information accessible to the decoder. An adaptive binary transcript of depth at most B satisfies the same bound when its query tree is fixed in advance and the choices and termination are determined by its previous bits. An exact real parameter is outside this finite-alphabet class.

theorems.label: ass:ns3
theorems.title: NS-3: Uniform Response Fidelity
theorems.statement: [NS-3: Uniform Response Fidelity] The decoders g_j: 0,1 ^B to Y_j must satisfy rho _j(g_j(c(x)),F_j(x)) leq eta for every x in X and j in J . The tolerance is in the declared response units, after normalizing them if necessary. Faithfulness of additional structures, such as the bonding maps or the intervention cost sector, imposes separate constraints.

theorems.label: thm:non-simulability
theorems.title: Finite-Budget Obstruction by Response Separation
theorems.statement: [Finite-Budget Obstruction by Response Separation] Under NS-1--NS-3, let A subseteq X be a finite set such that for each distinct x,y in A there is j with rho _j(F_j(x),F_j(y))>2 eta . Then |A| leq 2^B . For exact fidelity, a code exists exactly when the number of equivalence classes of x sim y defined by F_j(x)=F_j(y) for all j is at most 2^B .

theorems.label: thm:finite-budget-approximation
theorems.title: Approximation Barrier
theorems.statement: [Approximation Barrier] On the binary prefix tower S_t= 0,1 ^ t with weights w_t=2^ -t and discrete stage metrics, use Y=X= 0,1 ^ mathbb N as the decoded history space, with d_w(x,y)=2^ -m at the first differing bit m geq 1 . Among all encoders with at most 2^B states and decoders into X , the minimum worst-case d_w error is 2^ -(B+1) . Exact recovery of all finite prefix responses requires unbounded B as the query horizon increases.

theorems.label: ex:unbounded-precision-control
theorems.title: One Exact Real Encodes Every Binary History
theorems.statement: [One Exact Real Encodes Every Binary History] The map b mapsto sum _ j geq 1 2b_j3^ -j is injective: at the first unequal bit j the leading difference is 2 cdot 3^ -j and the remaining tail is bounded by 3^ -j . On the image, inverse decoding followed by each prefix projection recovers all the canonical observations from one exact real. As a separate intervention control, any declared family that leaves the target limit set fixed has MO =+ infty by the defining convention, even if the allowed interventions have finite cost. Neither fact supplies a finite binary budget.

theorems.title: What has been removed
theorems.statement: [What has been removed] The resource obstruction concerns the declared responses, metric tolerance and binary budget. Infinite-precision scalar encodings and finite-cost interventions require independent hypotheses before a binary-budget theorem can be applied to them. In the CCR program, non-finite determination and infinite resistance are separately specified; any stronger obstruction to faithful embeddings must state its category and preserved observations. Exact response classes determine whether a finite sufficient statistic exists for the declared queries.

theorems.label: prop:base-wedge-metric-sector
theorems.title: Metric-Sector Stability of the Hilbert Wedge
theorems.statement: [Metric-Sector Stability of the Hilbert Wedge] For Q= 0 le z_j le 2^ -j subset ell ^2 let W=(Q times 0 ) cup ( 0 times Q) and R=1/ sqrt 3 . Cartesian products in these fixed axes, with both factor diameters at least d_0>0 , have Hausdorff distance at least max d_0/2,R/2 from W. More generally, for maximum-metric products of compact factors with these diameter bounds and embeddings with uniform constants 0<c le C , [ d_H(W,F(A times B)) ge delta _W:= frac c^2 min d_0/2,1/(4C) 2C+4c >0. ] Every nonempty compact support at distance less than delta _W/2 from W therefore retains a gap greater than delta _W/2 against this same sector.

theorems.label: def:phenspace
theorems.title: Structural Readout Space
theorems.statement: [Structural Readout Space] A structural readout space is a nonempty set mathcal E , with historical alias ``phenomenological configurations'' for its elements. The set-level definition supplies no topology. All limit and distance statements below use the complete metric class declared immediately next, with its induced Hausdorff topology. Separability, and hence a Polish conclusion, must be supplied or proved where used; completeness alone does not imply it.

theorems.label: hyp:H3-metric
theorems.title: H3: Metric on $\mathcal{E}$
theorems.statement: [H3: Metric on mathcal E ] The structural readout space mathcal E admits a metric d_ mathcal E such that ( mathcal E , d_ mathcal E ) is a complete metric space. Limits and continuity use the topology induced by this metric.

We do not claim that mathcal E represents ``conscious states'' or ``qualia''. It is an abstract mathematical space whose interpretation is not specified by the formalism. The space mathcal E is introduced purely as the codomain of a structural assignment; its ontological status is deliberately left open.

theorems.title: Endomorphisms Preserving All Canonical Projections
theorems.statement: [Endomorphisms Preserving All Canonical Projections] If F: mathcal I to mathcal I satisfies p_t circ F=p_t for every t , then F= operatorname Id . This does not exclude endomorphisms with nonidentity coordinate actions.

theorems.label: def:phenassign
theorems.title: Structural Assignment
theorems.statement: [Structural Assignment] A structural assignment is a family of total maps on the declared observable state spaces: phi _t: S_t to mathcal E indexed by t in mathbb N .

theorems.label: def:limitassign
theorems.title: Induced Limit Assignment
theorems.statement: [Induced Limit Assignment] Given a structural assignment phi _t , the induced limit assignment, whenever it exists, is the map: Phi : mathcal I to mathcal E , quad Phi ((x_t)_t) := lim _ t to infty phi _t(x_t), The convergence statements below use the complete metric codomain of Hypothesis~ ref hyp:H3-metric . Partial readouts may instead be studied on a specified common domain, with all projections and factorizations restricted to that domain.

theorems.label: ax:e0
theorems.title: E0: Non-Triviality
theorems.statement: [E0: Non-Triviality] The structural readout space satisfies | mathcal E | geq 2 , i.e., there exist at least two distinct phenomenological configurations.

theorems.label: ax:e1
theorems.title: E1: Controlled Asymptotic Compatibility
theorems.statement: [E1: Controlled Asymptotic Compatibility] In the complete metric codomain of Hypothesis~ ref hyp:H3-metric , there are numbers a_t geq 0 , independent of the trajectory, with sum _ t=0 ^ infty a_t< infty , such that [ d_ mathcal E bigl ( phi _ t+1 (p_ t+1 x), phi _t(p_tx) bigr ) leq a_t qquad (x in mathcal I, t geq 0). ] Here p_t: mathcal I to S_t is the canonical projection. Define the tail budget A_n= sum _ t=n ^ infty a_t . Exact equality is the special case a_t=0 , not a requirement of E1.

theorems.label: prop:unique-phi
theorems.title: Uniqueness and Uniform Error of the Limit Assignment
theorems.statement: [Uniqueness and Uniform Error of the Limit Assignment] Under Axiom~ ref ax:e1 in the declared complete metric codomain, each trajectory has a unique limit assignment and [ d_ mathcal E bigl ( Phi (x), phi _n(p_nx) bigr ) leq A_n quad text for all x in mathcal I. ]

theorems.label: ax:e2
theorems.title: E2: Non-Locality
theorems.statement: [E2: Non-Locality] There exists no function f: S_t to mathcal E (for any fixed t ) such that for all trajectories (x_t)_t in mathcal I : Phi ((x_t)_t) = f(x_t).

theorems.label: thm:e0-necessary
theorems.title: E0 is Necessary
theorems.statement: [E0 is Necessary] If | mathcal E | = 1 , then every structural assignment is constant and no phenomenological classification is possible.

theorems.label: thm:e1-necessary
theorems.title: Controlled Compatibility Is Sufficient
theorems.statement: [Controlled Compatibility Is Sufficient] E1 guarantees existence of the limit with the error bound in Proposition~ ref prop:unique-phi . Absolute summability is sufficient, not necessary for an arbitrary convergent family.

theorems.label: thm:e2-necessary
theorems.title: Non-Factorization Is an Independent Requirement
theorems.statement: [Non-Factorization Is an Independent Requirement] E2 excludes readouts determined by a single canonical finite cut. The inverse-limit construction and E1 alone do not imply E2.

theorems.label: thm:minimality
theorems.title: Logical Dependencies of the Assignment Conditions
theorems.statement: [Logical Dependencies of the Assignment Conditions] On a nonempty trajectory domain, E2 implies E0. E1 does not imply E2. There exist assignments satisfying E0, the revised E1 and E2 simultaneously. Consequently these three conditions are not an independent minimal axiom basis as originally stated.

theorems.label: prop:exact-e1-obstruction
theorems.title: Exact Compatibility Forces Finite-Cut Factorization
theorems.statement: [Exact Compatibility Forces Finite-Cut Factorization] On a nonempty trajectory domain, if phi _ t+1 (p_ t+1 x)= phi _t(p_tx) for every x,t , then the limit assignment satisfies Phi = phi _0 circ p_0 . It cannot satisfy E2. The controlled E1 above replaces that exact equality, rather than assuming it together with E2.

theorems.label: thm:ternary-regime-realization
theorems.title: Ternary Realization of E0--E2
theorems.statement: [Ternary Realization of E0--E2] Let S_t= 0,1 ^ t+1 with bonding maps that delete the last bit. Identify its inverse limit with mathcal I= 0,1 ^ mathbb N and let mathcal E=[0,1] . Define [ phi _t(b_0, ldots ,b_t)= sum _ j=0 ^t frac 2b_j 3^ j+1 , qquad Phi (b)= sum _ j=0 ^ infty frac 2b_j 3^ j+1 . ] These assignments satisfy E0, controlled E1, and E2, with [ a_t= frac 2 3^ t+2 , qquad A_t= frac 1 3^ t+1 , qquad sup _b| Phi (b)- phi _t(p_tb)|=A_t. ] For distinct histories first differing at position m , put d_ mathcal I (b,c)=3^ -(m+1) , and put d_ mathcal I (b,b)=0 . Then [ d_ mathcal I (b,c) leq | Phi (b)- Phi (c)| leq 3d_ mathcal I (b,c). ] The domain is compact and complete, and the readout is injective and bi-Lipschitz onto its image. Thus a global lower bound is realized here rather tha

theorems.label: thm:finite-cut-minimax
theorems.title: Sharp Finite-Cut Approximation Error
theorems.statement: [Sharp Finite-Cut Approximation Error] For the ternary realization and an arbitrary decoder g:S_t to mathbb R , let [ R_t(g)= sup _ b in mathcal I | Phi (b)-g(p_tb)|. ] Then the exact minimax value is [ inf _g R_t(g)= frac 1 2 ,3^ t+1 . ] It is attained by g_ ast (s)= phi _t(s)+1/(2 ,3^ t+1 ) .

theorems.label: prop:ternary-arbitrary-code
theorems.title: Sharp Error for Arbitrary Binary Codes
theorems.statement: [Sharp Error for Arbitrary Binary Codes] For the ternary assignment above, let an encoder choose at most 2^B states as an arbitrary function of the whole history, and let each state decode to any real number. The minimum worst-case absolute error is 1/(2 cdot 3^B) for every integer B geq 0 .

theorems.label: thm:joint-transport-readout
theorems.title: Joint Realization of Transport and Controlled Readouts
theorems.statement: [Joint Realization of Transport and Controlled Readouts] Use circle-prefix stages S_t= mathbb T times 0,1 ^t , stage metric max ( rho , mathbf 1 _ text different prefix ) , and weights w_t=3^ -t , where rho is circle distance with circumference one. Take the usual truncation tower I_0 and its variant I_1 with angle shift -a at the single bonding level k , for 0<a<1/2 . Write beta =3^ -(k+1) . In the common weighted history space put Z=I_0 cup I_1 . Let the complete codomain be mathcal E= mathbb T^2 times with the maximum of the first circle distance, beta times the second circle distance, and the absolute scalar difference. Define [ F(x)= left ( theta _0(x), theta _ k+1 (x), sum _ j geq 1 2b_j(x)3^ -j right ). ] Then d_w(x,y) leq d_ mathcal E (F(x),F(y)) leq 3d_w(x,y) on all of Z . On each

theorems.label: prop:readout-continuity-control
theorems.title: Setwise Invariance Does Not Supply Continuity
theorems.statement: [Setwise Invariance Does Not Supply Continuity] Controlled E1 and E2 can hold for a discontinuous assignment, even if the identity domain is fixed under every declared intervention.

theorems.label: prop:transport-control
theorems.title: Setwise and Pointwise Transport Are Distinct
theorems.statement: [Setwise and Pointwise Transport Are Distinct] Preserving an identity domain as a set does not guarantee equal values of a common readout on transported states.

theorems.label: def:compat-class
theorems.title: Phenomenological Compatibility Class
theorems.statement: [Phenomenological Compatibility Class] For a declared identity domain and codomain, mathcal P(M_ Omega ) consists of maps Phi : mathcal I to mathcal E that are limits of some family phi _t satisfying E1, with E0 and E2 also satisfied. The readout family and its tail control are part of the realization data. The notation retains the mass index for comparisons, but no mass-dependent restriction follows from E0--E2 alone.
The compatibility class records choices of domain, codomain and readout family. A numerical mass label does not by itself determine those choices or their transport under perturbations.

theorems.label: thm:h3-necessary
theorems.title: Metric Data Required by Quantitative Formulas
theorems.statement: [Metric Data Required by Quantitative Formulas] The distance-based fragmentation and loss functionals used here require a declared metric, or a pseudometric with a stated quotient convention. Topological continuity can be defined without a metric. Completeness is used for the Cauchy-limit guarantee of E1.

theorems.label: prop:complete-necessary
theorems.title: Completeness and Existence of Limits
theorems.statement: [Completeness and Existence of Limits] Without completeness, the conclusion that every E1-type Cauchy family has its limit in the declared codomain can fail. Completeness is not necessary for a family whose limit is already known to belong to that codomain.

theorems.label: def:phen-continuity
theorems.title: Phenomenological Continuity
theorems.statement: [Phenomenological Continuity] A structural assignment Phi : mathcal I to mathcal E is textit structurally continuous if for every sequence (x^ (n) )_n in mathcal I converging in the d_w metric: d_w(x^ (n) , x) to 0 implies d_ mathcal E ( Phi (x^ (n) ), Phi (x)) to 0.
Structural continuity is derived under the finite-readout conditions of Theorem~ ref thm:forced-continuity . It is distinct from invariance under an external intervention.

theorems.label: def:fragmentation
theorems.title: Phenomenological Fragmentation
theorems.statement: [Phenomenological Fragmentation] A structural assignment Phi is textit fragmentable if there exists a perturbation epsilon _t with finite weighted energy such that: d_ mathcal E ( Phi (x), tilde Phi ( tilde x )) > 0 for corresponding identity trajectories x in mathcal I and tilde x in tilde mathcal I .
Fragmentation captures the vulnerability of phenomenological structure to perturbations. It is the phenomenological analog of identity deformability.

theorems.label: prop:metric-compat
theorems.title: Continuity from Controlled Finite Readouts
theorems.statement: [Continuity from Controlled Finite Readouts] Write g_n= phi _n circ p_n . Under E1, [ d_ mathcal E ( Phi (x), Phi (y)) leq 2A_n+d_ mathcal E (g_n(x),g_n(y)). ] Continuous g_n give a continuous Phi ; a common L -Lipschitz bound gives the same bound for Phi . On a compact metric history domain, put [ omega _n(r)= sup _ d_w(x,y) leq r d_ mathcal E (g_n(x),g_n(y)), qquad omega (r)= inf _n 2A_n+ omega _n(r) . ] If the g_n are continuous, omega is a finite nondecreasing modulus tending to zero at zero and bounds the limiting readout uniformly. No common Lipschitz constant for the finite readouts is required for this conclusion.

theorems.label: hyp:phi-regularity
theorems.title: $\Phi$-Regularity Lower Bound
theorems.statement: [ Phi -Regularity Lower Bound] Let ( mathcal I , d_w) be the identitary metric space from textit Rigid Identity and let ( mathcal E , d_ mathcal E ) be the abstract phenomenological metric space. A structural assignment Phi : mathcal I to mathcal E is said to satisfy Phi -regularity when it satisfies: [leftmargin=*] item (Properness) For every compact K subset mathcal E , Phi ^ -1 (K) is compact in mathcal I . item (Local Lipschitz regularity) For every x in mathcal I , there exist varepsilon > 0 and L_x > 0 such that for all y, z in B_ varepsilon (x) : d_ mathcal E ( Phi (y), Phi (z)) leq L_x cdot d_w(y, z). item (Non-collapse) For every x in mathcal I and every r > 0 , the restriction of Phi to B_r(x) is not constant. item (Global lower Lipschitz bound) There exists a constant C>0 such t

theorems.title: Status of $\Phi$-regularity
theorems.statement: [Status of Phi -regularity] The fourth clause is an additional structural assumption, not a consequence of the first three clauses. The counterexample in Appendix~ ref app:phi-regularity-counterexample shows that properness, local Lipschitz regularity, and non-collapse do not imply any uniform lower Lipschitz constant.

theorems.label: hyp:audited-comparison
theorems.title: Audited Perturbation Comparisons
theorems.statement: [Audited Perturbation Comparisons] Declare a finite-cost intervention class mathcal V , a common metric space (Z,d_Z) containing the unperturbed and perturbed identity domains, and transports h_ varepsilon : mathcal I to mathcal I_ varepsilon subseteq Z . Readouts are restrictions of one declared map F:Z to mathcal E : Phi =F|_ mathcal I and Phi _ varepsilon =F|_ mathcal I_ varepsilon . The following branches are alternatives, used separately. The positive-displacement branch has some varepsilon in mathcal V and x in mathcal I with d_Z(x,h_ varepsilon x)>0 . The zero-displacement branch has h_ varepsilon x=x for every varepsilon in mathcal V and x in mathcal I . Any use of the lower Lipschitz bound in a comparison requires that bound for F on the common comparison domain, not merely within

theorems.title: Burden linking rigidity and readout comparisons
theorems.statement: [Burden linking rigidity and readout comparisons] The scalar M_ Omega does not itself supply the transports or a common readout. Relating its finite and infinite regimes to these two branches is a separate model obligation. Setwise invariance does not imply pointwise fixed transport, and a lower bound within one domain does not compare unrelated assignments on different domains.

theorems.label: thm:fragmentation
theorems.title: Fragmentation under an Audited Displacement
theorems.statement: [Fragmentation under an Audited Displacement] Let an assignment satisfy E0--E2. Assume the positive-displacement branch of Hypothesis~ ref hyp:audited-comparison and a lower Lipschitz constant C>0 for F on its common comparison domain. Then, for the witnessing pair, [ d_ mathcal E ( Phi (x), Phi _ varepsilon (h_ varepsilon x)) geq C d_Z(x,h_ varepsilon x)>0. ] Thus the assignment is fragmentable. This applies to a finite- M_ Omega model when that model supplies the stated comparison data.

theorems.title: Fragmentability and Continuity Are Distinct
theorems.statement: [Fragmentability and Continuity Are Distinct] The positive-displacement conclusion does not establish a topological discontinuity. A continuous assignment may be fragmentable under a state-changing intervention.

theorems.label: thm:forced-continuity
theorems.title: Continuity and Conditional Perturbation Invariance
theorems.statement: [Continuity and Conditional Perturbation Invariance] Under E1, if each finite readout g_n= phi _n circ p_n is continuous, then Phi is continuous, irrespective of M_ Omega . Under the zero-displacement branch of Hypothesis~ ref hyp:audited-comparison , [ Phi _ varepsilon (h_ varepsilon x)= Phi (x) qquad ( varepsilon in mathcal V, x in mathcal I). ] For a CCR model the invariance conclusion therefore holds when its finite-cost interventions admit that branch. CCR alone is not a proof of continuity or of readout naturality.

theorems.title: Invariance on the Audited Zero-Displacement Branch
theorems.statement: [Invariance on the Audited Zero-Displacement Branch] A CCR model satisfying the zero-displacement comparison hypothesis has invariant assignment values under all interventions in its declared finite-cost class.

theorems.label: thm:dichotomy
theorems.title: Conditional Classification by Audited Branches
theorems.statement: [Conditional Classification by Audited Branches] Suppose a model supplies the positive-displacement branch and lower bound whenever M_ Omega < infty , and supplies continuous finite readouts and the zero-displacement branch whenever M_ Omega =+ infty . Then its finite regime is fragmentable and its infinite regime has a continuous, perturbation-invariant assignment. The mass cases are exclusive; fragmentability and topological continuity need not be exclusive properties.

theorems.title: The Mass Label Does Not Define Assignment Existence
theorems.statement: [The Mass Label Does Not Define Assignment Existence] For fixed identity domain, codomain and readout family, the class defined by E0--E2 is independent of a numerical label M_ Omega . A claim that M_ Omega =0 excludes assignments needs an additional link to the domain or admissible readouts.

theorems.title: Deformable Branch with Comparison Data
theorems.statement: [Deformable Branch with Comparison Data] For 0<M_ Omega < infty , the positive-displacement and lower-bound hypotheses of Theorem~ ref thm:fragmentation imply fragmentability.

theorems.title: Rigid Branch with Comparison Data
theorems.statement: [Rigid Branch with Comparison Data] For M_ Omega =+ infty , continuous finite readouts under E1 imply continuity, and the zero-displacement branch implies perturbation invariance. These are the respective hypotheses of Theorem~ ref thm:forced-continuity .

theorems.title: Inheritance under Audited Fixed Transport
theorems.statement: [Inheritance under Audited Fixed Transport] An assignment satisfying the zero-displacement comparison branch inherits invariance under that declared intervention class. This applies to CCR realizations only after checking that branch.

theorems.label: thm:readout-loss-stability
theorems.title: Quantitative Stability of Audited Readout Loss
