If a lower bound d_ mathcal E (Fx,F(h_ theta x)) geq C d_Z(x,h_ theta x) holds on these compared pairs, then [ C Delta leq R(F,h) leq omega _F( Delta ). ] For another readout G:Z to math

theorems.label: def:compatibility-operator
theorems.title: Compatibility Operator
theorems.statement: [Compatibility Operator] Declare a complete metric comparison domain (Z,d_Z) , a complete metric poset ( E , preceq , dE ) with bottom nullphi , and maps Phi _S:D_S to E . The audited readout Phi :Z to E is defined on its declared pair class W subseteq Z times Z . Extension and isomorphism transports j:D_S to D_ S' satisfy Phi _ S' circ j= Phi _S when claimed. On W , a certified C>0 satisfies [ dE ( Phi (x), Phi (y)) geq C d_Z(x,y). ] One may choose Z= I for history comparisons. Comparing whole identity objects requires a separate declared embedding/metric; Phi ( I ) is not a point value when the domain is the set I . A separated extension witness supplies two distinct defined points in a common comparison domain, not merely a relabeled copy under exact transport. CCR does not supply such

theorems.label: def:phenomenological-attractor
theorems.title: Phenomenological Attractor Set
theorems.statement: [Phenomenological Attractor Set] Use Attr (S) for structurally stable readout values under a declared perturbation/extension family, as defined below. Temporal attraction would additionally require a dynamics and a basin; neither is implied by this notation.

theorems.label: def:phenomenological-stability
theorems.title: Phenomenological Stability
theorems.statement: [Phenomenological Stability] A value e= Phi _S(z) is structurally stable if a finite modulus omega ( rho ) to 0 as rho downarrow 0 controls dE ( Phi _ S' (Pz),e) leq omega ( rho ) for all declared perturbation transports P of cost at most rho . Exact persistence instead requires equality. Stability does not force equality at a nonzero perturbation budget.

theorems.label: lem:null-bridge
theorems.title: Bridge Lemma
theorems.statement: [Bridge Lemma] For any defined e in E , distance dE (e, nullphi )=0 implies e= nullphi . No CCR assumption is needed.

theorems.label: thm:phenomenological-instability
theorems.title: Conditional Null Separation
theorems.statement: [Conditional Null Separation] Suppose (z_0,z_1) in W , d_Z(z_0,z_1)= epsilon >0 , and the lower constant in Definition~ ref def:compatibility-operator is C>0 . Their images cannot both equal null, and [ max _ i=0,1 dE ( Phi (z_i), nullphi ) geq C epsilon /2. ] The historical instability label denotes joint exact null exclusion here, not dynamical instability of an individual null endpoint.

theorems.label: cor:forced-non-nullity
theorems.title: Conditional Forced Non-Nullity
theorems.statement: [Conditional Forced Non-Nullity] Under the separated-pair hypotheses, at least one witness image is non-null. If one endpoint is fixed at null, the other has null distance at least C epsilon . CCR alone does not select a non-null endpoint or guarantee a stable regime.

theorems.label: ex:joint-external-null-witness
theorems.title: External Null Witness in a Common Readout Domain
theorems.statement: [External Null Witness in a Common Readout Domain] Fix k geq 0 and 0<a<1/2 . Use the weighted circle-prefix history metric with weights 3^ -t , the undeformed tower I_0 , the single-jump tower I_1 (bonding shift -a at level k ), and Z=I_0 cup I_1 . Set beta =3^ -(k+1) . The common readout F takes the initial angle, the angle at k+1 , and the ternary code of the bits, with codomain metric max ( rho _0, beta rho _1,| Delta text code |) . The two angular blocks give the first two terms of d_w , while the ternary leading term minus its tail bounds the binary part from below. Thus C=1 holds on the entire compact union. Order the codomain by equality together with e_0=(0,0,0) below every element. Declare internal interventions to be simultaneous rotations of all stages of I_0 , with cost the abs

theorems.label: def:positive-regime-space
theorems.title: Positive Regime Space
theorems.statement: [Positive Regime Space] Let Eplus = E setminus nullphi with inherited order. For a witness pair, let A= Phi (z_0), Phi (z_1) setminus nullphi and A_0=A cup nullphi .

theorems.label: thm:minimal-positive-regime
theorems.title: Minimal Positive Witness Regime
theorems.statement: [Minimal Positive Witness Regime] The finite positive witness image A is non-empty and has a minimal element. If its two possible values are comparable, it has a unique least element. No ambient order completeness is needed. This does not prove a least member of all of Eplus .

theorems.label: def:structural-intensity
theorems.title: Structural Intensity
theorems.statement: [Structural Intensity] Distinguish null distance r(e)= dE (e, nullphi ) , global lower gap iota (e)= inf _ f in E , f prec e dE (e,f) , and the audited relative gap iota _ A_0 (e) obtained by restricting this infimum to f in A_0 . All are measured in units of dE . A positive null distance does not imply a positive global gap.

theorems.label: thm:universal-intensity-bound
theorems.title: Anchored Witness Intensity Bound
theorems.statement: [Anchored Witness Intensity Bound] If one endpoint is null, the other image e is the unique positive member of A and satisfies iota _ A_0 (e)=r(e) geq C epsilon >0 . Without that anchor, only max _i r( Phi (z_i)) geq C epsilon /2 follows. No universal global intensity bound is claimed.

theorems.label: thm:forced-phenomenological-closure
theorems.title: Conditional Phenomenological Closure
theorems.statement: [Conditional Phenomenological Closure] A declared detected pair gives joint null exclusion and a minimal positive member of its finite image. A null anchor gives a unique positive witness value and the anchored quantitative bound. Uniqueness in the ambient regime space, temporal stability and CCR realizability require further hypotheses and constructions.

theorems.label: prop:profinite-bound
theorems.title: Profinite Bound
theorems.statement: [Profinite Bound] A profinite witness pair with declared positive separation epsilon , certified lower constant C_ mathrm prof >0 and one null endpoint gives r(e) geq C_ mathrm prof epsilon . Summable coordinate costs do not by themselves certify CCR.

theorems.label: prop:symbolic-bound
theorems.title: Symbolic Bound
theorems.statement: [Symbolic Bound] The same anchored conclusion holds for a symbolic witness with its audited metric and lower constant. The full binary shift with complement intervention and summable coordinate-change costs is a control against automatic infinite mass.

theorems.label: thm:rigidity-inheritance
theorems.title: Rigidity Inheritance
theorems.statement: [Rigidity Inheritance] Let a:Z' to Z , Phi :Z to mathcal E and b: mathcal E to mathcal E' be maps between declared metric domains, and set Phi '=b circ Phi circ a . On a specified pair class W' , assume positive lower constants c_a,C,c_b for a , Phi on the mapped pairs and b on the resulting image pairs. Then Phi ' has lower constant c_ac_bC on W' . Independently, suppose every admitted new finite-cost positive deformation pulls back to an admitted old finite-cost positive deformation. Infinite resistance of the old sector then implies infinite resistance of the new one. Transport of a null anchor additionally requires b( nullphi )= nullphi ' .

theorems.label: thm:null-categorical-universality
theorems.title: Factorization on a Faithful Image
theorems.statement: [Factorization on a Faithful Image] Let Phi :Z to mathcal E have a global lower metric bound C>0 . For every map Psi :Z to F there is a unique u: Phi (Z) to F satisfying u circ Phi = Psi , with Phi regarded as a map onto its image. If F is metric and Psi is L -Lipschitz, u is L/C -Lipschitz for the subspace metric. No extension or uniqueness outside Phi (Z) is implied.

theorems.label: thm:null-simulation-lower-bound
theorems.title: Finite-Prefix Simulation Bound
theorems.statement: [Finite-Prefix Simulation Bound] Let F(b)= sum _ j geq 0 2b_j/3^ j+1 on the full binary-history space. For a decoder g observing exactly bits 0, ldots ,N , N geq 0 , the sharp minimax scalar error is [ inf _g sup _b|F(b)-g(b_0, ldots ,b_N)|= frac 1 2 ,3^ N+1 . ] This positive fixed-prefix bound tends to zero with increasing budget and does not concern finite real dimension without a precision constraint.

theorems.label: thm:null-closure-by-non-alternatives
theorems.title: Conditional Closure by Non-Alternatives
theorems.statement: [Conditional Closure by Non-Alternatives] Every model with a defined pair of distance epsilon >0 and readout lower constant C>0 obeys joint null exclusion, has a nonempty finite positive witness image with a minimal element, and satisfies max _i dE ( Phi (z_i), nullphi ) geq C epsilon /2 . A null anchor gives a unique positive witness value with relative gap at least C epsilon . Additional models satisfy these same conclusions only after supplying the same typed hypotheses; transport uses the preceding lower-bound and sector-pullback conditions. This is a conditional closure, not an existence or physical-admissibility theorem for arbitrary alternative models.

theorems.title: BaseCore Envelope
theorems.statement: [BaseCore Envelope] The BaseCore envelope is the collection of theorem-level structures established directly within this foundational layer: [leftmargin=*] item foundational Hilbert-space projection dynamics; item typed computable witnesses and state spectral-gap bounds; item parameterwise non-collapse under explicit anti-constant assumptions; item inverse-limit identity under non-finite-determination assumptions; item conditional rigidity under admissible perturbation models; item conditional obstruction to uniform response fidelity under a binary representation budget; item operational-criterion grammar, certification, falsation, and claim-boundary ledgers.

theorems.title: Boundary Discipline
theorems.statement: [Boundary Discipline] BaseCore may define structures that downstream layers use, but it does not claim downstream closure. In particular, BaseCore does not by itself own runtime thresholds, bridge admissibility, human-comparator programs, phenomenality burdens, or Papers 7--9.

theorems.title: Separation of BaseCore from downstream extensions
theorems.statement: [Separation of BaseCore from downstream extensions] Runtime parameterization, non-convex extension classes, and cross-mode bridge vocabulary are kept outside BaseCore so that the mathematical base layer retains exact theorem-level hypotheses without dependence on empirical conventions.

theorems.title: BaseCore export object
theorems.statement: [BaseCore export object] A BaseCore export object is a tuple [ mathfrak E =( mathcal O , mathcal H , mathcal R , mathcal B ) ] where mathcal O is a typed mathematical object defined in BaseCore, mathcal H is the finite list of hypotheses under which it is used, mathcal R is the list of results actually proved from those hypotheses, and mathcal B is a boundary list of claims not entailed by mathcal R .

theorems.title: Downstream admissible extension
theorems.statement: [Downstream admissible extension] A downstream layer is an admissible extension of a BaseCore export object mathfrak E only if it supplies: [leftmargin=*] item an explicit target predicate P not already contained in mathcal R ; item a typed construction or estimator witnessing the objects on which P is evaluated; item a proof, reduction, or reproducible protocol connecting mathcal H to P ; item negative controls or failure modes under which P must not be asserted; item a provenance statement distinguishing theorem, implementation, internal support, and external adjudication.

theorems.title: No automatic downstream promotion
theorems.statement: [No automatic downstream promotion] Let mathfrak E =( mathcal O , mathcal H , mathcal R , mathcal B ) be a BaseCore export object and let P be a predicate introduced outside BaseCore. If P notin mathcal R , then BaseCore does not entail P unless an admissible extension supplies an additional bridge from mathcal H to P .

theorems.title: Runtime-use admissibility
theorems.statement: [Runtime-use admissibility] A runtime measurement may instantiate a BaseCore export object only as an implementation-level witness when all of the following are recorded: the measured state space, the estimator or update rule, the finite horizon, the calibration regime, the controls under which the measurement fails, and the claim class being asserted. Such a measurement is not a BaseCore theorem and is not external validation by itself.

theorems.title: Open-load placement for $I_{\mathrm{int}}$ and atomic separators
theorems.statement: [Open-load placement for I_ mathrm int and atomic separators] Quantities such as I_ mathrm int and any atomic-separator condition may be treated as downstream target predicates or estimator families only after their carrier objects, separator class, invariance target, and negative controls are specified. Until a proof or reproducible adversarial protocol closes that burden, BaseCore may export the ambient structural language but not the separator conclusion.

theorems.title: Boundary preservation under finite implementations
theorems.statement: [Boundary preservation under finite implementations] Suppose a finite implementation produces diagnostics for a downstream predicate P over a bounded horizon. If the implementation does not prove that the diagnostics are invariant over the relevant mathematical class, then the diagnostics remain implementation evidence for P and do not promote P to a BaseCore result.

theorems.label: thm:basecore-irreducible-observation
theorems.title: Irreducibility Derives Every Linear Response Separator
theorems.statement: [Irreducibility Derives Every Linear Response Separator] Let p be prime, d ge 2 , X= mathbb F_p^d , and let the minimal polynomial of A:X to X be irreducible of degree d . For every nonzero linear functional ell :X to mathbb F_p , the map [ x longmapsto ( ell x, ell Ax, ldots , ell A^ d-1 x) ] is injective. Encode a field symbol a by its integer representative iota (a)=a/(p-1) in . Distinct states have response distance at least 1/(p-1) in maximum norm. Every response-preserving state quotient is injective. Conversely, observability of every nonzero linear functional implies irreducibility of the characteristic polynomial of A .

theorems.label: prop:basecore-irreducible-control
theorems.title: A Coupled Instance and a Faithful Product Control
theorems.statement: [A Coupled Instance and a Faithful Product Control] For p=2,d=2 , A(a,b)=(b,a+b) has minimal polynomial t^2+t+1 , which is irreducible over mathbb F_2 . Each nonzero linear port separates all states in two readings. With the same carrier, two coordinate ports, word horizon and command labels, replacing A by the identity admits the exact independent product of its two binary coordinates.

theorems.label: thm:c1-irreducible-nonfactorization
theorems.title: Common Jacobian Obstruction to a Local Product
theorems.statement: [Common Jacobian Obstruction to a Local Product] Let (F_u)_ u in U be C^1 maps on an open set in mathbb R^d with a common fixed point x^ ast , and put A_u=DF_u(x^ ast ) . Suppose the A_u have no common nonzero proper real invariant subspace. Then there is no single local C^1 product chart H with C^1 inverse at x^ ast that conjugates all F_u to maps G_ 1,u times G_ 2,u on a product of open sets of positive dimensions. For a single planar A_u= rho R( theta ) with rho >0 and sin theta ne 0 , the hypothesis holds.

theorems.label: prop:c1-jacobian-family-controls
theorems.title: Two Contractive Controls in Every Finite Dimension
theorems.statement: [Two Contractive Controls in Every Finite Dimension] For d geq 2 a two-control family of linear contractions on mathbb R^d can satisfy the common-subspace hypothesis, even though each command has a proper invariant subspace. Removing the cyclic command in the following construction admits an exact coordinate product.

theorems.label: def:system
theorems.title: Admissible system
theorems.statement: [Admissible system] An admissible system is a tuple [ S=(X, Phi ,C,R, Gamma ,U) ] where: [leftmargin=1.5em] item X is a metrizable internal state space with metric d_X ; item Phi = Phi _u _ u in U is a family of admissible transition operators Phi _u:X to X ; item C is the effective causal structure used to test admissible factorization and intervention behavior; item R= r_ alpha _ alpha in Lambda _R is a family of readouts, each r_ alpha :X to Y_ alpha ; item Gamma = gamma _j _ j=1 ^m is an admissibility bundle defining [ X_ Gamma = x in X: gamma _j(x) le 0 forall j ; ] item U is the set of admissible interventions.

theorems.label: def:state-attractor
theorems.title: Declared State Attractor
theorems.statement: [Declared State Attractor] Fix a non-empty compact set operatorname Attr _X(S) subseteq X_ Gamma invariant under every admitted transition and a non-empty class of admitted schedules at every horizon. It is a controlled attracting region on a declared non-empty basin B_X if, for every x_0 in B_X , [ sup _ u_ bullet operatorname dist _ d_X bigl (x_n, operatorname Attr _X(S) bigr ) longrightarrow 0, qquad x_ k+1 = Phi _ u_k (x_k). ] The supremum is over admitted schedules. This is a state-space certificate to supply, not an existence theorem. Its codomain is X ; the structurally stable readout set Attr (S) in the null-regime section instead lies in E . No intersection of those different types is taken.

theorems.label: def:support
theorems.title: Admissible support
theorems.statement: [Admissible support] A subset Aset subseteq X_ Gamma is an admissible support if: [leftmargin=1.5em] item Aset is non-empty and compact; item Phi _u( Aset ) subseteq Aset for every u in U ; item Aset cap operatorname Attr _X(S) neq varnothing ; item Aset stays disjoint from the collapse set excluded by the base non-collapse burden.

theorems.label: def:history
theorems.title: Windowed readout history
theorems.statement: [Windowed readout history] Fix a horizon T in Nset and an intervention schedule u_ bullet =(u_0, dots ,u_ T-1 ) . For x in Aset , define [ h_ S,T (x;u_ bullet )= bigl (r_ alpha (x_t) bigr )_ 0 le t le T, alpha in Lambda _R , qquad x_ t+1 = Phi _ u_t (x_t), quad x_0=x. ] The set of all such histories is denoted Hist _ S,T .

theorems.label: def:partition
theorems.title: Operational partition candidate
theorems.statement: [Operational partition candidate] An operational partition candidate is a map [ pi _ S,T : Hist _ S,T to Class _ S,T ] into a finite or countable label set Class _ S,T .

theorems.label: def:margins
theorems.title: Witness margin vector
theorems.statement: [Witness margin vector] Define the witness margin vector [ Delta (S)= bigl ( delta _ mathrm per (S), delta _ mathrm ri (S), delta _ mathrm int (S), delta _ mathrm cont (S), delta _ mathrm diff (S), delta _ mathrm leg (S) bigr ) in [0, infty )^6. ] When the six witnesses are separately calibrated as certified radii in the same perturbation metric and class, their invariant budget is [ delta _ star (S)= min Delta (S). ] A positive radius certifies the associated predicate at the target and throughout its declared perturbation ball. A zero or unreported radius alone does not determine failure at the target. Raw separations, risks, durations, fragmentation ceilings and compression errors require separate calibration before taking this minimum.

theorems.label: def:iper
theorems.title: Structural persistence
theorems.statement: [Structural persistence] An admissible system satisfies structural persistence, written Iper (S)=1 , if there exists an admissible support Aset and a constant delta _ mathrm per (S)>0 such that: [leftmargin=1.5em] item Aset is forward invariant under all u in U ; item every admissible trajectory starting in Aset remains at least delta _ mathrm per (S) away from the collapse set; item Aset contains or converges into a non-empty admissible attractor region.

theorems.label: def:iri
theorems.title: Rigid identity
theorems.statement: [Rigid identity] An admissible system satisfies rigid identity, written Iri (S)=1 , if the observable family induced by R on Aset determines a unique identity object Id _S and there exists a gap delta _ mathrm ri (S)>0 such that every admissible alternative identity candidate remains at weighted deformation distance at least delta _ mathrm ri (S) from Id _S .

theorems.label: def:iint
theorems.title: Causal integration
theorems.statement: [Causal integration] An admissible system satisfies causal integration, written Iint (S)=1 , if there is no non-trivial factorization [ Aset =A_1 times A_2, qquad R=R_1 sqcup R_2, ] together with decomposed dynamics and causal structure reproducing admissible histories within error smaller than a positive margin delta _ mathrm int (S) while preserving Id _S . More explicitly, this shorthand is relative to a declared admissible factorization class. For such a class mathfrak D , write Iint (S; mathfrak D )=1 when no factorization in mathfrak D reproduces the admissible histories below a positive margin delta _ mathrm int (S; mathfrak D ) while preserving Id _S . The unqualified notation Iint (S)=1 refers to the default structural class mathfrak D _ ast : fixed, time-homogeneous, schedule-ind

theorems.title: Class-relative integration margin
theorems.statement: [Class-relative integration margin] The integration criterion is class-relative. Adopting mathfrak D _ ast does not assert that S resists every broader behavioral simulator. In particular, under decoder-coupled or schedule-dependent behavioral classes such as mathfrak D _ mathrm approx , the corresponding margin delta _ mathrm int (S; mathfrak D _ mathrm approx ) may vanish, i.e. may be equal to 0 ; the current coupled-carrier analysis records precisely this failure mode. Thus the default structural reading preserves a falsation surface and must not be read as an unconditional closure of integration, nor as a strengthening of any downstream theorem that assumes Iint (S)=1 .

theorems.label: lem:two-factor-label-obstruction
theorems.title: Two Factor Fibers Cannot Share a Nonconstant Label
theorems.statement: [Two Factor Fibers Cannot Share a Nonconstant Label] Let chi :A to A_1 times A_2 be surjective. If a label g:A to L is constant on every fiber of each of the two factor projections of chi , then g is constant on A .

theorems.label: def:icont
theorems.title: Regime continuity
theorems.statement: [Regime continuity] An admissible system satisfies regime continuity, written Icont (S)=1 , if there exists a complete metric space ( E ,d_ E ) and an admissible assignment [ Pi _S: Aset to E ] such that: [leftmargin=1.5em] item every admissible trajectory induces a continuous path in E on admissible windows; item there exists delta _ mathrm cont (S)>0 bounding the fragmentation functional on all admissible histories; item no admissible finite-energy perturbation produces a discontinuous jump into an incompatible regime class while Id _S is preserved.

theorems.label: def:idiff
theorems.title: Non-null differentiation
theorems.statement: [Non-null differentiation] An admissible system satisfies non-null differentiation, written Idiff (S)=1 , if there exist x,y in Aset , a horizon T , and a readout subfamily Read ^ star subseteq R such that [ dist bigl (h_ S,T (x;u_ bullet ),h_ S,T (y;u_ bullet ) bigr ) ge delta _ mathrm diff (S)>0 ] for some admissible schedule u_ bullet , and if the null class nullclass is not an asymptotically stable admissible attractor.

theorems.label: def:decoder
theorems.title: Decoder Family and Structural Closure
theorems.statement: [Decoder Family and Structural Closure] A decoder family uses one declared class set and acts on the specified history windows. For each intervention-response comparison, declare its response cells and a matching relation on those cells. The family is structurally closed when decoder class equality composes exactly and the response-cell matching relations are reflexive, symmetric and transitive. These are conditions on the chosen comparison data; they are not inferred from a numerical tolerance alone. The legibility clauses below supply the additional operational requirements.

theorems.label: def:ileg
theorems.title: Operational legibility
theorems.statement: [Operational legibility] An admissible system satisfies operational legibility, written Ileg (S)=1 , if there exist: [leftmargin=1.5em] item a declared readout subfamily Read ^ mathrm leg subseteq R ; item a structurally closed decoder family Dec _S acting on windows of length at least tau _ min (S) ; item a class set Class _S ; item a measurement protocol with separation sigma >0 , readout noise radius r>0 , minimum duration tau _ min ge 1 , miss and false-positive budgets p_ mathrm miss ,p_ mathrm fp in item Distinct declared classes have distance at least sigma in the specified clean comparison domain. item On the specified noise domain, perturbations with readout norm at most r preserve the label. item Under declared sham schedules, labels remain stable throughout every tested window o

theorems.label: prop:invariant-necessity
theorems.title: Each invariant is individually necessary
theorems.statement: [Each invariant is individually necessary] If any one of Iper , allowbreak Iri , allowbreak Iint , allowbreak Icont , allowbreak Idiff , allowbreak Ileg fails, then S notin Critop .

theorems.title: Certified decoder
theorems.statement: [Certified decoder] A decoder D in Dec _S is certified as part of a structurally closed family when the six clauses of Definition~ ref def:ileg hold on the chosen admissible support. Structural closure and operational certification are separate requirements.

theorems.title: Criterion indistinguishability
theorems.statement: [Criterion indistinguishability] For x,y in Aset , write x sim _ Partop ,S y if, for every certified decoder D in Dec _S , every admissible horizon T ge tau _ min (S) , and every admissible intervention schedule u_ bullet , [ D(h_ S,T (x;u_ bullet ))=D(h_ S,T (y;u_ bullet )), ] and the intervention responses remain matched within the legibility margin.

theorems.label: prop:qop-welldefined
theorems.title: Well-definedness of the certified partition
theorems.statement: [Well-definedness of the certified partition] On any declared support Aset with a structurally closed decoder family, the relation sim _ Partop ,S is an equivalence relation. This conclusion does not require the other critical invariants; certification of criterion membership still does.

theorems.label: rem:tolerance-control
theorems.title: Tolerance Alone Is Not Transitive
theorems.statement: [Tolerance Alone Is Not Transitive] With constant decoder labels, let response matching mean distance at most 1 on 0,3/4,3/2 . Adjacent points match, but the endpoints do not. Thus decoder equality plus raw tolerance is not enough. By contrast, equality under a declared response-cell map is an equivalence relation and supplies a concrete structurally closed matching rule. This example concerns closure only, not satisfaction of all six legibility clauses.

theorems.label: def:qop
theorems.title: Certified operational partition
theorems.statement: [Certified operational partition] Assume Proposition~ ref prop:qop-welldefined . The certified operational partition of S is [ Partop (S):= Aset / sim _ Partop ,S . ]

theorems.label: def:cop
theorems.title: Operational-criterion class membership
theorems.statement: [Operational-criterion class membership] An admissible system belongs to the BaseCore operational-criterion class, written S in Critop , if there exists a non-empty admissible support Aset such that [ Iper (S)= Iri (S)= Iint (S)= Icont (S)= Idiff (S)= Ileg (S)=1. ]

theorems.title: Neutrality of the class symbol
theorems.statement: [Neutrality of the class symbol] The symbol Critop is a shorthand for a conjunctive operational criterion. It is not a theorem of phenomenality, metaphysical subjectivity, or human equivalence.

theorems.label: def:rupture
theorems.title: Rupture
theorems.statement: [Rupture] A rupture is any loss of admissibility or loss of at least one critical invariant margin beyond its admissible threshold.

theorems.label: thm:rupture
theorems.title: Rupture by Invariant Loss
theorems.statement: [Rupture by Invariant Loss] If a critical invariant has no admissible witness on any support, then S notin Critop . Loss of a witness on one chosen support invalidates that support's certificate, but does not exclude a certificate on another support without further analysis. Quotient undefinedness, triviality and loss of legibility are not mutually exclusive labels and need not accompany every loss of criterion membership.

theorems.title: Reduced criterion
theorems.statement: [Reduced criterion] Let [ mathfrak I = Iper , allowbreak Iri , allowbreak Iint , allowbreak Icont , allowbreak Idiff , allowbreak Ileg . ] For every subset J subseteq mathfrak I define the reduced class [ mathcal C _ mathrm op (J):= S:I(S)=1 text for every I in J . ]

theorems.title: Single-rupture witness family
theorems.statement: [Single-rupture witness family] leavevmode par Fix one invariant index k in mathrm per , mathrm ri , mathrm int , mathrm cont , mathrm diff , mathrm leg . A single-rupture witness family mathcal W _k consists of admissible systems for which predicate I_k fails and every other predicate holds on the declared comparison domain.

theorems.title: Single-rupture witnesses create false positives
theorems.statement: [Single-rupture witnesses create false positives] Let J_k= mathfrak I setminus I_k and assume mathcal W _k neq varnothing . Then every S in mathcal W _k satisfies [ S in mathcal C _ mathrm op (J_k) qquad text but qquad S notin Critop . ]

theorems.label: thm:invariant-basis-minimality
theorems.title: Minimality of the six-invariant basis
theorems.statement: [Minimality of the six-invariant basis] Let mathfrak U be any admissible universe containing at least one single-rupture witness for each invariant. Then no strict subset of mathfrak I is extensionally equivalent to Critop on mathfrak U .

theorems.label: crit:legibility
theorems.title: Legibility certificate
theorems.statement: [Legibility certificate] An operational partition candidate is certified only if: [leftmargin=1.5em] item comparator separability holds against pre-registered baselines; item admissible noise does not dissolve the class map below the legibility margin; item the same class assignment survives on windows of length at least tau _ min (S) ; item targeted interventions on an invariant induce the predicted directional class change; item sham or off-target interventions do not generate the same class signature; item audit-friendly compression preserves class structure without total collapse.

theorems.label: prop:legibility
theorems.title: Legibility is jointly constrained
theorems.statement: [Legibility is jointly constrained] No single legibility metric is sufficient for Ileg . The invariant requires simultaneous control of separation, admissible noise robustness, persistence window, intervention fidelity, negative controls, and structured compressibility.

theorems.label: def:cert
theorems.title: Base criterion certificate
theorems.statement: [Base criterion certificate] A BaseCore criterion certificate for an admissible system S is a tuple [ Cert (S)= bigl ( Aset , Dec _S, pi _S, Delta (S),E_S bigr ), ] where: [leftmargin=1.5em] item Aset is a certified admissible support; item Dec _S is a certified decoder family; item pi _S is the decoder-induced partition on admissible histories; item Delta (S) is the witness margin vector; item E_S is the evidence bundle localizing the witness for each invariant.

theorems.label: crit:cert
theorems.title: Candidate certification rule
theorems.statement: [Candidate certification rule] A candidate system may be certified as a member of Critop only if all of the following are available on the same admissible support: [leftmargin=1.5em] item a non-empty compact forward-invariant support certificate; item a positive witness margin vector Delta (S)>0 coordinate-wise; item a decoder family satisfying Definition~ ref def:ileg ; item a targeted intervention panel together with negative controls; item an auditable compression map preserving class structure; item a traceable dependency ledger showing which upstream result supports each invariant witness.

theorems.title: Certified criterion membership
theorems.statement: [Certified criterion membership] If Cert (S) exists and satisfies Criterion~ ref crit:cert , then S in Critop and Partop (S) is well-defined.

theorems.title: Boundary discipline
theorems.statement: [Boundary discipline] The section above defines a theorem-tight grammar for certification, rupture, and falsation. It does not prove phenomenality, subjectivity, biological primacy, or cross-substrate identity transport.

theorems.label: def:forensic-packet
theorems.title: Forensic packet
theorems.statement: [Forensic packet] Each operational run emits a packet [ K=( mathrm tick , mathrm seed , mathrm versionHash ,H_v, mathrm metrics , mathrm sensorSummary , mathrm checksum ). ]

theorems.label: ass:packet-admissibility
theorems.title: Packet admissibility
theorems.statement: [Packet admissibility] A run is admissible only if checksum, schema, seed consistency, version hash, and H_v consistency all pass. A claimed replay must also pass its critical-state comparison. Write a(K) in 0,1 for this conjunction of required checks.

theorems.label: def:severe-violation
theorems.title: Severe violation
theorems.statement: [Severe violation] A run has a severe violation if any of the following holds: checksum mismatch, schema failure, seed/version inconsistency, or critical-state replay mismatch.

theorems.label: crit:integrity-gate
theorems.title: Integrity gate
theorems.statement: [Integrity gate] Severely violated runs are excluded from support counting and marked as hard failures.

theorems.label: prop:integrity-first
theorems.title: Integrity-first inference
theorems.statement: [Integrity-first inference] Let an actionable decision use the rule A(K,p)=a(K) mathbf 1_ p leq alpha , with a declared threshold alpha , and let a run contribute support only through a(K) mathbf 1_ text support condition . If any required admissibility check fails, both contributions are zero, regardless of p .

theorems.label: def:operational-certification
theorems.title: Operational Certification Indicator
theorems.statement: [Operational Certification Indicator] Keep Cert (S) for the certificate object of Definition~ ref def:cert . Define a distinct mathematical indicator operatorname CertFlag (S) to be 1 exactly when there exists such a certificate satisfying Criterion~ ref crit:cert on one common admissible support and meeting the integrity grammar above; otherwise its value is 0 . This does not identify a tuple with a Boolean value. An empirical audit may have an unknown verdict: missing evidence is not a proof that this mathematical indicator is zero.

theorems.label: def:equivalence-discriminator
theorems.title: Equivalence discriminator
theorems.statement: [Equivalence discriminator] For two admissible systems S_1,S_2 , define Eq _ Gamma , eps (S_1,S_2)=1 when the relevant signatures, admissibility bundle, decoder behavior, and invariant deltas match within the allowed comparison regime. A numerical match is not by itself an isomorphism of all certificate data; the sufficient transport conditions are specified below.

theorems.label: def:rupture-event
theorems.title: Rupture event
theorems.statement: [Rupture event] Fix a candidate certificate and a targeted invariant family J . The notation Rupt _J(S)=1 is relative to that declared certificate and means that an admissible intervention or perturbation defeats at least one of its required witness obligations or certified margins. The affected certificate then becomes invalid or unavailable. Exclusion of every replacement certificate is a separate quantified assertion.

theorems.label: prop:complexity-only-negative-control
theorems.title: Complexity-only negative control prediction
theorems.statement: [Complexity-only negative control prediction] Suppose that for every admissible support at least one of the six required predicates fails, so no common support realizes their conjunction. Then [ operatorname CertFlag (S)=0, qquad S notin Critop , qquad Partop (S) text is not certified . ] High connectivity, entropy or activity alone does not replace that conjunction. The hypothesis is universal nonexistence, not failure to find a support in a finite search.

theorems.label: prop:ablation-prediction
theorems.title: Ablation prediction
theorems.statement: [Ablation prediction] Let c be a fixed certificate with its stored support, witnesses and margins. If an intervention makes a required obligation false for the transported tuple, that tuple is no longer a valid certificate. This does not exclude replacement witnesses on the same support or a replacement certificate on another support.

theorems.label: prop:grammar-transport-prediction
theorems.title: Exact grammar-transport prediction
theorems.statement: [Exact grammar-transport prediction] Suppose a bijection of state spaces and inverse transport preserve the complete certificate data: dynamics and time windows, admissible supports, attractors and collapse sets, intervention/cost classes, identity comparison metrics, factorization and decoder classes, readout distances and noise domains, and the probability laws of the declared target/control populations. Then valid certificates transport in both directions and criterion membership is equivalent. For an approximate transport, a given certificate persists if the error is smaller than all its certified radii in the same perturbation metric and all remaining discrete admissibility data are preserved.

theorems.label: prop:threshold-sensitive-boundary
theorems.title: Threshold-sensitive boundary behavior
theorems.statement: [Threshold-sensitive boundary behavior] On a fixed admissible parameter patch, suppose a candidate certificate's required tests are represented exactly by six signed margins m_i( lambda )>0 , and the other admissibility data remain fixed. If each margin is L_i -Lipschitz, write L= max _iL_i and m= min _i m_i . A perturbation of parameter distance at most r preserves a pass where m>Lr and a failure of that candidate where m<-Lr . For a scalar threshold parameter with m( lambda _*)=0 and |m( lambda )| geq s| lambda - lambda _*| , s>0 , measurement error eta and parameter error r confine ambiguity to [ | lambda - lambda _*| leq ( eta +Lr)/s. ] Thus a band-width bound requires an explicit transversal lower slope; no universal narrow band follows without it.

theorems.label: prop:legibility-dependence
theorems.title: Legibility dependence prediction
theorems.statement: [Legibility dependence prediction] Failure of a required clause L1--L6 invalidates the particular legibility certificate using that decoder, protocol and budget. Excluding legibility altogether requires failure for every admitted candidate. In the uniform-distortion version of L6, if M declared classes are pairwise at class-metric distance at least sigma _C>0 , distortion below sigma _C/2 with an integer B -bit code requires M leq 2^B .

theorems.label: prop:continuity-nonnull-relevance
theorems.title: Continuity and non-null relevance
theorems.statement: [Continuity and non-null relevance] Failure of Icont or Idiff excludes the operational criterion. In particular Idiff fails if every admitted differentiation comparison has zero history separation, or if the null class is an asymptotically stable admissible attractor. Falling below a stored positive margin invalidates that certificate; merely tending toward zero does not imply failure at a finite parameter value or exclude recertification at a smaller positive margin.

theorems.title: What stays outside BaseCore
theorems.statement: [What stays outside BaseCore] Runtime status classes, empirical comparative programs, human comparator campaigns, Papers 7--9, and bridge-facing burden architectures remain downstream constructs. BaseCore includes only the falsation grammar and claim-boundary semantics needed to keep theorem hypotheses explicit.

theorems.title: Discrete State Space
theorems.statement: [Discrete State Space] Let N geq 1 and let a node network be indexed by i in 1, dots ,N . Each node carries: [leftmargin=*] item a local coherence state x_i(t) in ; item an energy coordinate e_i(t) in ; item a phase coordinate phi _i(t) in ^N times ^N times

theorems.title: Mean Coherence Observable
theorems.statement: [Mean Coherence Observable] leavevmode par For a discrete state s(t)=((x_i(t))_i,(e_i(t))_i,( phi _i(t))_i) in mathcal S _N , define [ X_N(t):= frac 1 N sum _ i=1 ^N x_i(t) in . ] This is an observable of the coherence coordinate only; it is not a complete state descriptor.

theorems.title: Finite Hilbert Embedding
theorems.statement: [Finite Hilbert Embedding] Let [ Hilb _N:= mathbb R ^N, qquad inner mathbf a mathbf b _N:= frac 1 N sum _ i=1 ^N a_i b_i. ] The coherence embedding [ iota _N: mathcal S _N to Hilb _N ] is [ iota _N((x_i)_i,(e_i)_i,( phi _i)_i)=(x_1, dots ,x_N). ] Thus iota _N forgets energy and phase except where they enter the transition rule below.

theorems.title: Piecewise-Constant Isometry
theorems.statement: [Piecewise-Constant Isometry] Let Hilb =L^2([0,1]) and partition [0,1] into intervals [ I_ N,i = left Define J_N: Hilb _N hookrightarrow Hilb by [ (J_N mathbf x )(s)=x_i quad text for s in I_ N,i . ] Then J_N is an isometry from ( Hilb _N, norm cdot _N) into L^2([0,1]) . Its adjoint J_N^ dagger : Hilb to Hilb _N is the cell-averaging map [ (J_N^ dagger f)_i=N int _ I_ N,i f(s) ,ds. ]

theorems.title: Discrete Transition Operator
theorems.statement: [Discrete Transition Operator] Fix auxiliary energy and phase coordinates (e_i)_i and ( phi _i)_i , a graph with incoming neighborhoods operatorname conn (i) , and a control u in U . Write [ C_N=[0,1]^N, qquad d_N^ rm in = max _i| operatorname conn (i)|, qquad d_N^ rm out = max _j| i:j in operatorname conn (i) |. ] The coherence-coordinate transition [ widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi :C_N to C_N ] is defined componentwise by [ bigl ( widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi mathbf x bigr )_i = operatorname clamp _ [0,1] ! left ( x_i+ eta R_i( mathbf x ;e, phi )+ alpha ,B_i( mathbf x )+ Gamma _ N,i (u) right ), ] where [ R_i( mathbf x ;e, phi ) = sum _ j in operatorname conn (i) I_j(x_j) frac exp (-|e_i-e_j|/(kT)) theta cos ( phi _i- phi _j) . ] Here I_j:[0,1] to is the intensity readout, B_i is a feedback term, Ga

theorems.label: ass:discrete-regularity
theorems.title: Discrete Regularity Conditions
theorems.statement: [Discrete Regularity Conditions] For a fixed parameter region, assume: [leftmargin=*] item I_j is L_I -Lipschitz for every node j . item The phase denominator is uniformly separated from zero: there exists c_ phi >0 such that | cos ( phi _i- phi _j)| ge c_ phi on every active edge. item There exist beta >0 and an L_D -Lipschitz map D:C_N to Hilb _N such that B( mathbf x )=- beta mathbf x +D( mathbf x ) . item Gamma _N(u) is independent of mathbf x for fixed u . item The parameters satisfy [ L_R:= frac L_I sqrt d_N^ rm in d_N^ rm out theta c_ phi , qquad rho _N:=|1- alpha beta |+ eta L_R+ alpha L_D<1. ]

theorems.title: Relation to the runtime guard
theorems.statement: [Relation to the runtime guard] A denominator guard can ensure that the quotient is defined on a parameter region. It does not establish the dissipative feedback condition or contractivity. On the stated energy domain and for kT>0 , the exponential coefficient is at most 1 . The conditions above are sufficient, not necessary; a specified feedback must be checked against them.

theorems.label: lem:directed-resonance-bound
theorems.title: Directed Resonance Bound
theorems.statement: [Directed Resonance Bound] Under the first two regularity conditions, R is L_R -Lipschitz in the normalized Hilbert norm.

theorems.label: thm:discrete-contraction
theorems.title: Discrete Operator Contractivity
theorems.statement: [Discrete Operator Contractivity] Under Assumption~ ref ass:discrete-regularity , for fixed u,e, phi the operator widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi is a strict contraction on the complete set C_N : [ norm widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi ( mathbf x )- widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi ( mathbf y ) _N le rho _N norm mathbf x - mathbf y _N qquad forall mathbf x , mathbf y in C_N. ] It has a unique fixed point in C_N , and every iterate starting there converges to it.

theorems.label: ex:discrete-identity-control

Its validity and any claimed rate must be proved for the discretization under consideration; H1--H5 alone do not provide a quadrature rate.

theorems.label: prop:joint-energy-phase-controls
theorems.title: Joint Bridge Failure Controls
theorems.statement: [Joint Bridge Failure Controls] A positive local memory gain can prevent uniform consistency on the full L^2 box. A unit local gain can prevent strict contractivity. A large spectral radius of an upper-bound matrix alone decides only whether that matrix certifies contraction.

Thus even strict contractions need additional structure for a uniform approximation rate over all of C . The profile-based realization above supplies that structure explicitly.

theorems.label: rem:bridge-applicability
theorems.title: Applicability to the Current QICN Runtime
theorems.statement: [Applicability to the Current QICN Runtime] Application to any implementation requires identifying its actual state domain, coefficients, feedback, frozen or evolving auxiliary coordinates, and approximation error. Network size or mean degree alone cannot discharge these conditions. The realized family above is an explicit mathematical example; no assertion is made here that a current runtime implements it or satisfies its hypotheses.

theorems.title: No duplicated theorem ownership
theorems.statement: [No duplicated theorem ownership] The present paper does not re-prove rigid identity, forced continuity, null-instability, legibility, or the well-definedness of Qop (S) from scratch. It imports those results and proves a new relation among them.

theorems.label: def:bridge-system
theorems.title: Admissible system and support
theorems.statement: [Admissible system and support] Throughout the paper, an admissible system is the Paper 5 tuple [ S=(X, Phi ,C,R, Gamma ,U), ] with admissible support Aset subseteq X_ Gamma . The transition family is written Phi = Phi _u _ u in U , where U is the set of admissible interventions. Histories, certified decoders, class sets, and admissible windows are inherited from Paper 5.

theorems.label: def:bridge-cop
theorems.title: Six-predicate operational criterion membership
theorems.statement: [Six-predicate operational criterion membership] An admissible system belongs to Cop exactly when all six Paper 5 invariants hold on Aset : [ S in Cop quad Longleftrightarrow quad Iper (S)= Iri (S)= Iint (S)= Icont (S)= Idiff (S)= Ileg (S)=1. ] When the witness margins are needed, write [ Delta (S)= bigl ( delta _ mathrm per , delta _ mathrm ri , delta _ mathrm int , delta _ mathrm cont , delta _ mathrm diff , delta _ mathrm leg bigr ). ]

theorems.label: def:bridge-implication
theorems.title: Bridge-strength implication
theorems.statement: [Bridge-strength implication] A bridge concept P is emph entailed by Cop if every admissible system S satisfying Definition~ ref def:bridge-cop satisfies P(S) . It is emph conditionally entailed if there exists an explicitly named additional hypothesis H such that S in Cop and H(S) imply P(S) . It is emph not entailed if a consistent admissible descriptor model can satisfy Cop while failing P .

theorems.title: Why a bridge-strength vocabulary is needed
theorems.statement: [Why a bridge-strength vocabulary is needed] Without Definition~ ref def:bridge-implication , the paper would risk conflating three different statements: a theorem from Cop , a theorem from Cop plus an added burden, and a philosophical association. Only the first two are formal claims.

theorems.label: def:sigma-op
theorems.title: Autonomous Commuting Self-Model $\Sigmaop$
theorems.statement: [Autonomous Commuting Self-Model Sigmaop ] The autonomous condition Sigmaop (S)=1 holds if an admissible system S has a map [ Sigma : Aset to Aset ] and constants eps _ Sigma ge 0 and 0 le L_ Sigma <1 such that: [leftmargin=1.5em] item textbf Approximate self-accuracy: for every x in Aset , [ d_X( Sigma (x),x) le eps _ Sigma . ] item textbf Contractive stabilization: [ d_X( Sigma (x), Sigma (y)) le L_ Sigma d_X(x,y) quad text for all x,y in Aset . ] item textbf Intervention commutation: for every admissible intervention u in U , [ Sigma circ Phi _u = Phi _u circ Sigma quad text on Aset . ] Any such Sigma is called a contractive admissible self-model.

theorems.label: ass:sigma1
theorems.title: Self-model hypothesis $\Sigma1$
theorems.statement: [Self-model hypothesis Sigma 1 ] The system S satisfies Sigma 1 when it admits a contractive admissible self-model in the sense of Definition~ ref def:sigma-op .

theorems.label: thm:sigma-common-fixed-point
theorems.title: Exact Commutation Requires a Common Fixed Point
theorems.statement: [Exact Commutation Requires a Common Fixed Point] Let Aset be a nonempty complete metric space. If a strict contraction Sigma : Aset to Aset commutes with each admissible self-map Phi _u , then its unique fixed point is fixed by every Phi _u . On the common tower support of Paper V, the two neutral controls with phase commands 0 and 1/4 exclude such a Sigma .

theorems.title: Fibre Truncation Has a Sharp Commutation Defect
theorems.statement: [Fibre Truncation Has a Sharp Commutation Defect] On the tower (p, theta ,b) with c(b)= sum _ j ge 1 2b_j3^ -j , fix m ge 1 and let b^ star =(0,1,0,1, ldots ) . The truncation T_m fixes p, theta ,b_1, ldots ,b_m and fills the tail with that of b^ star . In the metric max mathbf 1_ p ne p' , rho ( theta , theta '),|c(b)-c(b')| it has uniform approximation error at most 3^ -m and Lipschitz constant zero within every fibre of the retained data. For Phi _ u,q (p, theta ,b)=(p,u+q lambda b_1,Rb) with Rb=(0,1-b_1,1-b_2, ldots ) , its pointwise commutation defect is [ d(T_m Phi _ u,q x, Phi _ u,q T_m x) =2 ,3^ -(m+1) , mathbf 1_ b_m ne b^ star _m . ] In particular the uniform defect is exactly 2 ,3^ -(m+1) .

theorems.title: Fixed-Point Displacement under Approximate Commutation
theorems.statement: [Fixed-Point Displacement under Approximate Commutation] Let Sigma be an L -Lipschitz self-map of a nonempty complete metric space, where 0 le L<1 , and let p be its fixed point. In particular, [ (1-L)d( Phi _u(p), Phi _v(p)) le e_u(p)+e_v(p). ] If both uniform defects are bounded by varepsilon , the separation is at most 2 varepsilon /(1-L) . Both bounds are sharp, including simultaneously on rational affine models.

For a global L -contraction the two native neutral phases 0,1/4 force uniform defect at least (1-L)/8 . The full neutral family of phases forces defect at least (1-L)/2 . In fact with all phases the sharp uniform floor is 1/2 for every L<1 , even allowing the other writable commands, and uniform reconstruction error is at least 1/2 . In contrast, the depth- d truncation T_d of Proposition~ ref prop:sigma-fibre-truncation , extended to retain memory as well as phase, profile and the first d ge 1 digits, is constant on each retained-data fibre. theorems.label: prop:sigma-not-entailed
theorems.title: Conditional obstruction to self-reference within $\Cop$
theorems.statement: [Conditional obstruction to self-reference within Cop ] If a complete admissible support witnessing Cop has no common fixed point of its admitted interventions, then it has no self-model of Definition~ ref def:sigma-op on that support. Such a system refutes entailment on the declared support once all six upstream witnesses are supplied.

theorems.label: thm:sigma-equivariant-tower-realization
