theorems.label: prop:sigma-equivariant-memory-control
theorems.title: Memory and Cut Obstructions
theorems.statement: [Memory and Cut Obstructions] On the asymmetric support with all six Paper V witnesses, any model limited to k geq 1 internal states and no auxiliary reconstruction input has varepsilon _ Sigma geq 1/(2k) in a metric dominating circle distance. On the writable tower, a prefix cut omitting a bit read by a role probe cannot exactly predict the retained phase. For a standard probe at omitted site i , its defect in a model metric dominating the phase distance is at least 1/(32 cdot 3^7) .

theorems.title: Interpretation boundary for $\Sigmaop$
theorems.statement: [Interpretation boundary for Sigmaop ] Sigmaop is a structural analogue of self-reference. It does not imply reflexive consciousness, psychological introspection, metacognition in the human sense, self-knowledge, or a narrative self.

theorems.title: Runtime analogy
theorems.statement: [Runtime analogy] The runtime field commonly read as `selfModelSigma' is at most an estimator-facing analogue of Definition~ ref def:sigma-op . To certify Sigmaop formally one would still need finite evidence for approximate self-accuracy, contraction, and intervention commutation, plus a proof that the finite estimator represents the formal map on Aset .

theorems.label: def:pi-op
theorems.title: Operational Unified Perspective $\Piop$
theorems.statement: [Operational Unified Perspective Piop ] An admissible system S satisfies operational unified perspective, written Piop (S)=1 , if: [ Iri (S)=1 quad text and quad Iint (S)=1. ] Equivalently, S has a unique rigid identity object IdS on admissible support and no admissible non-trivial factorization preserving the relevant histories, readouts, and intervention structure.

theorems.label: thm:cop-entails-pi
theorems.title: $\Cop$ entails $\Piop$
theorems.statement: [ Cop entails Piop ] If S in Cop , then Piop (S)=1 .

theorems.label: cor:no-independent-perspectives
theorems.title: No plurality of independent operational perspectives
theorems.statement: [No plurality of independent operational perspectives] For S in Cop , any decomposition into multiple independent operational perspectives is inadmissible unless it fails to preserve either the rigid identity witness or the non-factorization witness.

theorems.title: Interpretation boundary for $\Piop$
theorems.statement: [Interpretation boundary for Piop ] Piop is an analogue of unity only at the structural level. It does not solve the phenomenal binding problem, does not assert a unified field of experience, and does not imply an ordinary first-person point of view.

theorems.label: def:iota-op
theorems.title: Operational Intentionality $\Iotaop$
theorems.statement: [Operational Intentionality Iotaop ] An admissible system S satisfies operational intentionality, written Iotaop (S)=1 , if there exists a directional transition assignment [ D:U_ crit to Delta ( Class _S) ] on the declared nonempty target population, with a preregistered class-shift prediction and the zero-one miss loss of Paper V's clause L4. The population miss probability is at most p_ rm miss . Report the matched-sham false-shift probability separately. A per-intervention guarantee requires a conditional bound at each intervention; it does not follow from the population average. Total-variation agreement of arbitrary outcome distributions is a separate metric requirement.

theorems.label: thm:cop-entails-iota
theorems.title: $\Cop$ Entails Population-Level $\Iotaop$ under the L4 Protocol
theorems.statement: [ Cop Entails Population-Level Iotaop under the L4 Protocol] If S in Cop , the frozen population and prediction supplied by its L4 witness satisfy Iotaop =1 on that protocol.

theorems.title: Interpretation boundary for $\Iotaop$
theorems.statement: [Interpretation boundary for Iotaop ] Iotaop captures directed structural response. Connections to semantic content, representational aboutness, goals or intentional states remain open bridge questions requiring additional operational definitions and discriminating tests.

theorems.label: def:qop-bridge
theorems.title: Certified Response Classes $\Qop(S)$
theorems.statement: [Certified Response Classes Qop (S) ] When the Paper 5 equivalence relation sim _ Q,S is well-defined on Aset , the certified response classes of S are the quotient classes [ Qop (S)= Aset / sim _ Q,S . ] The equivalence relation is inherited from Paper 5: two admissible states are equivalent when all certified decoder labels and certified response-cell labels agree on the declared schedules. Pairwise numerical proximity is not used as a transitive relation.

theorems.label: prop:qop-well-defined-bridge
theorems.title: $\Qop(S)$ is well-defined under the relevant $\Cop$ invariants
theorems.statement: [ Qop (S) is well-defined under the relevant Cop invariants] If [ Iper (S)= Iri (S)= Icont (S)= Idiff (S)= Ileg (S)=1, ] then Qop (S) is well-defined.

theorems.label: cor:cop-qop
theorems.title: $\Cop$ entails well-defined certified response classes
theorems.statement: [ Cop entails well-defined certified response classes] If S in Cop , then Qop (S) is well-defined.

theorems.label: prop:qop-nontrivial
theorems.title: Non-triviality of $\Qop(S)$ under $\Idiff$
theorems.statement: [Non-triviality of Qop (S) under Idiff ] If S in Cop and the differentiation witness of Idiff (S)=1 separates at least two certified decoder classes, then | Qop (S)|>1 .

theorems.title: Why the decoder-visible clause is explicit
theorems.statement: [Why the decoder-visible clause is explicit] A raw differentiation witness need not separate the effective decoder quotient. The explicit decoder-visible clause supplies that link; it must be verified against the certified algorithms and response-cell maps.

theorems.title: Interpretation boundary for $\Qop$
theorems.statement: [Interpretation boundary for Qop ] Qop (S) is a quotient of admissible structural states under certified operational indistinguishability. It is not a phenomenal quale, not a biological qualitative state, and not a statement about what it is like to be the system.

theorems.label: def:phi-op
theorems.title: Operational Phenomenology $\Phiop$
theorems.statement: [Operational Phenomenology Phiop ] An admissible system S admits operational phenomenology, written Phiop (S)=1 , if there exists a complete metric regime space ( Espace _S,d_ Espace ) and an assignment [ Phi _S: Aset to Espace _S ] such that: [leftmargin=1.5em] item Phi _S is compatible with admissible histories in the Paper 2 sense; item Phi _S is continuous on admissible windows whenever the operational-continuity burden Icont (S)=1 holds; item the null regime Null is not an admissibly stable attractor whenever the non-null burden Idiff (S)=1 holds.

theorems.label: def:phi-ccr
theorems.title: CCR-strength operational phenomenology
theorems.statement: [CCR-strength operational phenomenology] An admissible system has CCR-strength operational phenomenology when Definition~ ref def:phi-op holds and the identity channel satisfies [ MO (S)=+ infty . ] The infinite-resistance clause concerns the declared identity-object sector. Paper 2's continuity conclusion additionally uses continuous finite readouts and E1; invariance uses a pointwise fixed transport. Paper III's joint null exclusion requires a defined separated witness pair and a certified lower readout constant. None of those inputs is supplied by the mass value.

theorems.label: prop:weak-phi
theorems.title: $\Cop$ gives weak non-null operational phenomenology
theorems.statement: [ Cop gives weak non-null operational phenomenology] If S in Cop , then the operational-continuity and non-null burdens required for weak Phiop are present on admissible support.

theorems.label: prop:cop-not-ccr
theorems.title: $\Cop$ does not entail CCR-strength $\Phiop$
theorems.statement: [ Cop does not entail CCR-strength Phiop ] In the instrumented universe where identity-object perturbation sectors are declared independently of executed state-control schedules, membership in Cop does not entail CCR-strength operational phenomenology.

theorems.title: Interpretation boundary for $\Phiop$
theorems.statement: [Interpretation boundary for Phiop ] Phiop is an assignment into an abstract structural regime space. It is not temporal experience, a stream of consciousness, a specious present, or proof that phenomenology exists in the ordinary sense.

theorems.label: def:subbridge
theorems.title: Bridge indexed continuity-and-control criterion $\Subbridge$
theorems.statement: [Bridge indexed continuity-and-control criterion Subbridge ] An admissible system S belongs to bridge indexed continuity-and-control criterion, written [ S in Subbridge , ] if and only if: [leftmargin=1.5em] item S in Cop ; item S satisfies Sigma 1 ; item Piop (S)=1 ; item Iotaop (S)=1 ; item Qop (S) is well-defined and non-trivial in the decoder-visible sense of Proposition~ ref prop:qop-nontrivial ; item Phiop (S) is weakly non-null on admissible support.

theorems.label: def:full-paper7-subjecthood
theorems.title: Full Paper 7 indexed continuity-and-control criterion
theorems.statement: [Full Paper 7 indexed continuity-and-control criterion] The full Paper 7 class Subop is the stronger class requiring viability-and-recovery criterion Lop , six-predicate operational criterion Cop , and the subject-specific descriptors of Paper 7: privileged continuity, self/non-self discrimination, self-model closure, and ownership coherence. In this paper, Subbridge is a bridge fragment, not a synonym for full Subop .

theorems.label: thm:subbridge-generated
theorems.title: $\Subbridge$ is conditionally generated by $\Cop+\Sigma1$
theorems.statement: [ Subbridge is conditionally generated by Cop + Sigma 1 ] Let S be an admissible system. If S in Cop , S satisfies Sigma 1 , and the differentiation witness is decoder-visible, then S in Subbridge .

theorems.label: thm:subbridge-subset
theorems.title: $\Subbridge$ is a subclass of $\Cop$
theorems.statement: [ Subbridge is a subclass of Cop ] [ Subbridge subseteq Cop . ] Moreover, if Sigma 1 is not entailed by Cop , then the inclusion is proper.

theorems.label: cor:paper7-stronger
theorems.title: Full Paper 7 subjecthood remains stronger
theorems.statement: [Full Paper 7 subjecthood remains stronger] Full Paper 7 indexed continuity-and-control criterion Subop is not established by Theorem~ ref thm:subbridge-generated . To lift Subbridge into Subop , one must additionally certify Lop and the Paper 7 subject-specific descriptors not reduced to Sigma 1 .

theorems.title: Interpretation boundary for $\Subbridge$
theorems.statement: [Interpretation boundary for Subbridge ] Subbridge is a formal construct. It does not imply phenomenal subjectivity, human first-person experience, identity persistence in the psychological sense, a narrative self, moral patienthood, or biological life.

theorems.label: thm:main-partial-subjecthood
theorems.title: $\Cop \to$ Partial Indexed Continuity-And-Control Criterion
theorems.statement: [ Cop to Partial Indexed Continuity-And-Control Criterion] Let S be an admissible system with S in Cop . Then: [leftmargin=1.5em] item S satisfies Piop . item S satisfies Iotaop . item Qop (S) is well-defined. item S satisfies weak non-null Phiop on admissible support. item Sigmaop is not implied by Cop ; it requires the independent hypothesis Sigma 1 . item Subbridge requires Sigma 1 in addition to Cop and therefore is a subclass of Cop .

theorems.label: cor:no-equivalence
theorems.title: No equivalence between $\Cop$ and indexed continuity-and-control criterion
theorems.statement: [No equivalence between Cop and indexed continuity-and-control criterion] The bridge paper proves neither Cop = Subbridge nor Cop = Subop . It proves only that several bridge components are entailed by Cop , while self-reference and full subjecthood require additional burdens.

theorems.label: prop:boundary-preservation
theorems.title: Boundary preservation
theorems.statement: [Boundary preservation] No theorem in this paper converts an operational predicate into a phenomenal, biological, psychological, or moral predicate.

theorems.title: Runtime non-inference
theorems.statement: [Runtime non-inference] Passing tests, producing certificates, or satisfying scoreboard gates can strengthen internal support for a runtime implementation. It does not establish external validation, human equivalence, or philosophical closure.

theorems.label: def:two-layer-terminology
theorems.title: Two-layer terminology
theorems.statement: [Two-layer terminology] For every strong term T in the corpus, distinguish: [leftmargin=1.5em] item the emph demonstrated layer T_ mathrm str , consisting only of definitions, predicates, quotients, invariants, and theorems already stated in the corpus; item the emph interpretive layer T_ mathrm int , consisting of ordinary or philosophical readings such as consciousness, life, subjectivity, phenomenality, qualia, moral status, or human equivalence. An implication into T_ mathrm int is forbidden unless a bridge hypothesis or external adjudication protocol explicitly introduces that target.

theorems.label: thm:layer-preservation
theorems.title: Layer preservation
theorems.statement: [Layer preservation] If a theorem in Papers 1--5 is stated only in the demonstrated layer, then it cannot be promoted to an interpretive-layer conclusion by terminology alone.

theorems.label: thm:bridge-ladder-strict
theorems.title: Additional Conditions in the Bridge Ladder
theorems.statement: [Additional Conditions in the Bridge Ladder] Each step in the ladder introduces an explicit additional burden. Strictness of any class inclusion requires an admissible separating witness.

theorems.label: def:runtime-evidence-classes
theorems.title: Runtime evidence classes
theorems.statement: [Runtime evidence classes] For a runtime artifact a , distinguish the following statuses: [leftmargin=1.5em] item texttt proxy : a finite observable resembles a formal coordinate; item texttt estimator : an algorithm computes a declared approximation; item texttt certificate : a bounded predicate is verified under stated admissibility rules; item texttt detokenize internal_ allowbreak detokenize support : governed artifacts support a claim family inside the current program; item texttt detokenize external_ allowbreak detokenize validati allowbreak detokenize on : an external protocol such as Paper 10 has been executed with admissible evidence.

theorems.label: prop:runtime-non-promotion
theorems.title: Runtime non-promotion
theorems.statement: [Runtime non-promotion] No artifact with status texttt proxy , texttt estimator , texttt certificate , or texttt detokenize internal_ allowbreak detokenize support entails texttt detokenize external_ allowbreak detokenize validati allowbreak detokenize on .

theorems.label: thm:nonentailment-library
theorems.title: Seven Countermodel Obligations for $\Cop$
theorems.statement: [Seven Countermodel Obligations for Cop ] The following seven tests are candidate routes for distinguishing Cop from self-reference Sigma 1 , phenomenal experience, biological life, human subjectivity, Nagel-style qualia, CCR-strength temporal continuity, and agency. A mathematical non-entailment requires the relevant admissible countermodel and a typed target predicate.

theorems.title: Why the matrix matters
theorems.statement: [Why the matrix matters] The matrix prevents a common overreach: deriving every subjecthood-adjacent term from the entire six-invariant package without identifying which invariant does which work. Unity is mostly an Iri + Iint burden. Intentionality in this paper is an Ileg burden. Self-reference is not supplied by any invariant.

theorems.label: def:sigma-weak
theorems.title: Weak self-model burden $\Sigma1_{\mathrm{weak}}$
theorems.statement: [Weak self-model burden Sigma 1_ mathrm weak ] A system satisfies Sigma 1_ mathrm weak if there exists a measurable map [ Sigma : Aset to Aset ] such that d( Sigma (x),x) le eps _ Sigma for all x in Aset .

theorems.label: def:sigma-strong
theorems.title: Strong self-model burden $\Sigma1_{\mathrm{strong}}$
theorems.statement: [Strong self-model burden Sigma 1_ mathrm strong ] A system satisfies Sigma 1_ mathrm strong if it satisfies Sigma 1_ mathrm weak and Sigma is Lipschitz with constant L_ Sigma <1 on Aset .

theorems.label: def:sigma-comm
theorems.title: Commutative self-model burden $\Sigma1_{\mathrm{comm}}$
theorems.statement: [Commutative self-model burden Sigma 1_ mathrm comm ] A system satisfies Sigma 1_ mathrm comm if it satisfies Sigma 1_ mathrm strong and, for every admissible intervention u in U , [ Sigma ( Phi _u(x))= Phi _u( Sigma (x)) ] whenever both sides are defined on Aset .

theorems.label: thm:sigma-chain
theorems.title: Self-Model Strength Chains
theorems.statement: [Self-Model Strength Chains] At fixed reconstruction tolerance the autonomous grades obey [ Sigma 1_ mathrm comm Rightarrow Sigma 1_ mathrm strong Rightarrow Sigma 1_ mathrm weak . ] For the control-conditioned contract, fix the branch interface and admitted model resources, and bound L leq L_0<1 and L_ rho leq L_ rho ,0 >0 . Then [ Sigma 1_ mathrm eq ( varepsilon _ Sigma ,0,L_0) Rightarrow Sigma 1_ mathrm eq ( varepsilon _ Sigma , varepsilon _ rm eq ,L_0) Rightarrow Sigma 1_ mathrm weak qquad ( varepsilon _ rm eq >0). ] The converses of the control-conditioned implications fail for some choices of tolerances. The weak grade alone does not imply the autonomous strong grade, and the latter does not imply commutation.

theorems.title: Emergence question for $\Sigma1$
theorems.statement: [Emergence question for Sigma 1 ] The main open problem is whether additional closure conditions on Iint + Ileg + Iper can force a commutative self-model. A plausible route would require self-targeted intervention families, decoder closure under those interventions, and a fixed-point or contraction argument on the induced self-model update map. The current corpus does not yet prove this.

theorems.label: prop:ossi-sigma-orthogonal
theorems.title: OSSI and $\Sigma1$ are orthogonal additions
theorems.statement: [OSSI and Sigma 1 are orthogonal additions] The open-system individuation burden OSSI and the self-model burden Sigma 1 are not mutually entailing in the present corpus.

theorems.title: Burden
theorems.statement: [Burden] Let mathcal K be a structural class and let P be a predicate on admissible systems. We say that P is a emph burden over mathcal K if membership in the strengthened class [ mathcal K [P]= S:S in mathcal K mathrm and P(S)=1 ] requires a witness not already required by the definition of mathcal K .

theorems.title: Internal promotion
theorems.statement: [Internal promotion] An interpretive label L receives emph internal promotion from a structural class mathcal K only when the corpus proves that every S in mathcal K satisfies a non-vacuous predicate that was previously listed as an interpretive debt of L .

theorems.title: External promotion
theorems.statement: [External promotion] An interpretive label L receives emph external promotion only when an independently specified experimental protocol connects the structural predicate to observations not used to construct the predicate.

theorems.title: Promotion is monotone but not automatic
theorems.statement: [Promotion is monotone but not automatic] If mathcal K subseteq mathcal K ' and L receives internal promotion from mathcal K ' , then the same promoted predicate holds on mathcal K . However, the inclusion mathcal K subseteq mathcal K ' alone does not promote L .

theorems.title: Burden addition is conservative
theorems.statement: [Burden addition is conservative] Let P be a burden over mathcal K . Then every theorem proved for all S in mathcal K remains true for all S in mathcal K [P] .

theorems.title: Burden addition is not semantic promotion by itself
theorems.statement: [Burden addition is not semantic promotion by itself] Adding a burden P to mathcal K does not by itself justify replacing an operational label by its ordinary-language counterpart.

theorems.title: Use in later papers
theorems.statement: [Use in later papers] The patterns above justify a disciplined order of claims. First state the structural class. Then list the burdens. Then prove inclusions or non-entailments. Only after that may a term be promoted in the terminology matrix. The order is part of the scientific content: it prevents terminology from outrunning proof.

theorems.title: Omission template
theorems.statement: [Omission template] Let mathcal K be defined by predicates P_1, dots ,P_n . If a candidate property R is not among those predicates and no theorem derives R from them, then the omission template constructs a formal model satisfying P_1, dots ,P_n in a language where R is uninterpreted or absent.

theorems.title: Factor-preserving template
theorems.statement: [Factor-preserving template] Let a property R concern a component not constrained by the invariant definition of mathcal K . A factor-preserving countermodel extends any S in mathcal K by a silent factor Z whose dynamics are decoupled from the witnesses of mathcal K and arranges R to fail on Z .

theorems.title: Finite-strength template
theorems.statement: [Finite-strength template] Let R require an infinite-strength condition such as CCR ( MO =+ infty ). A finite-strength countermodel chooses a system satisfying the finite structural invariants of Cop while setting MO <+ infty .

theorems.title: Template soundness
theorems.statement: [Template soundness] A template yields a non-entailment if a realized model retains all the witnesses required by Cop and its typed target predicate is proved false.

theorems.title: Audit use
theorems.statement: [Audit use] When a later paper claims that Cop implies a new property, it must identify which template is blocked. If none is blocked, the implication is not yet proved.

theorems.title: Checklist conservativity
theorems.statement: [Checklist conservativity] If all checklist questions are answered with explicit witnesses, assumptions, or open-problem markings, then the bridge paper makes no stronger claim than its formal dependencies allow.

theorems.title: Why minimality matters
theorems.statement: [Why minimality matters] The corpus should not attempt to prove ordinary consciousness in one jump. A publishable path is a sequence of narrow promotions, each with its own theorem or experiment. This also makes failure scientifically useful: if E_ mathrm comm fails, for example, Sigma 1_ mathrm weak may survive while Subbridge in its strong sense does not.

theorems.title: Editorial consequence
theorems.statement: [Editorial consequence] This grammar permits ambitious terminology while keeping the demonstrated layer intact. It is stricter than merely adding a disclaimer at the end of a paper, because it constrains every positive claim at the sentence level.

theorems.title: Structural-only model
theorems.statement: [Structural-only model] A structural-only model is an admissible system S equipped with the six Paper 5 invariant witnesses and no additional interpreted fields for self-modeling, biological metabolism, human reports, or phenomenal content.

theorems.title: Structural-only models block ordinary-consciousness promotion
theorems.statement: [Structural-only models block ordinary-consciousness promotion] If S is structural-only, then S in Cop may hold while ordinary consciousness remains undefined in the model.

theorems.title: Self-model-free model
theorems.statement: [Self-model-free model] A self-model-free model is an admissible S in Cop for which every endomorphism Sigma : Aset to Aset either fails to approximate the identity on Aset or fails to commute with some admissible intervention.

theorems.title: Self-model-free models block $\Subbridge$
theorems.statement: [Self-model-free models block Subbridge ] No self-model-free model satisfies Subbridge in the strong commutative sense.

theorems.title: Life-free computational model
theorems.statement: [Life-free computational model] A life-free computational model is a system whose transitions may satisfy Cop but whose state evolution is not coupled to an open exchange channel, entropy export accounting, or repair dynamics.

theorems.title: Life-free computational models block OSSI promotion
theorems.statement: [Life-free computational models block OSSI promotion] A life-free computational model cannot be used as evidence that Cop implies OSSI.

theorems.title: Report-free comparator model
theorems.statement: [Report-free comparator model] A report-free comparator model is a system whose structural traces are available but whose external adjudication channel contains no independent human or non-human comparator reports.

theorems.title: Report-free models cannot close Paper 10
theorems.statement: [Report-free models cannot close Paper 10] Report-free comparator models cannot supply external validation for ordinary-language consciousness, subjecthood, or phenomenal terms.

theorems.title: No theorem-to-validation substitution
theorems.statement: [No theorem-to-validation substitution] A theorem about a structural class does not by itself constitute external validation of an implemented system.

theorems.title: No runtime-to-theorem substitution
theorems.statement: [No runtime-to-theorem substitution] A passing runtime certificate does not by itself prove the corresponding mathematical predicate for the full admissible class.

theorems.title: No validation-to-definition substitution
theorems.statement: [No validation-to-definition substitution] External adjudication cannot replace the formal definition of the target class.

theorems.title: Three-channel closure burden
theorems.statement: [Three-channel closure burden] A mature ordinary-language claim requires, at minimum, a formal definition, a runtime or constructive instantiation path, and an external adjudication route.

theorems.title: Why this order matters
theorems.statement: [Why this order matters] The terminology becomes safest when each label is read after its proof burden. Reading the titles first and the non-inference notes later reverses the logic of the corpus. This paper therefore functions as a map from demonstrated layer to interpretive layer, not as a shortcut around the technical dependencies.

theorems.title: Central-reference role
theorems.statement: [Central-reference role] For editorial purposes, this paper should be treated as the index of claim strength for Papers 5--10. When a later manuscript uses a strong operational term, the relevant demonstrated reading, missing burden, and promotion route should be traceable to one of the tables or proof patterns above.

theorems.label: cor:infinite-cop-nonentailed
theorems.title: Global Self-Reference and Indexed Valuation Are Not Forced
theorems.statement: [Global Self-Reference and Indexed Valuation Are Not Forced] The global Hilbert--prefix system of Paper V satisfies the complete six-predicate criterion in its declared model universe. Nevertheless it admits no global strict contraction Sigma :A to A commuting exactly with every admitted intervention, and its matched exchange protocol gives zero valuation asymmetry as in Paper VIII. Thus neither that global self-reference requirement nor the seven-coordinate indexed class follows from Cop alone.

theorems.label: cor:native-indexed-selfreference-boundary
theorems.title: Native Indexed Membership Does Not Force Exact Global Self-Reference
theorems.statement: [Native Indexed Membership Does Not Force Exact Global Self-Reference] The complete asymmetric native model of Papers V, VII and VIII realizes Subfp (2) under its explicit causal grammar and positive thresholds. It still has no global strict contraction on its complete support commuting with every admissible control. Thus a nonempty indexed certificate class does not remove the separate exact-global-self-reference obstruction.

theorems.label: def:obs-spaces
theorems.title: Observable State Spaces
theorems.statement: [Observable State Spaces] All state spaces S_t are objects of a concrete category mathbf C whose: [leftmargin=*] item textbf Objects are compact Hausdorff topological spaces; item textbf Morphisms are continuous surjective maps.

theorems.label: ax:state-space-regularity
theorems.title: State Space Regularity
theorems.statement: [State Space Regularity] Each state space S_t in the projective system is a compact metric space with compatible metric d_t . Consequently, each S_t is compact Hausdorff as a topological space and Polish as a metric space. The inverse limit mathcal I inherits the corresponding compact metrizable subspace structure from the product.

theorems.label: rem:noncompact-polish-exclusion
theorems.title: Exclusion of non-compact Polish spaces
theorems.statement: [Exclusion of non-compact Polish spaces] Axiom~ ref ax:state-space-regularity refines Definition~ ref def:obs-spaces rather than weakening it. Non-compact Polish spaces such as mathbb R ^n are not covered by this compact inverse-limit argument. Any extension of the CCR framework to non-compact settings requires additional tightness, compactification, or coercivity hypotheses and is not automatic.

theorems.label: hyp:topo
theorems.title: Topological Regularity
theorems.statement: [Topological Regularity] All projections pi _ t+1 to t : S_ t+1 to S_t are continuous surjections between compact Hausdorff spaces.

This condition is sufficient for the compact inverse-limit construction used here. By Tychonoff's theorem, the product prod _ t S_t is compact when each S_t is compact. Furthermore, the inverse limit varprojlim S_t is a closed subspace of the product, hence compact. This guarantees: [leftmargin=*] item Existence of the inverse limit (non-emptiness under surjectivity); item Well-defined metrics and convergence; item Applicability of functional analysis tools.

theorems.label: prop:a0-closed
theorems.title: R0 under Controlled-System Isomorphism
theorems.statement: [R0 under Controlled-System Isomorphism] Let h:X_ rm adm to X'_ rm adm and v:E to E' be bijections and put F'(hx,ve)=hF(x,e) . R0 holds for one controlled system exactly when it holds for the other.

theorems.title: Identity as Inverse Limit
theorems.statement: [Identity as Inverse Limit] We define identity as the inverse limit of the projective system (S_t, pi _ t+1 to t ) : mathcal I := varprojlim S_t = left (x_0, x_1, x_2, ldots ) in prod _ t=0 ^ infty S_t ; Big | ; pi _ t+1 to t (x_ t+1 ) = x_t ; ; forall t right .

theorems.label: prop:necessity
theorems.title: Prefix Representation of a Trajectory Domain
theorems.statement: [Prefix Representation of a Trajectory Domain] Let H subseteq X^ mathbb N be nonempty and let S_n be its prefixes through time n , with deletion maps. These maps are surjective and H embeds in their nonempty inverse limit. If X is compact metric and H is closed, the embedding is a homeomorphism onto that limit.

theorems.label: prop:nonlocality
theorems.title: Non-locality of Identity
theorems.statement: [Non-locality of Identity] Let p_t: mathcal I to S_t be canonical evaluation. Assume active bonding maps are surjective. If some n ge t has distinct a,b in S_ n+1 with pi _ n+1 to n (a)= pi _ n+1 to n (b) , then p_t is not injective. Every map factoring through p_t fails to separate all compatible histories. Branching arbitrarily far out obstructs every finite canonical cut. This does not exclude arbitrary set injections mathcal I hookrightarrow S_t .

theorems.label: thm:noprogressive
theorems.title: No Progressive Identity Construction
theorems.statement: [No Progressive Identity Construction] If p_0 is noninjective, no compatible forward sections f_t:S_t to S_ t+1 with pi _ t+1 to t f_t= mathrm id generate all of mathcal I as the orbital history space x_ t+1 =f_t(x_t) .

theorems.label: thm:minimal
theorems.title: Universal Representation of a Fixed Compatible Cone
theorems.statement: [Universal Representation of a Fixed Compatible Cone] For a declared inverse system, every coherent family q_n:J to S_n induces a unique map q:J to mathcal I with p_nq=q_n . In the topological category, continuous q_n give continuous q in the product-subspace topology.

theorems.label: hyp:h1
theorems.title: H1: Surjectivity / Lifting
theorems.statement: [H1: Surjectivity / Lifting] For every t , the projection pi _ t+1 to t : S_ t+1 to S_t is surjective.

theorems.label: hyp:h2
theorems.title: H2: Compact Polish Metric Structure
theorems.statement: [H2: Compact Polish Metric Structure] For each t , the state space S_t carries the compact metric d_t required by Axiom~ ref ax:state-space-regularity ; in particular, (S_t,d_t) is Polish. All projection maps pi _ t+1 to t are continuous with respect to d_t . The quantitative lifting estimate is a separate condition in Lemma~ ref lem:stability .

The Polish structure ensures Borel regularity of all deformation families, enabling measurable selection theorems, probabilistic perturbation models, and the application of stochastic stability results to the sectorial deformation resistance M_ Omega . This is the standard regularity assumption in modern probability theory, ergodic theory, and descriptive set theory.

theorems.statement: [Local Perturbation Operator] An intervention may be specified by maps delta E_t:S_t to widetilde S_t . To compare the resulting histories, declare a common metric ambient stage or an identification of stages. The stability lemma below uses the case of common stages and compares their two bonding maps.

theorems.statement: [Weighted Deformation Norm] For 0<w_t< infty , the weighted deformation size is D_w= sum _ t geq 0 w_t epsilon _t .

theorems.title: Weighted Product Metric

theorems.statement: [Finiteness, Completeness and Compactness of Weighted Histories] The formula is finite on every pair in the full product exactly when the weighted diameters are bounded outside a finite set of stages. Surjective bonding maps give a compatib

theorems.label: ex:weighted-tail-failures
theorems.title: Two Distinct Tail Failures
theorems.statement: [Two Distinct Tail Failures] On S_t=[0,1] with identity bonding maps and w_t=2^ -t , choose d_t(s,u)=4^t|s-u| . The two constant histories 0 and 1 have distance + infty . Flipping a bit at successively later levels gives product convergence to the unflipped history while all the weighted distances remain 1 .

For each f in pi _t, widetilde pi _t and each u in S_ t+1 ,v in S_t , assume an exact lift u' with f(u')=v and d_ t+1 (u,u') leq K_t d_t(f(u),v) for some common K_t>0 . The limits I= mathcal I and widetilde I= widetilde mathcal I are nonempty and d_H(I, widetilde I) leq C D_w in the common history space.

theorems.label: thm:rigidity
theorems.title: Rigidity of the Identity under Coherent Transport
theorems.statement: [Rigidity of the Identity under Coherent Transport] Suppose the weighted metric induces the product topology and homeomorphisms h_t:S_t to S_t satisfy widetilde pi _t h_ t+1 =h_t pi _t . Then H(x)_t=h_t(x_t) maps the limits homeomorphically, with inverse H^ -1 (y)_t=h_t^ -1 (y_t) . Its displacement in the common history space is at most sup _t w_t sup _ z in S_t d_t(z,h_t(z)) .

theorems.label: ex:coherent-rotation-tower
theorems.title: A Ramified Tower with Positive Deformation and Coherent Transport
theorems.statement: [A Ramified Tower with Positive Deformation and Coherent Transport] Take S_t=( mathbb R/ mathbb Z) times 0,1 ^ t with the maximum of the circle distance (circumference one) and the discrete prefix distance. Let pi _t keep the angle and delete the last bit, and take w_t=2^ -t . For an intervention at stage k with amplitude 0<a<1/2 , replace pi _k by prefix deletion and angle shift -a . Set h_t to the identity for t leq k and to angle shift a for t>k . The inverses shift by -a on those same levels. The squares commute at k by cancellation and at every other level by commutation with prefix deletion. Each limit has at least two histories over every finite cut, since a later bit may be flipped. All bonding maps are 1 -Lipschitz and satisfy the fiber estimate with K_t=1 : set the required angle

theorems.label: ex:hausdorff-not-isomorphism
theorems.title: Hausdorff Stability Without a Homeomorphism
theorems.statement: [Hausdorff Stability Without a Homeomorphism] Take S_t= 0, ldots ,2^t-1 with discrete distance scaled by r>0 , w_t=2^ -t , and pi _t(j)= lfloor j/2 rfloor . For t geq 1 , change only the image of j=1 to 1 , keeping widetilde pi _0= pi _0 . Both maps remain surjective and satisfy the fiber estimate with K_t=1 . The weighted intervention cost is r sum _ t geq 1 2^ -t =r . The all-zero history of the perturbed tower is isolated by the cylinder y_1=0 because each subsequent zero has exactly one lift. The original tower is the binary-prefix space and has no isolated histories. Thus the limits are not homeomorphic, even though the Hausdorff bound tends to zero with r . All hypotheses of Lemma~ ref lem:stability hold.

theorems.title: Small Displacement of Coherent Transports
theorems.statement: [Small Displacement of Coherent Transports] For a family of commuting coordinate homeomorphisms, if sup _t w_t sup _ z in S_t d_t(z,h_t(z)) tends to zero, then the induced transports converge uniformly to the inclusion of I in the common history space.

theorems.title: Perturbation Energy
theorems.statement: [Perturbation Energy] For a controlled perturbation process delta E_t we define its weighted energy: E_w( delta E_t ) := sum _ t=0 ^ infty w_t , H_t( delta E_t) where H_t( delta E_t) is a non-negative scalar measuring the entropy or information content injected at time t (e.g., Shannon entropy of stochastic perturbation).

theorems.label: def:ontmass
theorems.title: Sectorial Deformation Resistance
theorems.statement: [Sectorial Deformation Resistance] Fix a common metric history space (Z_ mathrm h ,d_w) and a baseline nonempty closed identity set mathcal I . Compare identity objects in its Hausdorff metric component [ mathfrak C_ mathcal I = J subseteq Z_ mathrm h :J ne varnothing , J text closed , d_H^ Z_ mathrm h ( mathcal I,J)< infty . ] For a declared intervention sector with widetilde mathcal I _ delta in mathfrak C_ mathcal I and cost E_w( delta ) in , define [ M_ Omega = inf _ substack delta text admitted 0<d_H^ Z_ mathrm h ( mathcal I, widetilde mathcal I _ delta )< infty frac E_w( delta ) d_H^ Z_ mathrm h ( mathcal I, widetilde mathcal I _ delta ) , qquad inf varnothing =+ infty . ] Infinite cost divided by a finite positive distance is + infty ; zero deformation is excluded from the ratio. Po

theorems.label: def:internal-external
theorems.title: Internal perturbations and external extensions
theorems.statement: [Internal perturbations and external extensions] Let S be a CCR channel with identity object mathcal I (S) . [leftmargin=*] item textbf Internal perturbations are operators delta in Omega _ mathrm int (S) that act on the identity structure of S : delta maps mathcal I (S) to a deformed identity widetilde mathcal I (S) belonging to the same declared structural class, with finite weighted energy E_w( delta )< infty . Internal perturbations test rigidity of mathcal I (S) under deformation. item textbf External extensions are operations eta in mathrm Ext (S) that produce a different channel S' : eta maps S to S' with D_ mathrm ext (S,S')= epsilon >0 . External extensions compare mathcal I (S) with an independently specified object mathcal I (S') not introduced as an element of Omega _ mathrm in

theorems.label: rem:typed-separation
theorems.title: Interpretation of typed separation
theorems.statement: [Interpretation of typed separation] The typed separation Omega _ mathrm int (S) cap mathrm Ext (S)= varnothing is an axiom, not a theorem derived from CCR membership. A protocol that confuses internal perturbations with external witnesses commits a category error: it uses rigidity under internal deformation, which CCR is meant to constrain, as evidence for a witness-relative comparison that requires a separately specified external extension. QICN has not verified that all downstream perturbation protocols respect this separation.

theorems.title: Relation to Rigidity
theorems.statement: [Relation to Rigidity] Use Definition~ ref def:ontmass , including its common Hausdorff metric component. Suppose all admitted finite-cost interventions satisfy Lemma~ ref lem:stability with one C>0 and D_w leq A E_w with one A>0 . Then M_ Omega geq 1/(CA) . One admitted finite-cost positive deformation implies M_ Omega < infty ; if no such deformation exists, M_ Omega =+ infty .

theorems.label: thm:lml
theorems.title: Finite Resistance Requires an Admitted Deformation Witness
theorems.statement: [Finite Resistance Requires an Admitted Deformation Witness] In a declared common metric space, finite resistance for a candidate of this class is equivalent to the existence of an admitted intervention of finite cost with positive Hausdorff deformation. Finite latent dimension and Lipschitz dynamics alone permit systems without such a witness.

theorems.title: Observable Channel
theorems.statement: [Observable Channel] An observable channel is a triple mathcal C = (E, O, R) , where: [leftmargin=*] item E is the environment (unobserved state space), item O is a measurable output space, item R is a (possibly unknown) response mechanism producing observable outputs O_t in O .

theorems.label: def:channel-projection
theorems.title: Channel--projection composition
theorems.statement: [Channel--projection composition] Let C_ mathrm obs : mathcal U to mathcal O denote the observable map realized by the response mechanism of an observable channel, and let pi _ infty to t : mathcal I to S_t be the canonical finite-level projection from the inverse limit. When a concrete model declares a map iota _t:S_t to mathcal U from finite-level states into the internal state domain, the composed finite-level observable is C_t := C_ mathrm obs circ iota _t circ pi _ infty to t : mathcal I to mathcal O . This composition is the typed route from the identity object mathcal I through a finite projection S_t to observable outputs.

theorems.label: def:obs-equiv
theorems.title: Observable Equivalence
theorems.statement: [Observable Equivalence] Let mathcal H_O be the declared domain of admissible observable histories and mathcal D a nonempty family of finite-cost probes, including sham. For each delta in mathcal D require a specified response map T_ delta : mathcal H_O to mathcal H_O^ delta and reconstruction map J_ delta into nonempty closed identity supports in a common comparison space. Define [ O sim _ mathcal I O' quad Longleftrightarrow quad forall delta in mathcal D, quad d_H(J_ delta (T_ delta O),J_ delta (T_ delta O'))=0. ]

theorems.label: def:emp-mass
theorems.title: Empirical Sectorial Deformation Resistance Estimator
theorems.statement: [Empirical Sectorial Deformation Resistance Estimator] hat M _ Omega := inf _ substack k = 1, ldots , N Delta ^ (k) > 0 frac E_w^ (k) Delta ^ (k) .

theorems.label: thm:detectability
theorems.title: Finite Witnesses for Deformation Resistance
theorems.statement: [Finite Witnesses for Deformation Resistance] Assume the specified intervention sector and common metric of Definition~ ref def:ontmass . For any finite family of interventions of finite cost with exactly known Hausdorff distances, its infimum ratio is an upper bound on M_ Omega . This infimum is finite exactly when the family contains a positive-deformation witness. Moreover M_ Omega <+ infty exactly when the full sector contains such a finite-cost witness. Exhaustion by nested families gives convergence to M_ Omega if their union contains witnesses with ratios arbitrarily close to the sector infimum.

theorems.label: def:phenom-compat
theorems.title: Observable Compatibility Operator
theorems.statement: [Observable Compatibility Operator] Let T_ Phi :( mathcal I,d_w) to (O,d_O) be the declared observable assignment.

theorems.label: def:spectral-constant
theorems.title: Separation Modulus
theorems.statement: [Separation Modulus] For r>0 such that A_r= (x,y) in mathcal I^2:d_w(x,y) ge r is nonempty, define [ omega _T(r)= inf _ (x,y) in A_r d_O(T_ Phi (x),T_ Phi (y)). ] An empty A_r gives no observable separation test at that scale.

theorems.label: thm:spectral-coupling
theorems.title: Positive Separation at a Fixed Scale
theorems.statement: [Positive Separation at a Fixed Scale] If mathcal I is a nonempty compact metric space and T_ Phi is continuous and injective, then omega _T(r)>0 at every scale in its domain. The infimum is attained.

theorems.label: cor:spectral-derivation
theorems.title: Resolution and Coercivity
theorems.statement: [Resolution and Coercivity] If each of two observed values has error at most eta in d_O , then true separation in d_w of at least r gives measured separation at least omega _T(r)-2 eta . A global linear bound requires a positive lower Lipschitz constant c , established or assumed for the stated domain.

theorems.label: rem:scale-vs-linear
theorems.statement: The separation modulus is metric and scale-dependent. No spectral interpretation is required.

theorems.label: prop:causal-rigid
theorems.title: Observational Isolation Does Not Determine Interventional Invariance
theorems.statement: [Observational Isolation Does Not Determine Interventional Invariance] Even beth _q=1 does not determine whether the state law is invariant under interventions on Y . With a structural model X=f(Y,Z) and a fixed exogenous law for Z , the law under mathrm do (Y=y) is the pushforward of that law by f(y, cdot ) . Invariance of these laws on a specified intervention family requires equality of the corresponding pushforwards.

theorems.label: def:coexist
theorems.title: Coexisting Identities
theorems.statement: [Coexisting Identities] Fix a common comparison of admitted identity objects, with the same separating object-deformation metric d_ mathrm Id used in Definition~ ref def:ontmass (Hausdorff distance on the common closed supports), or first quotient zero-distance objects. Histories have a well-defined assignment h mapsto mathcal I(h) . An emph operating channel mathcal C_ alpha is a nonempty class intrinsically connected by finite chains of support-preserving admissible finite-energy perturbations. The connecting moves have certified finite-energy reverses, or one uses mutual finite reachability. Finite concatenations remain admissible with finite total cost bounded by the sum of costs. Equality of observable outputs alone does not imply this connection. Two assigned objects coexist in that

theorems.label: thm:uniqueness
theorems.title: Strong Uniqueness
theorems.statement: [Strong Uniqueness] Within one operating channel of Definition~ ref def:coexist , at most one CCR identity assignment exists up to the declared zero-deformation equivalence, provided the connecting moves belong to that same CCR comparison sector. Two coexisting assignments therefore have d_ mathrm Id ( mathcal I, mathcal J)=0 .

theorems.label: def:atomicity-certificate
theorems.title: Typed product-retraction certificate
theorems.statement: [Typed product-retraction certificate] Fix a system S , a compact identity support I subset Z , its declared resistance sector mathcal D_S , nonnegative intervention cost E_w , and Hausdorff deformation Delta ( delta )=d_H(I,I^ delta ) . A product datum P=(A_P,B_P,F_P) has nonempty compact metric factors of positive diameter and a homeomorphism F_P:I to A_P times B_P preserving the specified observations, dynamics and intervention structure. The admitted family is mathcal A_ rm prod . Its projections are a dependent family [ mathcal R_1(P)= operatorname pr _1 circ F_P:I to A_P, qquad mathcal R_2(P)= operatorname pr _2 circ F_P:I to B_P. ] They are not two maps with a fixed codomain for every possible product. A certificate [ mathrm Cert _ rm atom (S)= ( mathcal A_ rm prod , mathcal R_1, ma

theorems.label: prop:product-clamp-certificate
theorems.title: A Checkable Nonempty Product Certificate
theorems.statement: [A Checkable Nonempty Product Certificate] Suppose the declared product sector uses isometries from I onto products with the maximum metric, with operatorname diam (B_P) ge d_0>0 . Suppose each factor clamp is realized by an admissible compatible intervention of cost at most K . Then the projections above and delta _ rm atom =d_0/2 give a certificate. For a unit square with its coordinate product, a single admissible clamp (x,y) mapsto (x,0) of cost one gives the sharper values delta _ rm atom =K=1 .

theorems.label: lem:cantor-product-obstruction
theorems.title: Cantor Product Obstruction to Unconditional Atomicity
theorems.statement: [Cantor Product Obstruction to Unconditional Atomicity] Let B= 0,1 ^ mathbb N_ >0 with its compact prefix topology and its canonical finite projections. Admit the maps T_c(b)=b mathbin oplus c for c in B , with cost sum _ j ge 1 3^ -j c_j . Every map preserves the full inverse-limit support, so its resistance is infinite. Nevertheless, [ b longmapsto ((b_ 2j-1 )_ j ge 1 ,(b_ 2j )_ j ge 1 ) ] is a homeomorphism onto B times B . Both induced factor sectors also have infinite resistance. The retraction clause of Definition~ ref def:atomicity-certificate fails for this flip sector.

theorems.label: thm:cutpoint-product-atomicity
theorems.title: An Infinite-Dimensional Exact Product Obstruction
theorems.statement: [An Infinite-Dimensional Exact Product Obstruction] Let Q= z in ell ^2:0 le z_j le 2^ -j and [ W=(Q times 0 ) cup ( 0 times Q) subset ell ^2 oplus ell ^2. ] Then W is a compact connected support with infinite affine dimension and is not homeomorphic to a product of two non-singleton compact spaces. This is an exact topological obstruction; it does not assert a positive approximation gap against an unspecified closure of products.

theorems.label: cor:indivisible
theorems.title: Atomicity Conditional on a Factorization-to-Deformation Certificate
theorems.statement: [Atomicity Conditional on a Factorization-to-Deformation Certificate] Assume a verified mathrm Cert _ rm atom (S) in the fixed product-comparison sector of Definition~ ref def:atomicity-certificate . If M_ Omega =+ infty , there is no admitted nontrivial faithful factorization. With a finite uniform cost bound, the stronger quantitative implication is M_ Omega >K_ rm atom / delta _ rm atom Rightarrow mathcal A_ rm prod = varnothing . A statement about all products requires the sector to include every product structure under consideration.

theorems.label: prop:wedge-cartesian-gap
theorems.title: Cartesian Corner Gap
theorems.statement: [Cartesian Corner Gap] For nonempty compact A,B subset H with both diameters at least d_0>0 , [ d_H(W,A times B) ge delta _ rm cart (d_0):= max d_0/2,R/2 >0. ] In the fixed coordinate axes the bound R/2 holds even without the diameter assumption and is attained by (Q/2) times (Q/2) .

theorems.label: thm:wedge-bilipschitz-gap
theorems.title: Bounded-Distortion Wedge Gap
theorems.statement: [Bounded-Distortion Wedge Gap] Let A and B be nonempty compact metric spaces of diameter at least d_0>0 . Give A times B the maximum metric. Suppose an embedding F:A times B to H oplus H satisfies [ c ,d_ infty (p,p') le |F(p)-F(p') | le C ,d_ infty (p,p'), qquad 0<c le C. ] Put [ d_*:= min d_0/2,1/(4C) , qquad delta _W:= frac c^2d_* 2C+4c . ] Then d_H(W,F(A times B)) ge delta _W>0 . Consequently, if a nonempty compact widetilde W satisfies d_H(W, widetilde W)<r_W:= delta _W/2 , its distance from every product in this same (d_0,c,C) sector exceeds delta _W/2 . The factors need not be assumed path connected.

theorems.label: prop:wedge-degenerate-controls
theorems.title: Degenerating-Factor and Unbounded-Distortion Controls
theorems.statement: [Degenerating-Factor and Unbounded-Distortion Controls] There are embedded products arbitrarily close to W in each of these two larger sectors: (i) uniformly bi-Lipschitz embeddings with one factor diameter tending to zero; (ii) factors of uniformly positive diameter with no uniform positive lower Lipschitz constant. Neither control is a Cartesian product in the fixed axes of Proposition~ ref prop:wedge-cartesian-gap .

theorems.label: prop:wedge-energy-regimes
theorems.title: Operational Barrier and Cheap-Damage Contrast
theorems.statement: [Operational Barrier and Cheap-Damage Contrast] On W let D_ s_L,s_R (x,y)=((1-s_L)x,(1-s_R)y) , s_L,s_R in , and s= max s_L,s_R . These maps commute with all finite coordinate cuts and have deformation Delta =sR . In a unit-duration quadratic actuation model their minimum worst-state motion energy is s^2R^2 . Declare two sectors of completed protocols, both including all these maps: a damage sector with this motion energy alone; and a protected sector requiring a completed unlock of energy at least B=1 before any motion. Then [ M_ rm damage =0, qquad M_ rm protected =R+R^ -1 =4/ sqrt 3>2/3. ] The actual damage clamp D_ 0,1 has cost K_ rm atom =1/3 and deformation R ge delta _ rm atom =1/2 , so it enforces M_ rm damage le K_ rm atom / delta _ rm atom =2/3 . The protected sector admits that

theorems.label: cor:nodup
theorems.title: No Distinct Assignment by a Matched Finite-Cost Replication
theorems.statement: [No Distinct Assignment by a Matched Finite-Cost Replication] In the connected comparison of Theorem~ ref thm:uniqueness , an admitted finite-cost replication cannot produce an assignment at positive separating deformation distance. Copying an encoding or creating a different operating component is not excluded by this result.

theorems.label: prop:cardinality
theorems.title: Cardinality Bound
theorems.statement: [Cardinality Bound] The assignment C mapsto is well-defined and its image has cardinality at most | mathfrak C| . It is injective only if different components are separately known to carry different assignment classes.

theorems.title: Category of Minimal Observation
theorems.statement: [Category of Minimal Observation] Let mathbf Obs be the category whose objects are nonempty state spaces S_t and whose morphisms are surjective maps pi _ t+1 to t : S_ t+1 to S_t satisfying the compatibility condition pi _ t+1 to t circ pi _ t+2 to t+1 = pi _ t+2 to t .
mathbf Obs is the minimal category in which persistent observability is definable. No continuity, memory, dynamics, or identity is assumed.

theorems.label: thm:noalt
theorems.title: No--Alternative Representation
theorems.statement: [No--Alternative Representation] Let q_t:J to S_t be coherent: pi _ t+1 to t q_ t+1 =q_t . A faithful complete encoding means joint separation ( q_t(j)=q_t(k) for every t implies j=k ) and exhaustivity (every compatible history equals (q_t(j))_t for some j ). Then Q(j)=(q_t(j))_t is the unique bijection J to mathcal I commuting with cut evaluations. It is a topological isomorphism if J is compact, mathcal I Hausdorff, and all q_t continuous.

theorems.label: thm:collapse
theorems.title: Collapse under Pure Progressive Causality
theorems.statement: [Collapse under Pure Progressive Causality] Suppose f_t:S_t to S_ t+1 satisfies pi _ t+1 to t f_t= mathrm id _ S_t . Set B_0=S_0 , B_ t+1 =f_t(B_t) and restrict histories to x_ t+1 =f_t(x_t) . The restricted bonding map B_ t+1 to B_t is bijective with inverse f_t|_ B_t , and the orbital inverse limit is canonically bijective to S_0 (homeomorphic for continuous maps on compact Hausdorff stages). The original unrestricted limit need not collapse.

theorems.label: def:degeneracy
theorems.title: Projective Degeneracy
theorems.statement: [Projective Degeneracy] The system is projectively degenerate when some canonical evaluation p_T: mathcal I to S_T is bijective: the history is recoverable through that specified cut. Under active surjectivity this is equivalent to bijective bonding maps at every level t ge T . Non-degeneracy means no such canonical evaluation exists. An arbitrary set isomorphism mathcal I cong S_T is not the criterion; the previous unqualified notation failed to enforce this and is explicitly replaced.
Projective degeneracy is the formal characterization of ``collapse to a finite prefix.'' Under non-degeneracy, the compatible history contains information beyond every canonical finite prefix.

theorems.title: Necessity of Retroinduction
theorems.statement: [Necessity of Retroinduction] Breaking purely progressive causality is necessary under the non-degeneracy condition. Minimal retroinduction is structurally required within that model class.

theorems.title: Minimal Projection Operator
theorems.statement: [Minimal Projection Operator] Given an ambient history Psi and a declared metric d , define the set of nearest compatible histories by aleph ( Psi ) := arg min _ Phi in mathcal I d( Phi , Psi ). Existence and uniqueness require the separate conditions below.

theorems.label: def:weighted-metric
theorems.title: Weighted Sum Metric for the Minimization Problem
theorems.statement: [Weighted Sum Metric for the Minimization Problem] leavevmode par Use d( Phi , Psi )= sum _ t geq 0 lambda ^t d_t( phi _t, psi _t) , where 0< lambda <1 and sum _t lambda ^t operatorname diam (S_t)< infty . The diameter sum controls tails uniformly. This is a different metric from the weighted supremum in Definition~ ref def:weighted-sup-metric .

theorems.label: thm:aleph-unique
theorems.title: Existence of Minimizers and Conditional Uniqueness of $\aleph$
theorems.statement: [Existence of Minimizers and Conditional Uniqueness of aleph ] For a nonempty inverse limit of compact metric stages with continuous bonding maps and the diameter-sum condition above, the objective d( Phi , Psi ) attains its minimum over mathcal I for every ambient product point Psi . If mathcal I is convex in a specified real linear ambient space and this objective is strictly convex on mathcal I , the minimizer is unique.

theorems.title: Nearest-Point Selection Is an Extra Requirement
theorems.statement: [Nearest-Point Selection Is an Extra Requirement] A selector from aleph ( Psi ) returns a compatible history when the minimizer set is nonempty. Compatibility of the output alone allows any map into mathcal I and does not force nearest-point selection.

theorems.label: def:causal-closure
theorems.title: Structural Causal Closure
theorems.statement: [Structural Causal Closure] A system is textit structurally causally closed if for every extension E , the inverse limit identity satisfies: varprojlim S_t cong varprojlim S_t^ (E) .

This reformulation of causal closure is purely categorical: it requires invariance of the inverse limit under extensions, without appealing to information-theoretic quantities. This makes the definition operationally precise and independent of Shannon-theoretic assumptions.

theorems.label: thm:info-isolation
theorems.title: Finite-Prefix Recovery and Information
theorems.statement: [Finite-Prefix Recovery and Information] For a canonical projection p_t: mathcal I to S_t , exact recovery of every history from its prefix is possible precisely when p_t is injective, with a decoder defined on its image. If P=p_t(X) is a finite-valued prefix of a random history X under a declared law, then I(P;X)=H(P) .

theorems.label: def:isolation-functor
theorems.title: Normalized Conditional Entropy
theorems.statement: [Normalized Conditional Entropy] For finite-valued (X,Y) with a declared joint law and H(X)>0 , set mathfrak B(X;Y)=H(X mid Y)/H(X) .

theorems.label: lem:isolation-properties
theorems.title: Coarsening and Relabeling
theorems.statement: [Coarsening and Relabeling] For fixed X , replacing Y by a function of Y cannot decrease mathfrak B . Bijective relabelings of the random variables preserve it. It vanishes precisely when X is determined by Y almost surely under the declared law.

theorems.label: rem:law-dependent-isolation
theorems.statement: The normalization is defined only when the chosen law gives positive finite entropy.

theorems.label: def:mir
theorems.title: MIR Geometry
theorems.statement: [MIR Geometry] The textit Manifold of Retroactive Inversion (MIR) is defined as the class of all non-degenerate projective systems in mathbf C admitting a non-trivial inverse limit identity. Formally: text MIR := (S_t, pi _ t+1 to t ) in mathbf Obs :p_T text is not bijective for every T .

This definition avoids ambiguity: ``MIR'' is not a differential manifold in the classical sense, but a textit class of projective systems satisfying non-degeneracy. The term ``geometry'' refers to the compatibility structure imposed by the projective system, not to smooth structure.

theorems.label: thm:nosemigroup
theorems.title: No Semigroup Compatibility
theorems.statement: [No Semigroup Compatibility] If p_0 is noninjective, no compatible deterministic forward family generates all projective histories as its orbital subsystem. Forward semigroups on spaces already storing complete histories are not excluded.

theorems.label: lem:bridge-identity
theorems.title: Structural Coupling: Observable--Identity
theorems.statement: [Structural Coupling: Observable--Identity] Use the connected operating channel and separating comparison of Definition~ ref def:coexist , with CCR for its connecting perturbations. Its observable--identity assignment is unique up to zero deformation by Theorem~ ref thm:uniqueness . For a compatible point-history x , if w_t operatorname diam (S_t) to 0 , every compatible completion x^ [N] agreeing through cut N satisfies [ d_w(x^ [N] ,x) le sup _ t>N w_t operatorname diam (S_t) longrightarrow 0. ] This is prefix reconstruction, not temporal attraction. If additionally a contraction T acts on a nonempty complete metric space of admitted identity candidates, with d(Ta,Tb) le qd(a,b) , 0 le q<1 , it has a unique attracting fixed point. Identification with the channel assignment further requir

theorems.label: cor:identity-forcing
theorems.title: Identity Forcing under CCR
theorems.statement: [Identity Forcing under CCR] In an energy-connected CCR operating channel with a well-defined assignment into the separating comparison, all assigned identities coincide. An attracting realization additionally needs the dynamical hypotheses of Lemma~ ref lem:bridge-identity .

The lemma separates assignment uniqueness, reconstruction and dynamical attraction under distinct hypotheses: [leftmargin=*] item Existence is determined by projective compatibility; item Uniqueness uses CCR and intrinsic channel connection; item Temporal attraction needs the stated contraction; infinite mass alone gives no temporal dynamics. Within the same observable channel and hypotheses, no distinct compatible identity object is available.

theorems.label: def:proj-obs-limit
theorems.title: Projective Observable Limit
theorems.statement: [Projective Observable Limit] For finite nonempty discrete spaces S_t and surjective bonding maps, let mathcal I= varprojlim S_t with the subspace product topology. Let O= varprojlim mathrm Prob (S_t) with pushforward bonding maps and the subspace product topology of the finite probability simplexes.

theorems.label: thm:stone-classification
theorems.title: Topology of Point and Law Limits
theorems.statement: [Topology of Point and Law Limits] The point limit mathcal I is nonempty, compact, metrizable, and has a clopen basis. The law limit O is nonempty, compact, metrizable, and convex under coordinatewise mixing. If O contains distinct points, it is path connected and is not a Stone space.

theorems.label: cor:obs-morphism
theorems.title: Embedding by Compatible Dirac Measures
theorems.statement: [Embedding by Compatible Dirac Measures] The map x mapsto ( delta _ x_t )_t embeds mathcal I homeomorphically as a closed subspace of O .

theorems.label: rem:point-vs-law-topology
theorems.statement: The Dirac image carries the topology of histories of points; mixtures belong to the law limit.

theorems.label: ex:minimal-ccr
theorems.title: Canonical Minimal CCR
theorems.statement: [Canonical Minimal CCR] Let S_t=[0,1] times 0,1 ^t , with d_t((u,a),(v,b))= max |u-v|, mathbf 1_ a ne b , w_t=2^ -t , and bonding maps deleting the last bit while retaining u . Its actual coordinate cone identifies [ mathcal I cong times 0,1 ^ mathbb N_ >0 . ] Declare an internal sector of coherent bit-flip automorphisms: for A subseteq mathbb N_ >0 , h_t flips A cap 1, ldots ,t , at the declared dimensionless cost E(A)= sum _ j in A 2^ -j , using the stage-injection costs H_j(A)= mathbf 1_ j in A for j ge 1 and H_0=0 . These homeomorphisms commute with deletion. Operating channels for point preparations may fix u and use the mutually reversible bit-flip moves.

theorems.title: Minimal CCR is Non-Degenerate and Rigid
theorems.statement: [Minimal CCR is Non-Degenerate and Rigid] The example has compact stages, summable weighted diameter tails, two-point fibres at each bonding map and 2^t prefixes over each initial u . Every p_T is noninjective. Its identity-support mass is M_ Omega =+ infty in the specified internal sector.

The former identity-link example was canonically degenerate, so its non-degeneracy claim was false. This replacement is genuinely ramified, although every stage and its limit still have continuum cardinality. Rigidity is conditional on the declared support-preserving sector, not implied by branching. Finite-cost changes of the whole support can give finite mass, as Example~ ref ex:coherent-rotation-tower shows. No immunity to every perturbation, nor minimality among all realizations, follows.

theorems.label: ex:symbolic-ccr
theorems.title: Symbolic CCR System
theorems.statement: [Symbolic CCR System] Let: [leftmargin=*] item S_t = 0, 1 ^ mathbb N , endowed with the product topology and the metric d_t(x, y) = sum _ k=1 ^ infty 2^ -k |x_k - y_k|. item Define the projections pi _ t+1 to t as the left shift operator: pi _ t+1 to t (x_1 x_2 x_3 ldots ) = (x_2 x_3 x_4 ldots ). This is a projectively non-degenerate inverse system. Infinite mass is asserted only in a separately declared coherent support-preserving sector, not against all perturbations.

This example connects the framework to: [leftmargin=*] item Symbolic dynamics and subshifts; item Automata theory and formal languages; item Profinite structures in algebra. The existence of CCR systems is therefore universal across mathematical disciplines.

theorems.label: thm:non-simulability
theorems.title: Conditional Non-Simulability from a Finite-Cost Witness
theorems.statement: [Conditional Non-Simulability from a Finite-Cost Witness] For any candidate simulator with a declared intervention sector and common comparison metric, suppose there is an admissible finite-cost intervention producing positive Hausdorff deformation. Then M_ Omega <+ infty in that sector. It cannot faithfully realize an infinite-resistance target if faithfulness is required to preserve the resistance class.

theorems.label: thm:non-transferability
theorems.title: Resistance under Audited Transport
theorems.statement: [Resistance under Audited Transport] leavevmode par Let an ambient bijection A satisfy c ,d(x,y) leq d'(Ax,Ay) leq C ,d(x,y) with 0<c leq C< infty . It maps the baseline identity to the target identity. Suppose a bijection between the declared intervention sectors maps delta to delta ' with A(I_ delta )=I'_ delta ' and a E( delta ) leq E'( delta ') leq b E( delta ) for 0<a leq b< infty . For nonempty baseline and deformed sets at finite Hausdorff distance, the two resistance values satisfy [ frac a C M_ Omega leq M'_ Omega leq frac b c M_ Omega . ] In particular such a transport preserves the finite versus infinite resistance class.

theorems.label: lem:canonical-closure
theorems.title: Closure under Composed Sector Comparisons
theorems.statement: [Closure under Composed Sector Comparisons] Two consecutive transports satisfying Theorem~ ref thm:non-transferability compose to a transport of the same kind. If both also intertwine the specified readouts exactly, their composition does so.

theorems.title: Rigidity Degree
theorems.statement: [Rigidity Degree] For a projective system (S_t, pi _ t+1 to t ) , define the rigidity degree rho in [0, infty ] as: rho := sup left r geq 0 ; Big | ; forall epsilon _t : | epsilon _t |_w < r implies d_H^ Z_ mathrm h ( mathcal I , tilde mathcal I ) = 0 right .

theorems.label: thm:stratification
theorems.title: Stratification Theorem
theorems.statement: [Stratification Theorem] The class of observable channels admits a stratification by rigidity degree: mathcal U = mathcal U _0 sqcup mathcal U _ (0, infty ) sqcup mathcal U _ infty , where: [leftmargin=*] item mathcal U _0 : channels with rho = 0 (zero rigidity, fully deformable); item mathcal U _ (0, infty ) : channels with 0 < rho < infty (partial rigidity); item mathcal U _ infty : channels with rho = infty (CCR rigidity).

theorems.title: Deformation Spectrum
theorems.statement: [Deformation Spectrum] For a perturbation family epsilon _t , define the deformation spectrum as the sequence: sigma ( epsilon _t ) := left ( | epsilon _0 |_ text op , | epsilon _1 |_ text op , | epsilon _2 |_ text op , ldots right ).

theorems.title: Weighted Polynomial Decay Condition
theorems.statement: [Weighted Polynomial Decay Condition] Let w_n le K n^p and | epsilon _n |_ rm op le C n^ - alpha for n ge 1 , with K,C>0 , p ge 0 , and a finite term at zero. If alpha >p+1 , then sum _n w_n | epsilon _n |_ rm op < infty .

theorems.title: Projective Completeness
theorems.statement: [Projective Completeness] A projective system (S_t, pi _ t+1 to t ) is textit projectively complete if for every Cauchy sequence (x^ (n) )_ n in mathbb N in ( mathcal I , d_w) , the limit exists in mathcal I .

theorems.label: thm:completeness
theorems.title: Completeness Inheritance
theorems.statement: [Completeness Inheritance] If the coordinate spaces are complete and the bonding maps continuous, every finite-distance component of ( mathcal I,d_w) is complete. Under the full-product finiteness condition of Proposition~ ref prop:weighted-history , this gives completeness on all of mathcal I .

theorems.title: Universal Property of Identity
theorems.statement: [Universal Property of Identity] For the declared tower of sets, every coherent family phi _t:J to S_t induces a unique map psi :J to mathcal I= varprojlim S_t with p_t psi = phi _t . For a tower of topological spaces with its product-subspace limit topology, continuous phi _t induce the unique continuous such map.

theorems.title: Invariance in the Declared Finite-Cost Sector
theorems.statement: [Invariance in the Declared Finite-Cost Sector] Suppose a structural model associates to each intervention an identity object in a common metric comparison space and a cost in the sector of Definition~ ref def:ontmass . If M_ Omega =+ infty , each intervention in that sector of finite cost has zero Hausdorff deformation. If the compared objects are closed, they are equal as subsets of the comparison space.

theorems.title: Complexity Lower Bound for CCR Simulation
theorems.statement: [Complexity Lower Bound for CCR Simulation] Suppose a deterministic code of B bits must recover any requested prefix of a binary history through horizon t . Exact prefix recovery requires B geq t . For complete decoded histories in the prefix metric d(x,y)=2^ -m at first differing position m geq 1 , the optimal uniform error is 2^ -(B+1) .

theorems.title: Impossibility of Perfect Simulation
theorems.statement: [Impossibility of Perfect Simulation] A fixed finite binary budget cannot recover every prefix on the binary-prefix target.

theorems.title: External adjudication object
theorems.statement: [External adjudication object] An external adjudication object is the tuple mathfrak E =(P,D_h,D_m,C_n,C_a, Sigma , mathcal R , mathcal A ), where P is a frozen preregistered protocol, D_h and D_m are human and machine trace datasets in mathcal T , C_n and C_a are negative and active control families, Sigma = sigma _k _ k=1 ^K is a finite family of predeclared measurable statistics sigma _k: mathcal T ^n to mathbb R , mathcal R is the reviewer layer, and mathcal A : mathcal Y to 0,1, mathtt undetermined is the final adjudicator operator on masked evidence summaries mathcal Y .

theorems.title: Admissible comparative evidence
theorems.statement: [Admissible comparative evidence] A dataset pair (D_h,D_m) is admissible under mathfrak E only if the following predicates are all true: item D_h,D_m are measurable finite samples from ( mathcal T , mathcal B ( mathcal T )) . item The preregistered protocol hash, control manifest hash, and analysis shell hash match their frozen records. item Human-side records are not generated, rewritten, or completed by synthetic systems: epsilon _ mathrm syn =0 for the human channel. item Blinding leakage is bounded by the preregistered budget: mathbb P ( mathrm leak ) leq epsilon _ mathrm blind . item Every declared negative control has an executed and timestamped outcome under the same admissibility grammar.

theorems.title: Non-transitivity of internal support
theorems.statement: [Non-transitivity of internal support] Let mathcal G _ mathrm internal in denote any internal runtime support score computed from operational invariants, and let mathcal G _ mathrm external in 0,1, mathtt undetermined denote the external adjudication verdict. In the absence of an admissible measurable dataset pair (D_h,D_m) , one has mathcal G _ mathrm internal centernot implies mathcal G _ mathrm external .

theorems.title: Operational closure of a comparative program
theorems.statement: [Operational closure of a comparative program] The comparative program reaches operational closure only when there exists a predeclared alignment map T: mathcal T to mathcal Z into a common Polish feature space ( mathcal Z ,d_ mathcal Z ) and the total divergence Delta _ mathrm comp = lambda _1 W_1(T_ # widehat mu _h,T_ # widehat mu _m) + lambda _2 D_ mathrm KL ( widehat p _h Vert widehat p _m) + lambda _3 max _k | sigma _k(D_h)- sigma _k(D_m)| is defined and satisfies the frozen budget Delta _ mathrm comp leq epsilon _ mathrm budget . This closure is a precondition for comparative interpretation, not a claim of consciousness, identity, or substrate equivalence.

theorems.title: Cryptographic freeze map
theorems.statement: [Cryptographic freeze map] Let mathcal P _ mathrm config be the set of canonical preregistration configurations after deterministic serialization. A freeze map is a collision-resistant hash function H: mathcal P _ mathrm config to 0,1 ^ 256 . A preregistration record p is locally frozen at digest h when H(p)=h , h is written into the lock manifest, and every amendment policy references h rather than an editable natural-language description.

theorems.title: Hash-anchored non-alterability
theorems.statement: [Hash-anchored non-alterability] Assume the hash function H is collision resistant over the canonical serialization domain. If a post-execution preregistration configuration p' has the same published digest as the frozen pre-execution configuration p , then either p'=p byte-for-byte under canonical serialization or a collision for H has been found.

theorems.title: Homologous channel statistic
theorems.statement: [Homologous channel statistic] For each channel c , let T_c: mathcal T to mathcal Z _c be a frozen feature map into a metric standard Borel space ( mathcal Z _c,d_c) . Given human and machine samples D_h^c,D_m^c , define empirical pushforward measures [ widehat mu _h^c=(T_c)_ # D_h^c, qquad widehat mu _m^c=(T_c)_ # D_m^c. ] The channel is statistically comparable only if both empirical measures are defined, the feature map was frozen before execution, and the channel-specific missingness policy accepts both samples.

theorems.title: Divergence shell
theorems.statement: [Divergence shell] The predeclared divergence shell for channel c is Delta _c = alpha _c W_1( widehat mu _h^c, widehat mu _m^c) + beta _c D_ mathrm KL ( widehat p _h^c Vert widehat p _m^c) + gamma _c | widehat s _h^c- widehat s _m^c |_1, where W_1 is the Kantorovich--Rubinstein Wasserstein-1 distance, D_ mathrm KL is the Kullback--Leibler divergence on a frozen finite partition or smoothed density model, and widehat s _h^c, widehat s _m^c are predeclared summary vectors. The weights alpha _c, beta _c, gamma _c geq 0 must be frozen before execution.

theorems.title: Comparator homologation is conditional
theorems.statement: [Comparator homologation is conditional] A human--machine channel pair is homologated by Paper 10 only if every term in Delta _c is defined and the frozen channel budget Delta _c leq epsilon _c is satisfied. Homologation is therefore a statistical transport condition over predeclared observables, not a statement that the channels share a biological, phenomenal, or metaphysical substrate.

theorems.title: Blind adjudicator loss
theorems.statement: [Blind adjudicator loss] For a(Y) in h,m, mathtt tie and a declared gamma in , put [ L_ gamma (a(Y), ell )= bf 1 a(Y) ne ell , a(Y) ne mathtt tie + gamma bf 1 a(Y)= mathtt tie . ] Report R_ gamma = mathbb E L_ gamma , coverage C= Pr (a(Y) ne mathtt tie ) , and error conditional on coverage when C>0 . For acceptance require a preregistered C ge C_ min >0 . Forced choice has C=1 ; always abstaining has C=0 and R_ gamma = gamma .

theorems.label: thm:null-forced
theorems.title: Null error lower bound
theorems.statement: [Null error lower bound] Let E denote leakage and p= Pr (E) . If in the clean stratum ell is balanced conditional on Y,E^c , then [ R_ gamma (a) ge (1-p)/2. ] Alternatively, suppose Y is coupled to a clean bundle Y_0 for which ell is balanced conditional on Y_0 , and Y=Y_0 outside an event of probability at most p . Then [ R_ gamma (a) ge max 0,1/2-p . ] The assumptions are distinct. Under the first, revealing the label on a leak event independent of the balanced label can attain the bound with forced choice.

theorems.title: Alternative detectability criterion
theorems.statement: [Alternative detectability criterion] Evidence for distinguishability under H_1 requires a preregistered rule a^ star , minimum coverage C_ min >0 , a justified null bound B_0 accounting for the leakage budget, and margin eta >0 . On admissible held-out bundles require C ge C_ min and R_ gamma (a^ star ) le B_0- eta after sampling uncertainty and multiple-comparison corrections. Forced-choice, balanced label permutations, always abstaining and known-leak controls are evaluated under the same loss and coverage protocol. The manuscript reports no campaign satisfying this criterion.

theorems.label: thm:coverage-sensitive-leakage
theorems.title: Sharp Leakage Bounds at Fixed Coverage
theorems.statement: [Sharp Leakage Bounds at Fixed Coverage] Writing z_+= max 0,z , the clean-stratum and coupling nulls of Theorem~ ref thm:null-forced respectively give [ B_ rm clean (C,p)= gamma (1-C)+ tfrac 12(C-p)_+, qquad B_ rm coup (C,p)= gamma (1-C)+(C/2-p)_+ . ] Both are sharp for each C,p in , with balanced marginal labels and leak probability at most p , including selective abstention. Minimizing over coverage gives the bounds of Theorem~ ref thm:null-forced .

theorems.label: thm:independent-block-risk-intervals
theorems.title: Independent-Block Risk and Coverage Inference
theorems.statement: [Independent-Block Risk and Coverage Inference] Let M count covered decisions and K count wrong covered decisions among n independent blocks. Then [ M sim operatorname Bin (n,C), qquad K mid M sim operatorname Bin (M,e), qquad e= Pr (W=1 mid B=1) quad (C>0). ] With I_C=I_ alpha _C (M,n) and I_e=I_ alpha _e (K,M) , simultaneous coverage is at least 1- alpha _C- alpha _e .
