theorems.label: prop:bilipschitz-rotation-spiral-control
theorems.title: Exact Bi-Lipschitz and Smooth Approximation Controls
theorems.statement: [Exact Bi-Lipschitz and Smooth Approximation Controls] For every 0< rho <1 and angle theta , there is a compact invariant support containing the unit disk on which F(z)= rho e^ i theta z has an exact autonomous product under a bi-Lipschitz chart. On this same support, smooth product charts of uniformly bounded bi-Lipschitz constants achieve arbitrarily small uniform history error over every horizon. When sin theta =0 , the rotation-dilation also admits an exact smooth coordinate product on the ordinary square.

theorems.label: thm:circle-prefix-integration-obstruction
theorems.title: Exact Split at the Initial Projective Cut
theorems.statement: [Exact Split at the Initial Projective Cut] On each circle-prefix tower, every continuous branch-preserving evolution that descends to depth zero factors into phase and binary dynamics. If the evolutions on both towers commute with the existing transport, the split extends to Z . The original dissipative family and the declared phase rotations, jump transport and split readouts then admit a structural comparator with zero error. Consequently no support certificate on this full Z can contain all six witnesses for the original dynamics and this sector.

theorems.label: thm:circle-prefix-cofinal-margin
theorems.title: Positive Split-Readout Margin on the Cofinal Tower
theorems.statement: [Positive Split-Readout Margin on the Cofinal Tower] Keep Z and the same three readout channels. Enlarge the control by q in -1,0,1 and fix 0< lambda le 1/9 . On branch s set [ Psi _ u,q (s, theta ,b)=(s,u+q lambda b_1,R(b)). ] These maps descend to all stages t ge 1 and commute with the jump transport, with the same inverse-limit support and the same E1--E2 readout. Each branch is forward invariant and each fixed-control map has sharp contraction factor 1/3 there. The sector of product encodings and split-readout approximants just declared is nonempty. Its infimal error e_ ast satisfies [ frac beta lambda 2 le e_ ast le frac lambda 2 . ] For comparators reproducing all three channels exactly at time zero, the infimal error is exactly lambda /2 . At lambda =0 the original exact comparator

theorems.label: thm:paired-integration-rupture
theorems.title: Sharp Paired Detection of Integration Loss
theorems.statement: [Sharp Paired Detection of Integration Loss] If eta <L/2 , the rule D>L detects the coupled case for every prepared state with b_1=1 and every allowed error. It rejects the uncoupled case and the sham with b_1=0 . The score has clearance at least L-2 eta from the threshold. With b_1=1 this distinguishes a zero comparator margin from a margin at least beta L/2 in the declared sector. If eta ge L/2 , there is no rule of the paired observations with a uniform guarantee over these two hypotheses, even if both phase channels and the ternary channel are recorded.

theorems.label: thm:tower-identity-observation-resolution
theorems.title: Sharp Single-Readout Resolution of Tower Identity
theorems.statement: [Sharp Single-Readout Resolution of Tower Identity] In the common history metric and the common readout metric, respectively, [ d_H(I_a,I_ a' )=d_H(F(I_a),F(I_ a' )) = frac beta 1+ beta rho (a,a'). ] Here F is the same early-phase, late-phase and ternary readout applied to every branch in the comparison. Two specified alternatives can be distinguished uniformly from a single observation with error at most eta if and only if [ rho (a,a')>2(1+ beta ^ -1 ) eta . ] A decoder can use the measured phase difference z=y_1-y_0 and retain every alternative within circle distance (1+ beta ^ -1 ) eta of z . For a separated family it returns the unique compatible alternative. A continuous interval of jumps has zero uniform deformation gap over distinct alternatives.

theorems.label: thm:addressable-identity-alternatives
theorems.title: Identity Separation from an Addressable Control Interface
theorems.statement: [Identity Separation from an Addressable Control Interface] For two candidate profiles p,p' write d_t=p_t-p'_t . Their branch sets have exact Hausdorff distance, both in the common history space and in the calibrated readout space, [ D(p,p')= max _ 0 le i,j le K+1 frac w_iw_j w_i+w_j |d_i-d_j|. ] The family of distinct candidates has minimum separation [ g= frac 1 M(3^ K+1 +1) . ] Uniform identification from one observation with unknown initial phase and adversarial error at most eta is possible for the entire family exactly when 2 eta <g . The measurement can return the set of compatible profiles and give a unique label only when that set is a singleton. Allowing continuous amplitudes or unbounded jump addresses removes the uniform gap. Omitting intermediate phase observations can make di

theorems.label: prop:circle-prefix-rupture-controls
theorems.title: Rupture Controls on the Declared Circle-Prefix Model
theorems.statement: [Rupture Controls on the Declared Circle-Prefix Model] Use the same two-branch reference support and the control family of Theorem~ ref thm:circle-prefix-cofinal-margin . Each of the following changes gives the specified witness loss under its declared protocol. The changes need not preserve all five other witnesses.

theorems.label: thm:integration-all-identity-channels
theorems.title: Integration with All Identity Channels
theorems.statement: [Integration with All Identity Channels] For 0< lambda le 1/9 , the split-readout sector on Z_ mathcal P is nonempty, and its infimal history error is bounded by [ frac w_ K+1 lambda 2 le e_ ast le frac lambda 2 . ] The infimum is exactly lambda /2 in the subsector with all time-zero readouts exact. At lambda =0 there is an exact comparator in both sectors. The bounds cover every nonempty partition of the specified scalar and circle channels.

theorems.label: prop:common-support-sham-obstruction
theorems.title: Common Support and the Obstruction to Stable State Labels
theorems.statement: [Common Support and the Obstruction to Stable State Labels] The support Z_ mathcal P provides the persistence, catalogue-relative identity, split-sector integration, discrete-time continuity and non-null differentiation witnesses below. Consider a legibility protocol assigning each state a label by decoding a fixed finite observation window under a repeated sham (u_0,0) . Suppose the label is robust to uniform observation noise of some positive radius, and invariant under advancing the sham by one step for every admissible starting state. Then the label is constant on each branch. No branch-preserving internal control can produce a shift in such a label. A target population requiring such a shift cannot meet L4 in this protocol.

theorems.label: def:matched-paired-response-window
theorems.title: Matched Paired Response Window
theorems.statement: [Matched Paired Response Window] On the common support Z_ mathcal P , a paired response window is the ordered pair of time-zero and time-one readout histories of two copies prepared from the same (p, theta ,b) with a common input u and coupling lambda . The two arms have fixed signs q=+1 and q=-1 . The metric is the maximum of the four-channel readout distances over both arms and both times. Use the distance D= rho (y_+,y_-) between the two observed time-one r_0 coordinates. The decoder returns low for D le L/2 , high for D ge 3L/2 , and abstains otherwise. Here L=1/12 turns. Preparation, command matching and arm order are guaranteed by the protocol. The decoder uses no hidden state or coupling parameter.

theorems.label: thm:matched-integration-legibility
theorems.title: Legibility of Matched Integration Responses
theorems.statement: [Legibility of Matched Integration Responses] Use the windows of Definition~ ref def:matched-paired-response-window with lambda in 0 cup and adversarial observation error at most eta =1/256 in the paired metric. The following are the L1--L6 properties of Definition~ ref def:ileg evaluated on the paired-response domain. [leftmargin=1.5em] item The clean high and low response sets have separation exactly L . item All observations in the allowed noise balls preserve the clean class, with zero abstentions. item For any train of at least three freshly reset pairs at a fixed coupling and fixed prepared first bit, the class persists when the common input phase varies across pairs. item In the nonempty target population, retain the same state and common input, prepare b_1=1 , and ablate lambda in

theorems.label: prop:writable-prefix-preservation
theorems.title: Projective Prefix Writes Preserve Identity and Integration
theorems.statement: [Projective Prefix Writes Preserve Identity and Integration] Each tape update commutes with prefix truncation at every positive depth. The full update is compatible on the cofinal system of depths at least seven. The safe support is invariant and the branch contraction factor is at most 9/16 under common commands in the phase-code-memory metric of Paper VI. Catalogue separation is 1/80 . In the four-channel split sector, [ frac 1 216 le e_ ast le frac 1 24 , ] with infimum 1/24 when all initial readouts are exact.

theorems.label: prop:writable-tower-trajectory-legibility
theorems.title: Finite Legibility on One Tower Trajectory
theorems.statement: [Finite Legibility on One Tower Trajectory] On this support use the binary decoder that reports whether the first ten tape digits contain a deviation from b^ star . It has clean code separation 3^ -10 and is correct at error at most 3^ -10 /4 . From a preparation with b=b^ star , any of the five opposite writes in J changes the label. The post-target label persists through three more native sham steps on the same trajectory. The matched sham has zero false shifts. One bit preserves the two classes exactly.

theorems.label: prop:writable-tower-legibility-horizon
theorems.title: Sharp Time Horizons for a Single Prefix Lesion
theorems.statement: [Sharp Time Horizons for a Single Prefix Lesion] Let t=0 be the observation just after an opposite write at j in 3, ldots ,7 from the alternating preparation, and then apply only native neutral shams without writes or probes. Against the matched unlesioned preparation, the scalar code gap at t is D_ j,t =2 ,3^ -(j+t) , with all other observed coordinates identical. For depth N ge j , the decoder of the first N digits keeps the target label exactly at times 0 le t le N-j on clean data and under code error at most 3^ -N /4 . The clean gap is at least the resolution 3^ -N exactly on this same interval. For the two specified preparations, classification from a single observation at time t is uniformly possible under code errors bounded by eta per observation exactly when 3^ -(j+t) > eta . In p

theorems.label: def:icont
theorems.title: Operational continuity and fragmentation bound
theorems.statement: [Operational continuity and fragmentation bound] An admissible system S satisfies operational continuity, written Icont (S)=1 , if there exists a complete metric space ( mathcal E _S,d_ mathcal E ) and an admissible assignment [ Pi _S : Aset to mathcal E _S ] such that: [leftmargin=1.5em] item for every admissible intervention schedule u_ bullet , the induced path t mapsto Pi _S(x_t) is continuous on admissible windows; item there exists delta _ mathrm cont (S) > 0 for which the fragmentation functional [ F_ S,T (x;u_ bullet ) = sup _ 0 le t < T d_ mathcal E bigl ( Pi _S(x_t), Pi _S(x_ t+1 ) bigr ) ] stays below delta _ mathrm cont (S) on all admissible histories; item no admissible finite-energy perturbation produces a discontinuous jump into an incompatible regime class while Id _S is pr

theorems.label: def:idiff
theorems.title: Non-null differentiation and differentiation gap
theorems.statement: [Non-null differentiation and differentiation gap] An admissible system S satisfies non-null differentiation, written Idiff (S)=1 , if there exist x,y in Aset , a horizon T , and a readout subfamily Read ^ star subseteq R such that [ dist bigl (h_ S,T (x;u_ bullet ), h_ S,T (y;u_ bullet ) bigr ) ge delta _ mathrm diff (S) > 0 ] for some admissible schedule u_ bullet , and if the null operational class nullclass is not an asymptotically stable admissible attractor.

theorems.label: def:decoder
theorems.title: Decoder family and structural closure
theorems.statement: [Decoder family and structural closure] A decoder family Dec _S for S is a family of maps from admissible readout windows h_ S,T (x;u_ bullet ) to a declared class set Class _S , indexed by admissible horizons and intervention schedules. The family is emph structurally closed when all its members use the same class set, class equality composes exactly, and the induced intervention-response cells are transitive under the certified matching relation. Definition~ ref def:ileg below adds the operational clauses required before such a structurally closed family counts as certified for legibility.

theorems.label: def:ileg
theorems.title: Operational legibility and legibility margin
theorems.statement: [Operational legibility and legibility margin] An admissible system S satisfies operational legibility, written Ileg (S)=1 , if there exist: [leftmargin=1.5em] item a certified readout subfamily Read ^ mathrm leg subseteq R ; item a certified decoder family Dec _S acting on windows of length at least tau _ min (S) ; item a class set Class _S ; item a measurement protocol with separation sigma >0 , readout noise radius r>0 , minimum duration tau _ min ge 1 , miss and false-positive budgets p_ mathrm miss ,p_ mathrm fp in item Distinct declared classes have distance at least sigma in the specified clean comparison domain. item On the specified noise domain, perturbations with readout norm at most r preserve the label. item Under declared sham schedules, labels remain stable throughout every

theorems.label: prop:necessity
theorems.title: Each invariant is individually necessary
theorems.statement: [Each invariant is individually necessary] If any one of Iper , allowbreak Iri , allowbreak Iint , allowbreak Icont , allowbreak Idiff , allowbreak Ileg fails, then S notin Cop .

theorems.label: def:indist
theorems.title: Operational indistinguishability
theorems.statement: [Operational indistinguishability] For x,y in Aset , write x sim _ Q,S y if, for every certified decoder D in Dec _S , every admissible horizon T ge tau _ min (S) , and every admissible intervention schedule u_ bullet , [ D bigl (h_ S,T (x;u_ bullet ) bigr )=D bigl (h_ S,T (y;u_ bullet ) bigr ), ] and the intervention response of the two histories remains matched within the legibility margin.

theorems.label: prop:qop-welldefined
theorems.title: Well-definedness of certified response classes
theorems.statement: [Well-definedness of certified response classes] If Iper (S)= Iri (S)= Icont (S)= Idiff (S)= Ileg (S)=1 , then sim _ Q,S is an equivalence relation on Aset .

theorems.label: def:qop
theorems.title: Certified response classes
theorems.statement: [Certified response classes] Assume Proposition~ ref prop:qop-welldefined . The certified response classes of S are the quotient classes [ Qop (S) = Aset / sim _ Q,S . ] An individual class [x]_ sim _ Q,S in Qop (S) is called an certified response classes class of S .

theorems.label: def:cop
theorems.title: Six-predicate operational criterion class membership
theorems.statement: [Six-predicate operational criterion class membership] An admissible system S belongs to Cop , written S in Cop , if there exists a non-empty admissible support Aset such that [ Iper (S)= Iri (S)= Iint (S)= Icont (S)= Idiff (S)= Ileg (S)=1. ]

theorems.label: rem:subdet
theorems.title: Subdetermination of membership
theorems.statement: [Subdetermination of membership] Membership in Cop depends on auxiliary choices: the decoder family Dec , the compression map, and the identity object Id . The paper does not prove that these choices are canonically determined by the system tuple S alone. Different auxiliary choices may yield different membership verdicts for the same system.

theorems.title: Minimality of the criterion
theorems.statement: [Minimality of the criterion] The criterion is conjunctive. No proper subset of the six invariants is taken as sufficient in this paper. This is intentional: weaker criteria collapse either into mere persistence, mere integration, or mere complexity claims, all of which are shown to be insufficient.

theorems.label: def:eqdatum
theorems.title: Structural equivalence datum
theorems.statement: [Structural equivalence datum] A structural datum ( chi , upsilon , rho ) consists of a bi-Lipschitz bijection of the declared state supports, extended to the admissible comparison neighborhoods whenever attraction is tested; a bijection of admissible interventions and their schedules; and bijections of readout indices and values. The latter include calibrated value metrics and class-label renamings. Time indices and protocol horizons are not reparameterized. All data have inverse correspondences on their comparison domains.

theorems.label: def:equiv
theorems.title: Exact and approximate structural equivalence
theorems.statement: [Exact and approximate structural equivalence] Write S_1 simeq _ ( Gamma , eps ) S_2 if a structural datum satisfies the following primitive-data conditions, with eps ge 0 : [leftmargin=1.5em] item textbf Geometric calibration. Supports, admissibility regions, designated collapse/null data, and the neighborhoods used for attraction correspond under chi . State/readout comparison metrics and protocol losses are transported pullbacks, so their calibrated comparisons are isometric. Displayed coordinate metrics need not be isometric: conversion to the common chart has finite inverse Lipschitz constants L_ chi ^ -1 ,L_ rho ^ -1 , equal to one in the normalized case. Unadjusted numerical thresholds in different units are not matched data. item textbf Dynamic intertwining. For all declared initia

theorems.label: def:transport-calibration
theorems.title: Calibrated presentation radius
theorems.statement: [Calibrated presentation radius] Fix the structural geometry and protocol/sector catalogues of Definition~ ref def:equiv . Express both systems on the same coordinate domains. A presentation z records its primitive one-step transition maps and instantaneous readout maps on the entire declared state/control domains, including the neighborhoods needed for attraction. On the finite-distance component use their maximum uniform metric d_ mathcal P in common calibrated units. No invariant score enters this metric. Global failure sets below use the original all-time predicates. Finite sampled histories alone do not bound this full operator metric or certify a positive global radius. For each of the original six predicates, let B_j be its failure set in this fixed presentation class, including und

theorems.label: def:rupture
theorems.title: Rupture
theorems.statement: [Rupture] Given S , a rupture is any loss of admissibility or loss of at least one critical invariant margin beyond its admissible threshold. Ruptures are classified as: [leftmargin=1.5em] item textbf persistence rupture (support loss or collapse exposure), item textbf identity rupture (loss of unique rigid identity), item textbf integration rupture (reducible factorization), item textbf continuity rupture (fragmentation into incompatible classes), item textbf differentiation rupture (null or trivial collapse), item textbf legibility rupture (decoder, noise, or negative-control failure).

theorems.label: lem:support-transfer
theorems.title: Support transfer under exact equivalence
theorems.statement: [Support transfer under exact equivalence] An exact structural equivalence transports a nonempty compact admissible support A_1 to an admissible support A_2= chi (A_1) on the specified comparison domain.

theorems.label: lem:decoder-transport
theorems.title: Decoder transport
theorems.statement: [Decoder transport] For exact equivalence, let H be the componentwise calibrated readout-window bijection and kappa its class-label bijection. The transported algorithm is D_2= kappa circ D_1 circ H^ -1 on the declared clean and noisy observation domains. It is certified whenever D_1 is, and every target decoder arises by inverse transport.

theorems.label: prop:transport
theorems.title: Operational classes are closed under exact transport
theorems.statement: [Operational classes are closed under exact transport] Under exact structural equivalence, [ x sim _ Q,S_1 y quad Longleftrightarrow quad chi x sim _ Q,S_2 chi y. ] Consequently [x] mapsto is a bijection of the operational quotients whenever those quotients are defined.

theorems.label: prop:margins
theorems.title: Approximate margin preservation
theorems.statement: [Approximate margin preservation] Use the common presentation metric and fixed sectors of Definition~ ref def:transport-calibration . If S_1 simeq _ ( Gamma , eps ) S_2 , then [ | delta _j^ mathrm cal (S_1)- delta _j^ mathrm cal (S_2)| le C_ chi , rho eps , quad C_ chi , rho = max 1,L_ chi ^ -1 ,L_ rho ^ -1 . ] The normalized isometric case has C_ chi , rho =1 . Hence delta _ star ^ mathrm cal (S_2) ge delta _ star ^ mathrm cal (S_1)-C_ chi , rho eps . At exact equivalence all six predicates, their calibrated radii, and the operational indistinguishability relation are preserved. Optimal raw margins defined by corresponding infima/suprema of isometric losses are also equal; arbitrary chosen certificate values need not be.

theorems.label: rem:sector-nontransfer
theorems.title: No automatic transfer without the sector
theorems.statement: [No automatic transfer without the sector] Conjugacy of an internal plant alone does not transport a rival-relative margin. For example, a constant-zero target has optimal error one against the sole constant-one rival, but error zero when a constant-zero rival is added, even though the plant and readout are unchanged. This is the no-automatic-transfer boundary of Paper III and the later bridge analysis. Clause4 of Definition~ ref def:equiv requires the corresponding rival sector, costs and loss calibration, not its verdict. Finite-time agreement likewise does not determine later collapse. Finally, certified lower bounds chosen arbitrarily can differ even for the same presentation; only a fixed functional or a specified calibration admits the quantitative transport theorem.

theorems.title: Why this section matters
theorems.statement: [Why this section matters] Without Lemmas~ ref lem:support-transfer and ref lem:decoder-transport , Theorem~ ref thm:substrate would be only intuitive. These lemmas are the exact reason the paper can speak of substrate invariance without collapsing into slogan-level analogy.

theorems.label: prop:core-per
theorems.title: Core-to-Persistence Transfer with a Common Support
theorems.statement: [Core-to-Persistence Transfer with a Common Support] Suppose a Core realization has a nonempty compact admissible support that is invariant under every admitted control, stays at positive distance from the collapse set, and contains or converges into an admitted attractor region. Then Iper holds on that support.

theorems.label: prop:p1-ri
theorems.title: Rigid Identity Transfer with a Declared Gap
theorems.statement: [Rigid Identity Transfer with a Declared Gap] An identified unique inverse-limit identity object and a positive lower deformation bound for every distinct admitted alternative certify Iri on their declared support.

theorems.label: prop:p2-cont
theorems.title: Regime Continuity Transfer on the Declared Windows
theorems.statement: [Regime Continuity Transfer on the Declared Windows] If the regime assignment takes values in the declared complete comparison space, its paths and fragmentation meet the time-domain bounds, and admissible interventions preserving identity cannot jump to incompatible regimes, then Icont holds there.

theorems.label: prop:p3-diff
theorems.title: Null-Regime Transfer with Temporal Evidence
theorems.statement: [Null-Regime Transfer with Temporal Evidence] If an admissible common schedule supplies a positive separation between two readout windows and the null class is excluded as an asymptotically stable admissible attractor, then Idiff holds on the support.

theorems.label: prop:p4-leg
theorems.title: Forensic Predictions-to-Legibility Transfer with Decoder Evidence
theorems.statement: [Forensic Predictions-to-Legibility Transfer with Decoder Evidence] A structurally closed decoder and finite-rate compression protocol that meet L1--L6 under the declared admissibility, target and sham comparisons certify Ileg .

theorems.label: prop:integration-transfer
theorems.title: Integration Requires a Separate Factorization Bound
theorems.statement: [Integration Requires a Separate Factorization Bound] On a declared support and a nonempty comparison sector, a uniform positive lower bound on the reproduction error of all identity-preserving comparators certifies the integration margin in that sector. Rigidity, continuity and intervention fidelity supply comparison data; a separate proof must exclude accurate factorizations.

theorems.title: Scope of the transfer
theorems.statement: [Scope of the transfer] Nothing in this section re-proves the Core, textit Rigid Identity , textit Structural Assignment Regimes , textit Null-Regime Instability , or textit Forensic Predictions . Each proposition only identifies the minimal upstream burden imported into the present criterion.

theorems.label: thm:existence
theorems.title: Existence of six-predicate operational criterion
theorems.statement: [Existence of six-predicate operational criterion] Let S=(X, Phi ,C,R, Gamma ,U) be an admissible system with non-empty admissible support Aset . If [ Iper (S)= Iri (S)= Iint (S)= Icont (S)= Idiff (S)= Ileg (S)=1, ] then: [leftmargin=1.5em] item S in Cop ; item Qop (S) is well-defined; item Qop (S) neq varnothing .

theorems.label: prop:decoder-visible-separation
theorems.title: Decoder-Visible Separation Gives a Nontrivial Quotient
theorems.statement: [Decoder-Visible Separation Gives a Nontrivial Quotient] If the quotient is defined and two admissible states receive different labels under one certified decoder, horizon and common intervention schedule, or under a certified response-cell map, then | Qop (S)| ge 2 .
