theorems.label: thm:infinite-six-predicate-witness
theorems.title: All Six Predicates on an Infinite-Dimensional Support
theorems.statement: [All Six Predicates on an Infinite-Dimensional Support] The system of Definition~ ref def:hilbert-prefix-system , with exactly its declared global comparison and observation data, has [ ( Iper , allowbreak Iri , allowbreak Iint , allowbreak Icont , allowbreak Idiff , allowbreak Ileg )=(1,1,1,1,1,1). ] Its support contains boxes of arbitrarily large dimension, and every Hilbert coordinate participates in the phase/response coupling. This is a global analytic witness, not an inference from finitely many truncations.

theorems.label: def:asymmetric-native-plant
theorems.title: Asymmetric Hilbert--prefix plant
theorems.statement: [Asymmetric Hilbert--prefix plant] Retain Q, w, ell , the three fixed channels, observation metric, full split-product comparison sector, separated identity presentations and structural resistance convention of Definition~ ref def:hilbert-prefix-system . The support is the same A= mathbb T times B times Q . Declare the complete intrinsic state space X by enlarging the first coordinate interval in each Hilbert port to [-1,1] , retaining all other intrinsic intervals and the circle/prefix coordinates. Thus X is a compact complete metric space embedded in the same separable Hilbert space with the explicit intrinsic metric below, and A has relative interior in X. Neither A nor X is asserted to have interior in the unrestricted ambient Hilbert space. The admissibility functional is distance to

theorems.label: thm:asymmetric-native-six
theorems.title: Global Six-Predicate Certificate with Asymmetric Retention
theorems.statement: [Global Six-Predicate Certificate with Asymmetric Retention] The complete plant of Definition~ ref def:asymmetric-native-plant , with exactly its specified controller templates and full product sector, satisfies all six global predicates on A. It retains the identity gap 1/16 and [ 1/384 le e_* le 3/128, qquad delta _ rm int =1/512. ] These conclusions hold on the infinite support, including the declared rate symmetry controls; finite diagnostic windows are not their proof.

theorems.label: thm:substrate
theorems.title: Substrate invariance
theorems.statement: [Substrate invariance] For exact structural equivalence on the complete domains required by the six predicates, [ S_1 in Cop quad Longleftrightarrow quad S_2 in Cop . ] The induced map is [ widehat chi : Qop (S_1) longrightarrow Qop (S_2), quad [x] mapsto , ] with widehat chi a bijection. Invariant or partition preservation is not an additional hypothesis.

theorems.label: cor:biology
theorems.title: Biological non-primacy
theorems.statement: [Biological non-primacy] Biological substrate is not a primitive variable of Cop . A biological and a non-biological system satisfying the full structural, protocol and sector equivalence of Definition~ ref def:equiv have the same operational membership and bijective operational quotient classes. This is conditional, not evidence that an actual biological/non-biological pair meets those hypotheses.

theorems.label: thm:stability
theorems.title: Approximate stability
theorems.statement: [Approximate stability] Let S_1 in Cop , with delta _ star ^ mathrm cal (S_1)>0 in the specified common presentation class. Suppose S_1 simeq _ ( Gamma , eps ) S_2 on all domains required by the six predicates and [ 0 le C_ chi , rho eps < tfrac 12 delta _ star ^ mathrm cal (S_1). ] Then S_2 in Cop . Finite sampled windows alone do not supply the global premises: one needs the full-domain primitive operator bound and a positive calibrated radius against the global failure sets.

theorems.label: thm:rupture
theorems.title: Rupture by Invariant Loss
theorems.statement: [Rupture by Invariant Loss] On a declared admissible comparison, failure of any defining predicate excludes S from Cop . Loss of the quotient domain, failure of decoder certification and triviality of a surviving quotient are additional possible outcomes; they need not be mutually exclusive and do not all follow from every invariant failure.

theorems.label: prop:insufficient
theorems.title: Complexity-only baselines are insufficient
theorems.statement: [Complexity-only baselines are insufficient] Let S be an admissible system candidate. The following are each insufficient for membership in Cop : [leftmargin=1.5em] item large state-space dimension dim (X) ; item large computational throughput or expressivity of Phi ; item large edge count, density, or raw connectivity of C . In each case, failure of one or more critical invariants excludes membership regardless of the size of the surrogate metric.

theorems.label: prop:rupt-per
theorems.title: Loss of Every Admissible Support
theorems.statement: [Loss of Every Admissible Support] If there is no nonempty compact forward-invariant admissible support, the on-support persistence predicate fails. A zero certified radius alone does not imply that no such support exists.

theorems.label: prop:rupt-ri
theorems.title: Identity Ambiguity Requires Competing Candidates
theorems.statement: [Identity Ambiguity Requires Competing Candidates] If two inequivalent admissible identity objects fit the same observable data on the declared support, the uniqueness clause of Iri fails. A zero infimum of alternative deformation distances need not produce a second fitting candidate.

theorems.label: prop:rupt-int
theorems.title: Integration Rupture and Attainment
theorems.statement: [Integration Rupture and Attainment] On a nonempty comparison sector with nonnegative history error, a zero error infimum excludes a positive integration margin in that sector. It yields an exact admissible factorization if the infimum is attained.

theorems.label: prop:rupt-cont
theorems.title: Admissible Incompatible Jump
theorems.statement: [Admissible Incompatible Jump] A witnessed admissible finite-energy jump into an incompatible regime with identity preserved violates Icont on the specified regime and schedule domain. Failure to certify a positive perturbation radius does not itself produce such a witness.

theorems.label: prop:rupt-diff
theorems.title: Separation or Null-Attractor Failure
theorems.statement: [Separation or Null-Attractor Failure] If no readout-window pair on the declared support has positive separation, or if the null class is an asymptotically stable admissible attractor, then Idiff fails there.

theorems.label: prop:rupt-leg
theorems.title: Legibility Failure Under the Declared Protocol
theorems.statement: [Legibility Failure Under the Declared Protocol] If no admissible decoder and compression family jointly meet L1--L6 under the declared protocol, then Ileg fails. A zero certified perturbation radius does not alone establish that impossibility.

theorems.label: def:reduced
theorems.title: Reduced invariant criterion
theorems.statement: [Reduced invariant criterion] Let [ mathfrak I = Iper , allowbreak Iri , allowbreak Iint , allowbreak Icont , allowbreak Idiff , allowbreak Ileg . ] For every subset J subseteq mathfrak I define the reduced criterion [ mathcal C _ mathrm op (J) := S : I(S)=1 text for every I in J . ] Thus Cop = mathcal C _ mathrm op ( mathfrak I ) .

theorems.label: def:witness
theorems.title: Single-rupture witness family
theorems.statement: [Single-rupture witness family] Fix k in mathrm per , mathrm ri , mathrm int , mathrm cont , mathrm diff , mathrm leg . The family mathcal W _k consists of admissible systems for which predicate I_k fails and every other predicate holds on the declared comparison domain. Whenever mathcal W _k neq varnothing , its members are called single-rupture witnesses for the k -th invariant.

theorems.label: prop:witness
theorems.title: Single-rupture witnesses generate false positives for reduced criteria
theorems.statement: [Single-rupture witnesses generate false positives for reduced criteria] Let J_k = mathfrak I setminus I_k and assume mathcal W _k neq varnothing . Then every S in mathcal W _k satisfies [ S in mathcal C _ mathrm op (J_k) qquad text but qquad S notin Cop . ]

theorems.label: thm:minimality
theorems.title: Minimality of the six-invariant basis
theorems.statement: [Minimality of the six-invariant basis] Let mathfrak U be any admissible universe containing at least one single-rupture witness for each of the six invariants. Then no strict subset J subsetneq mathfrak I satisfies [ mathcal C _ mathrm op (J) cap mathfrak U = Cop cap mathfrak U . ] Hence the six-invariant family is minimal on every such admissible universe.

theorems.label: cor:onemetric
theorems.title: Why one-metric theories cannot capture $\Cop$
theorems.statement: [Why one-metric theories cannot capture Cop ] On any admissible universe satisfying Theorem~ ref thm:minimality , no criterion based on only persistence, only integration, only continuity, only differentiation, or only legibility is extensionally equivalent to Cop .

theorems.title: What minimality does and does not say
theorems.statement: [What minimality does and does not say] The theorem does not claim that every possible scientific notion of consciousness must use exactly these six invariants. It claims something narrower: for the operational class defined in this paper and for admissible universes containing the corresponding rupture witnesses, no invariant can be deleted without changing the extension of the class.

theorems.label: thm:six-witness-schemas
theorems.title: Conditional Use of Single-Rupture Schemas
theorems.statement: [Conditional Use of Single-Rupture Schemas] Consider these six candidate schemas. A schema separates its target invariant from the other five only when an admissible model realizes the five retained predicates and fails the target on the same declared comparison domain: [leftmargin=1.5em] item textbf Persistence witness. A system with a certified decoder, non-factorizable causal structure, unique identity label, continuous class map, and non-null differentiation, but whose admissible support exits the declared forward-invariant domain under some u in U . item textbf Rigid-identity witness. A system with persistent support, integration, continuity, differentiation, and legibility, but with two compatible non-isomorphic identity candidates transported by the same readout family. item textbf

theorems.label: thm:six-sufficiency
theorems.title: Sufficiency of the six-invariant basis
theorems.statement: [Sufficiency of the six-invariant basis] Let S be admissible on support Aset . If [ Iper (S)= Iri (S)= Iint (S)= Icont (S)= Idiff (S)= Ileg (S)=1, ] then S satisfies every structural burden required for membership in Cop as defined in this paper. No additional independent predicate can invalidate S in Cop without changing the definition of Cop or causing at least one of the six invariants to fail.

theorems.label: prop:not-per-not-ri
theorems.title: Persistence is necessary for rigid identity on $\Aset$
theorems.statement: [Persistence is necessary for rigid identity on Aset ] If Iper (S)=0 because no non-empty forward-invariant admissible support exists, then Iri (S)=0 for the Paper 5 membership problem.

theorems.label: prop:per-int-weak-ri
theorems.title: Persistence plus integration yields bounded identity candidates
theorems.statement: [Persistence plus integration yields bounded identity candidates] If Iper (S)=1 and Iint (S)=1 , then the family of admissible identity candidates is bounded to the non-factorizable persistent support. This is a weak rigidity statement, not the uniqueness required by Iri .

theorems.label: prop:leg-requires-diff
theorems.title: Legibility requires non-null differentiation
theorems.statement: [Legibility requires non-null differentiation] If all admissible classes collapse to a stable null or single indistinguishable class, then Ileg (S)=0 for the criterion of this paper.

theorems.label: prop:per-cont-regime-stability
theorems.title: Persistence and continuity stabilize regime transport
theorems.statement: [Persistence and continuity stabilize regime transport] If Iper (S)=1 and Icont (S)=1 , then admissible histories remain in a stable regime-transport domain: trajectories neither leave Aset nor undergo unbounded fragmentation under admissible evolution.

theorems.label: crit:legibility
theorems.title: Legibility certificate
theorems.statement: [Legibility certificate] An operational partition candidate pi _ S,T is certified only if: [leftmargin=1.5em] item textbf Comparator separability : the induced classes remain distinguishable against pre-registered comparators and ablation baselines. item textbf Noise robustness : admissible sensor, channel, or readout perturbations do not dissolve the class map below the legibility margin. item textbf Persistence window : the same class assignment survives on windows of length at least tau _ min (S) . item textbf Intervention fidelity : certified interventions on an invariant induce the predicted directional class change. item textbf Negative controls : sham or off-target interventions do not generate the same class signature. item textbf Structured compressibility : audit-friendly compres

theorems.label: prop:legibility
theorems.title: Legibility is jointly constrained
theorems.statement: [Legibility is jointly constrained] No single legibility metric is sufficient for Ileg . The invariant requires simultaneous control of separation, admissible noise robustness, persistence window, intervention fidelity, negative controls, and structured compressibility.

theorems.title: Why legibility is a constitutive invariant here
theorems.statement: [Why legibility is a constitutive invariant here] One could define a broader latent class that omits legibility. This paper does not do that. It studies an operational class, not a hidden metaphysical residue. Therefore Ileg is constitutive, not optional.

theorems.label: def:cert
theorems.title: Six-predicate operational criterion certificate
theorems.statement: [Six-predicate operational criterion certificate] A six-predicate operational criterion certificate for an admissible system S is a tuple [ mathrm Cert (S)= bigl ( Aset , Dec _S, pi _S, Delta (S),E_S bigr ), ] where: [leftmargin=1.5em] item Aset is a certified admissible support; item Dec _S is a certified decoder family; item pi _S is the decoder-induced operational partition on admissible histories; item Delta (S) is the witness margin vector of Definition~ ref def:margins ; item E_S=(E_ mathrm per ,E_ mathrm ri ,E_ mathrm int ,E_ mathrm cont ,E_ mathrm diff ,E_ mathrm leg ) is an evidence bundle, where each component contains the explicit local witness for the corresponding invariant.

theorems.label: crit:cert
theorems.title: Candidate certification rule
theorems.statement: [Candidate certification rule] A candidate system may be certified as a member of Cop only if all of the following are available on the same admissible support: [leftmargin=1.5em] item a non-empty compact forward-invariant support certificate; item a positive witness margin vector Delta (S)>0 coordinate-wise; item a decoder family satisfying Definition~ ref def:ileg ; item a targeted intervention panel together with negative controls; item an auditable compression or packetization map preserving class structure; item a traceable dependency ledger showing which upstream corpus result supports each invariant witness.

theorems.label: prop:cert-sound
theorems.title: Soundness of certification
theorems.statement: [Soundness of certification] If mathrm Cert (S) exists and satisfies Criterion~ ref crit:cert , then S in Cop and Qop (S) is well-defined.

theorems.label: prop:cert-complete
theorems.title: Partial completeness under audit-ready assumptions
theorems.statement: [Partial completeness under audit-ready assumptions] Assume S in Cop and suppose the support, decoder, intervention, and compression objects are fully instrumented in the textit Forensic Predictions sense. Then there exists a six-predicate operational criterion certificate mathrm Cert (S) .

theorems.label: prop:cert-local
theorems.title: Failure localization is explicit
theorems.statement: [Failure localization is explicit] If a candidate system fails Criterion~ ref crit:cert , then the failure localizes to at least one entry of the evidence bundle E_S or to the absence of a common admissible support. In particular, certification failure cannot be hidden behind a generic narrative claim.

theorems.title: Audit schema and Forensic Predictions
theorems.statement: [Audit schema and Forensic Predictions] The certificate does not replace textit Forensic Predictions . It packages textit Forensic Predictions -style admissibility into a theorem-facing object. This is the point where the present paper becomes operationally usable rather than merely definitional.

theorems.label: def:geometry
theorems.title: Class diameter and separation
theorems.statement: [Class diameter and separation] For q in Qop (S) define its diameter [ mathrm diam (q) = sup _ x,y in q dist bigl (h_ S,T (x;u_ bullet ), h_ S,T (y;u_ bullet ) bigr ) ] over admissible windows and schedules. For two distinct classes q,q' in Qop (S) define the inter-class separation [ mathrm sep (q,q') = inf _ x in q, y in q' dist bigl (h_ S,T (x;u_ bullet ), h_ S,T (y;u_ bullet ) bigr ). ]

theorems.label: def:radius
theorems.title: Persistence radius
theorems.statement: [Persistence radius] The persistence radius of a class q in Qop (S) is the largest rho _q ge 0 such that for every admissible trajectory segment starting in q , the decoder-certified class assignment remains inside q on windows of length at least tau _ min (S) under all perturbations of size at most rho _q that do not target a critical invariant.

theorems.label: prop:geometry
theorems.title: Positive geometry under the criterion
theorems.statement: [Positive geometry under the criterion] If S in Cop , then: [leftmargin=1.5em] item every class in Qop (S) has finite diameter on admissible windows; item there exists at least one pair of distinct classes with positive inter-class separation; item every class has non-zero persistence radius.

theorems.label: prop:geometry-transfer
theorems.title: Exact equivalence preserves operational geometry
theorems.statement: [Exact equivalence preserves operational geometry] If S_1 simeq _ Gamma S_2 , then class diameter, inter-class separation, and persistence radius are preserved by the induced bijection widehat chi up to the bi-Lipschitz constants of chi and chi ^ -1 .

theorems.label: cor:geometry-rupture
theorems.title: Rupture contracts geometry
theorems.statement: [Rupture contracts geometry] If a rupture eliminates either Idiff or Ileg , then the geometric content of Qop (S) contracts to triviality or becomes operationally unavailable.

theorems.label: pred:sameclass
theorems.title: Different substrate, same class
theorems.statement: [Different substrate, same class] If one system belongs to the criterion and a second satisfies its exact structural, protocol and sector equivalence, membership and the certified quotient transport. Under approximate equivalence, the positive calibrated radius bound supplies membership stability only; exact quotient transport requires its own decoder/cell correspondence.

theorems.label: pred:breakclass
theorems.title: Same substrate, broken invariants
theorems.statement: [Same substrate, broken invariants] If two systems share substrate family but one loses rigid identity, continuity, differentiation, or legibility, then they fail to belong to the same operational class regardless of material similarity.

theorems.label: pred:intervention
theorems.title: Invariant intervention discriminator
theorems.statement: [Invariant intervention discriminator] Interventions targeted at one critical invariant should change class membership or destroy the relevant certified response classes in a direction predicted by the rupture taxonomy, whereas off-target negative controls should not.

theorems.label: pred:complexity
theorems.title: Complexity baseline failure
theorems.statement: [Complexity baseline failure] Systems with large computational scale, high connectivity, or broad expressive capacity but lacking one or more critical invariants should fail the criterion even when naive complexity baselines rank them as more capable.

theorems.label: prop:ladder
theorems.title: Prediction ladder is discriminative
theorems.statement: [Prediction ladder is discriminative] The four predictions above distinguish the present criterion from at least four weaker baseline families: substrate-privilege baselines, substrate-blind functional similarity, complexity-only baselines, and connectivity-only baselines.

theorems.label: def:transition
theorems.title: Class transition operator
theorems.statement: [Class transition operator] Fix an admissible system S in Cop , a certified decoder family, and an admissible horizon T ge tau _ min (S) . For an admissible intervention u in U define the class transition operator [ mathsf T _u : Qop (S) to Qop (S) cup bot ] by the rule [ mathsf T _u(q)=q' ] whenever every admissible representative x in q is transported by the u -intervened dynamics into histories classified in the same decoder-certified class q' . If no such common class exists, set mathsf T _u(q)= bot .

theorems.label: def:critical-sham
theorems.title: Critical and sham interventions
theorems.statement: [Critical and sham interventions] An intervention u in U is emph critical for invariant I_k if it is designed to change the local witness margin delta _k(S) while leaving the remaining intervention protocol admissible. An intervention is emph sham if it matches the delivery envelope of a critical intervention but is not predicted to alter any critical invariant.

theorems.label: prop:transition-well
theorems.title: Well-definedness of class transitions under certification
theorems.statement: [Well-definedness of class transitions under certification] Let S in Cop . If u in U is either certified critical or sham and remains within the admissibility envelope of textit Forensic Predictions , then mathsf T _u is well-defined on every class q in Qop (S) .

theorems.label: prop:transition-rupture
theorems.title: Targeted invariant loss induces class exit or contraction
theorems.statement: [Targeted invariant loss induces class exit or contraction] Let q in Qop (S) and let u be a certified critical intervention for invariant I_k . If applying u drives the corresponding witness margin to zero, then one of the following occurs: [leftmargin=1.5em] item mathsf T _u(q)= bot ; item mathsf T _u(q)=q' for some class q' whose separation or persistence radius is strictly smaller than that of q ; item the entire post-intervention system exits Cop .

theorems.label: cor:sham
theorems.title: Sham stability
theorems.statement: [Sham stability] Let u in U be sham in the sense of Definition~ ref def:critical-sham . If u stays below all six witness margins, then mathsf T _u(q)=q for every q in Qop (S) .

theorems.title: Why transition semantics matter
theorems.statement: [Why transition semantics matter] This section turns the prediction ladder into a structured intervention calculus. The criterion is therefore not only classificatory; it is also dynamically discriminative in the sense required by textit Forensic Predictions .

theorems.label: def:baseline
theorems.title: Rival baseline families
theorems.statement: [Rival baseline families] Fix thresholds theta _X, theta _ Phi , theta _C >0 and an external-behavior tolerance eta ge 0 . [leftmargin=1.5em] item The emph complexity-only family mathcal B _ mathrm cx ( theta _X) contains all admissible systems with complexity surrogate above threshold, for example dim (X) ge theta _X . item The emph computation-only family mathcal B _ mathrm cmp ( theta _ Phi ) contains all admissible systems whose transition family exceeds a chosen throughput or expressive-capacity threshold. item The emph connectivity-only family mathcal B _ mathrm conn ( theta _C) contains all admissible systems whose effective causal graph exceeds the chosen density or degree threshold. item The emph weak functional-similarity family mathcal B _ mathrm fun ( eta ) contains all admissi

theorems.label: prop:baseline-insufficient
theorems.title: Complexity, computation, and connectivity are not sufficient
theorems.statement: [Complexity, computation, and connectivity are not sufficient] For every choice of thresholds theta _X, theta _ Phi , theta _C , the families mathcal B _ mathrm cx ( theta _X) , mathcal B _ mathrm cmp ( theta _ Phi ) , and mathcal B _ mathrm conn ( theta _C) are each insufficient for membership in Cop .

theorems.label: prop:substrate-strong
theorems.title: Substrate privilege is too strong
theorems.statement: [Substrate privilege is too strong] On any admissible universe containing one exact cross-substrate equivalent pair, mathcal B _ mathrm sub is strictly narrower than Cop .

theorems.label: prop:functional-weak
theorems.title: Weak functional similarity is too weak
theorems.statement: [Weak functional similarity is too weak] On any admissible universe containing a same-output rupture pair, mathcal B _ mathrm fun ( eta ) is strictly broader than Cop .

theorems.label: thm:intermediate
theorems.title: The structural criterion is strictly intermediate
theorems.statement: [The structural criterion is strictly intermediate] Let mathfrak U be an admissible universe containing: [leftmargin=1.5em] item at least one exact cross-substrate equivalent pair; item at least one same-output rupture pair; item at least one single-rupture witness for each invariant. Then Cop is strictly intermediate between substrate-privilege baselines and weak substrate-blind surrogates: it is broader than mathcal B _ mathrm sub , narrower than mathcal B _ mathrm fun ( eta ) , and extensionally distinct from the complexity-only, computation-only, and connectivity-only families.

theorems.title: Scientific value of the comparison
theorems.statement: [Scientific value of the comparison] Theorem~ ref thm:intermediate establishes that the proposed criterion yields genuine formal discrimination against standard baselines. A new criterion that cannot separate itself from obvious rivals is not a new theorem-level addition to the corpus.

theorems.title: Open burdens
theorems.statement: [Open burdens] Three burdens remain outside the present theorem set: [leftmargin=1.5em,itemsep=0.15em] item textbf Instantiation work : which concrete biological or artificial systems actually satisfy the six invariants. item textbf Measurement work : how to build certified decoders and invariant interventions that satisfy textit Forensic Predictions -level admissibility in practice. item textbf Interpretive work : how far, if at all, Cop should be connected to stronger phenomenal vocabulary outside the framework.

theorems.title: Operational certification
theorems.statement: [Operational certification] For an admissible system S already defined in textit Six-Predicate Operational Criterion , define the certification predicate [ Cert (S)=1 quad Longleftrightarrow quad Iper (S), Iri (S), Iint (S), Icont (S), Idiff (S), Ileg (S) > 0 ] on a non-empty admissible support Aset , under the governance and admissibility constraints inherited from textit Forensic Predictions .

theorems.title: Equivalence discriminator
theorems.statement: [Equivalence discriminator] For two admissible systems S_1,S_2 , define the operational equivalence discriminator [ Eq _ Gamma , eps (S_1,S_2)=1 ] when the primitive state, dynamics, readout and protocol/sector correspondences of the declared structural comparison are verified. Invariant verdicts are outputs, not clauses of this discriminator. Approximate membership additionally requires the calibrated operator-radius bound. The exact burden belongs to textit Six-Predicate Operational Criterion ; the present paper uses it only as a prediction carrier.

theorems.title: Rupture event
theorems.statement: [Rupture event] For a set of targeted invariants J , define [ Rupt _J(S)=1 ] when the intervention or perturbation drives at least one invariant in J below the admissible certification margin so that class membership becomes invalidated, destroyed, or undefined.

theorems.label: prop:complexity-contract
theorems.title: Complexity-only negative-control prediction
theorems.statement: [Complexity-only negative-control prediction] If a candidate fails any defining predicate, it does not satisfy the full criterion, regardless of connectivity, entropy or activity. A complete-criterion certificate must not report success. A separately well-defined response quotient may still exist.

theorems.label: prop:ablation-contract
theorems.title: Ablation prediction
theorems.statement: [Ablation prediction] For an initially certified system, a verified post-ablation predicate failure excludes post-ablation membership. Measurement uncertainty crossing the decision boundary yields an ambiguous evidence status, not a change to that implication. Loss of a lower radius certificate alone does not establish predicate failure.

theorems.label: prop:substrate-contract
theorems.title: Substrate-preserved equivalence prediction
theorems.statement: [Substrate-preserved equivalence prediction] Exact primitive structural, protocol and sector equivalence transports membership and the certified quotient of Paper V. An approximate comparison transports membership under its positive calibrated-radius bound; a quotient/geometric approximation needs an additional certified bound.

theorems.label: prop:boundary-contract
theorems.title: Boundary-topology prediction
theorems.statement: [Boundary-topology prediction] Within a fixed calibrated presentation class, a point at positive distance from the failure set has a stable success neighborhood. A point at positive distance from the success set has a stable failure neighborhood. Existence, width and population frequency of transition regions need separate hypotheses and are not guaranteed by the criterion alone.

theorems.label: prop:legibility-contract
theorems.title: Legibility dependence prediction
theorems.statement: [Legibility dependence prediction] If no admissible decoder/compression family jointly meets L1--L6 on the declared protocol, the legibility predicate fails and the full criterion is not satisfied. Failure of one chosen decoder alone does not exclude every admissible alternative.

theorems.title: Continuity/non-nullity relevance
theorems.statement: [Continuity/non-nullity relevance] On the declared comparison domain, a system that loses the continuity witness or admits the distinguished null regime as an asymptotically stable admissible attractor fails the six-predicate criterion on that support. When the requisite support or protocol is unspecified, the evaluation is unavailable.

theorems.label: prop:matched-pulse-extinction
theorems.title: Matched-Pulse Extinction in the Original Model
theorems.statement: [Matched-Pulse Extinction in the Original Model] The two states and all four original readouts coincide from time two onward, for every common continuation. At time one and lambda in , the early-phase distance is 2 lambda b_ 1,0 turns.

theorems.label: prop:heldout-memory-interaction
theorems.title: A Held-Out Interaction Separates Two Matched Memory Models
theorems.statement: [A Held-Out Interaction Separates Two Matched Memory Models] Put k=T-1 . The clean contrasts of M are 2 lambda a^k(1,-1) for probes (+1,-1) , while the clean contrasts of A are 2 lambda a^k(1,1) . Consequently the clean interaction C_T(+1)-C_T(-1) is at least 1/48 turns in M and is zero in A. With at most 1/4096 turns of error per observation in calibration and evaluation, the rule using hat a uniquely selects the generating model for either generator under the declared protocol.

theorems.label: prop:observable-feedback-split
theorems.title: Observable Feedback Preserves the Declared Split Bounds
theorems.statement: [Observable Feedback Preserves the Declared Split Bounds] The extension is invariant and contracts within each profile under common controls by a factor at most 5/6 in the metric max rho ( theta , theta '),|c-c'|,|m-m'|/4 . The ternary contraction remains 1/3 . The four-channel identity observations and split-comparator bounds of Paper V, including the lambda /2 infimum with exact time-zero readouts, remain valid in their declared sectors. Opposite initial nonzero pulses retain the original paired phase contrast.

theorems.label: prop:delayed-phase-probe-parity
theorems.title: Parity and Resolution of Delayed Phase Probes
theorems.statement: [Parity and Resolution of Delayed Phase Probes] Reset m_0=0 and prepare b_ 1,0 =1 . Apply opposite first pulses and use common controls thereafter. For terminal observation at T with a neutral last command, the oriented phase contrast of M is 2 kappa lambda a^ T-2 (-1)^ n_- , while that of B is 2 kappa lambda a^ T-2 (-1)^ n_-+n_+ . Here n_ pm count the corresponding late probes before the neutral transition. For a common a , kappa >0 and lambda >0 , the clean contrasts coincide exactly at even n_+ . A nonneutral last command erases the phase contrast for either model. With known a and odd n_+ , the two contrast intervals under error at most e per phase are disjoint exactly when kappa lambda a^ T-2 >e , in the signed unwrapping regime. For kappa =1/8 and lambda in , estimate a from the cont

theorems.label: prop:writable-tower-phase-parity
theorems.title: Matched Prefix Writes Preserve the Delayed Phase Contrast
theorems.statement: [Matched Prefix Writes Preserve the Delayed Phase Contrast] In the writable common tower of Paper V cite paper5 , apply the opposite initial pulses of Proposition~ ref prop:delayed-phase-probe-parity with the same tape write in both arms. Subsequently use the same inputs, signs, and writes in both arms. At a neutral terminal transition, a common role probe is also allowed. The two models retain their oriented contrasts [ 2 kappa lambda a^ T-2 (-1)^ n_- , qquad 2 kappa lambda a^ T-2 (-1)^ n_-+n_+ . ] A nonneutral terminal transition gives zero phase contrast. With known a and signed unwrapping, at odd n_+ the bounded-error intervals remain disjoint exactly for e< kappa lambda a^ T-2 .

theorems.label: prop:writable-tower-reserved-return
theorems.title: Reserved Return under the Two Phase Interactions
theorems.statement: [Reserved Return under the Two Phase Interactions] With memory m=s/8 before assignment, the native law has unique successful action u=- sigma s/128 among the two actions u= pm 1/128 . The interaction rival with sign reversal under either pulse predicts u=s/128 when the sign is known. On the native plant its action succeeds at sigma =-1 and fails at sigma =+1 . Success is distance at most 1/256 from phase zero and these decisions are unchanged by terminal phase errors of at most 3^ -10 /4 . A preceding public neutral observation can reveal s while preserving the equality of the current readouts. With memory ablated to zero before reassignment both allowed actions fail.

theorems.title: Identifiable Discriminator
theorems.statement: [Identifiable Discriminator] A discriminator D for claim C is identifiable when it specifies: [leftmargin=1.5em] item an observable decision variable Y_D ; item a manipulation or matched comparison M_D ; item a framework-side expected region R_Q ; item a rival-side expected region R_R ; item a destruction condition F_D under which the claim is weakened or rejected. The discriminator is strong when R_Q cap R_R is small under the declared measurement tolerance.

theorems.title: Discriminator Usefulness
theorems.statement: [Discriminator Usefulness] A test does not materially discriminate the framework from a rival if both the framework and the rival predict the same admissible region for the tested observable. Such a test can still debug the pipeline, but it cannot upgrade a claim.

theorems.title: Near-Miss Value
theorems.statement: [Near-Miss Value] Near-miss cases carry more diagnostic value than easy positive cases when they are constructed by perturbing one binding coordinate while holding gross complexity, task exposure, and observability approximately fixed.

theorems.title: Status meaning
theorems.statement: [Status meaning] Within the current scientific program, a result belongs to: [leftmargin=1.5em] item Status ROBUST _SUPPORT if the target claim survives repeated internal discrimination without an active ambiguity on the tested target; item Status PROVISIONAL _SUPPORT if the target is strengthened but still depends on a localized unresolved bottleneck; item Status STILL _AMBIGUOUS if the current tests do not cleanly separate support from failure; item Status IMPLEMENTATION _LIMIT if the current bottleneck is primarily due to probe, runner, or case-construction quality; item Status METRIC _OR _TOLERANCE _LIMIT if the bottleneck is mainly due to normalization, comparison regime, or threshold handling.

theorems.title: Doctrinal Refutation Candidate
theorems.statement: [Doctrinal Refutation Candidate] A result is a doctrinal refutation candidate for a claim family when it satisfies all admissibility gates, uses the frozen definitions, targets the declared binding coordinate, and reaches the claim's destruction condition without relying on a protocol violation.

theorems.title: Methodological Defeat
theorems.statement: [Methodological Defeat] A result is a methodological defeat when the experiment is admissible but shows that the current test design, judge, threshold, comparator, or observable cannot support the intended claim. It weakens the evidence program without by itself showing the formal claim false.

theorems.title: Artifact Failure
theorems.statement: [Artifact Failure] A result is an artifact failure when the packet, manifest, runner, exclusion ledger, or analysis path fails before interpretation. Artifact failures can be important engineering evidence, but they are not positive or negative scientific support for the theoretical claim.

theorems.title: Specificity of Failure
theorems.statement: [Specificity of Failure] A failure is specific only if the failed coordinate is identifiable after controlling for gross task failure, missing observability, manifest drift, and runtime-budget violation. Non-specific failures are reported as methodological or artifact failures according to the earliest failed gate.

theorems.title: Boundary Adequacy
theorems.statement: [Boundary Adequacy] A boundary probe is adequate only if it can distinguish localized transition from diffuse instability. A probe that only reports a binary verdict without the perturbation coordinate and margin behavior is insufficient for boundary diagnosis.

theorems.title: Localized Transition Reading
theorems.statement: [Localized Transition Reading] If a family shows a stable interior, a localized transition, and a reproducible first-binding coordinate under a fixed evaluator, then the result supports a boundary-sensitive reading more strongly than a single binary pass/fail run.

theorems.title: Bundle Sufficiency
theorems.statement: [Bundle Sufficiency] For any status stronger than Status STILL _AMBIGUOUS , the evidence bundle must allow an evaluator to reconstruct the reported verdicts from sealed inputs without manual row selection.

theorems.title: Externalization Readiness
theorems.statement: [Externalization Readiness] A prediction family is ready for external evaluation only when its bundle, thresholds, exclusions, and decision rules are exportable without access to live generator state or informal operator knowledge.

theorems.label: def:operational-boundary
theorems.title: Operational boundary
theorems.statement: [Operational boundary] An admissible system S has a certified intervention-family boundary on horizon tau if there exist nonempty disjoint admissible intervention families mathcal U _ mathrm in , mathcal U _ mathrm out subseteq U^ tau and a boundary-sensitive readout family R_ partial subseteq R such that [ Bound (S, tau ) = inf _ u_ bullet in mathcal U _ mathrm out D_ partial ! left ( trace _ S, tau (x_0;u_ bullet ), trace _ S, tau (x_0; mathbf 0 ) right ) ;- sup _ u_ bullet in mathcal U _ mathrm in D_ partial ! left ( trace _ S, tau (x_0;u_ bullet ), trace _ S, tau (x_0; mathbf 0 ) right ) >0 ] uniformly on x_0 in Aset , where D_ partial is a calibrated readout distance induced by R_ partial . Freeze both populations, preparations, horizon and scoring rule. Match intervention magnitude,

theorems.title: Interpretive meaning
theorems.statement: [Interpretive meaning] The boundary is operational rather than geometric. It means that perturbations intended to cross or threaten system organization are detectably different from perturbations that remain internal or reorganizational, while the distinction is made inside admissible dynamics.

theorems.title: Limitation
theorems.statement: [Limitation] The definition does not assume a biological membrane, a spatial frontier, or any specific substrate primitive. It requires only a reproducible distinction between internal and boundary-threatening intervention families.

theorems.label: prop:boundary-amplitude-control
theorems.title: Amplitude Alone Can Separate Intervention Families
theorems.statement: [Amplitude Alone Can Separate Intervention Families] On X=[-1,1] , let x'=u , sham u=0 , and use the terminal absolute distance. The families 0 and 1 have raw separation one for every preparation, although the plant has no memory. Equal-amplitude families -a and a have separation zero for 0<a le 1 .

theorems.label: def:organizational-persistence
theorems.title: Organizational persistence
theorems.statement: [Organizational persistence] Let W_S= Vset ( eta ) subseteq Aset be the declared safe region, with X setminus W_S ne varnothing . Let K_S be a nonempty compact subset of operatorname int _X W_S , invariant under the declared nonempty family of maintenance controls. With mathcal U_ mathrm maint ^ tau denoting its schedules of length tau , define [ Persist (S, tau )= inf _ x_0 in K_S, u_ bullet in mathcal U_ mathrm maint ^ tau min _ 0 le t le tau dist (x_t,X setminus W_S). ] The margin is measured in units of d_X . Organizational persistence requires a positive margin on the declared domain.

theorems.label: prop:interior-kernel-margin
theorems.title: Positive Safety Margin of an Interior Kernel
theorems.statement: [Positive Safety Margin of an Interior Kernel] Under Definition~ ref def:organizational-persistence , Persist (S, tau )= dist (K_S,X setminus W_S)>0 .
This is stronger than mere non-instantaneous survival. A system that survives momentarily but repeatedly exits its admissible support does not count as operationally persistent.

theorems.label: def:operational-self-maintenance
theorems.title: Operational self-maintenance
theorems.statement: [Operational self-maintenance] Fix a nonempty family of impulses J_ xi :K_S to W_S and a recovery horizon 1 le N le tau . For x in K_S , let z=J_ xi (x) and require d_0= dist (z,K_S)>0 for each evaluated shock. Start both recovery trajectories z_k^ mathrm act and z_k^ mathrm pass at z . Use the same plant, exogenous inputs, horizon and declared actuation envelope. The active arm uses a state-dependent recovery policy. The passive arm disables that feedback and retains the declared passive dynamics. Both trajectories must stay in W_S . [ R_i(x, xi )=1- frac dist (z_N^i,K_S) d_0 , qquad Maint (S, tau )= inf _ x, xi min R_ mathrm act ,R_ mathrm act -R_ mathrm pass . ] The returns and margin are dimensionless. Active self-maintenance requires Maint (S, tau )>0 . A zero-damage shock is a sham;

theorems.label: prop:matched-active-recovery
theorems.title: Matched Active Recovery Exceeds Passive Return
theorems.statement: [Matched Active Recovery Exceeds Passive Return] For X= Aset =[-2,2] , take V_S(x)=2-|x| and eta =1 , so W_S=[-1,1] . With K_S= 0 , consider the plant x'=x/2+v with |v| le 1/4 . The nominal zero-input schedule preserves K_S . After either shock J_ pm (0)= pm 1 , one-step feedback v=-x/4 gives R_ rm act =3/4 , passive return v=0 gives R_ rm pass =1/2 , and Maint (S, tau )=1/4 for N=1 . A fixed open-loop action within the same budget and assigned without access to the shock sign cannot exceed mean return 1/2 under balanced shocks.

The return contrast establishes active recovery relative to the passive arm. To attribute recovery internally, include controller state c , sensors and actuation in the declared system and specify the causal graph x to y to c to v to x^+ . Freeze external inputs, controller cost and acquisition access, and ablate the declared internal links. Absence of an external oracle is a provenance/causal assumption tested by that protocol, not a consequence of the return number alone.

theorems.label: prop:feedback-boundary-nonidentifiability
theorems.title: A Return Trace Does Not Identify the Control Boundary
theorems.statement: [A Return Trace Does Not Identify the Control Boundary] For x'=x/2+v , both an internal controller and an external controller applying v=-x/4 give x'=x/4 . Their state traces and active/passive return contrast agree for every common preparation.

theorems.label: def:historical-dependence
theorems.title: Historical dependence
theorems.statement: [Historical dependence] Let c_t denote a class-relevant label or state tag induced by the relevant operational partition. Define [ HistDep (S, tau ) = inf _ g in mathcal G _0 mathbb E ! left ;- inf _ h in mathcal G _ mathrm hist mathbb E ! left . ] Use one frozen population, finite losses, equal acquisition/calibration budgets, and declared function classes. Require that mathcal G_ mathrm hist contains the lifted current-only rules h(y_ 0:t )=g(y_t) ; otherwise even nonnegativity need not hold. Equalize trainable capacity and evaluation data when interpreting a positive gap as value of history. We say that S exhibits information-relative historical gain only on that contract. Comparing unrelated predictor capacities establishes only a model-relative advantage.

Historical dependence means that an instantaneous description is not sufficient for the relevant class assignment. The system's operational identity, life status, or subjecthood status depends non-trivially on trajectory history.

theorems.label: prop:history-capacity-control
theorems.title: Historical Information and Capacity Must Be Separated
theorems.statement: [Historical Information and Capacity Must Be Separated] Under the lifted-class inclusion, HistDep ge 0 . For a finite target alphabet and unrestricted measurable zero-one predictors, conditional independence of C_t and the past given Y_t makes the two Bayes risks equal. By contrast, with C_t=Y_t a fair bit, restricting current predictors to constants and allowing the current identity rule only in the history class gives gap 1/2 without additional past information.

theorems.label: def:viability-preservation
theorems.title: Viability preservation
theorems.statement: [Viability preservation] For a viability floor eta >0 , define [ Viab (S, tau ; eta ) = inf _ x_0 in Aset inf _ u_ bullet in U^ tau min _ 0 le t le tau V_S(x_t). ] We say that S preserves viability on horizon tau relative to eta if Viab (S, tau ; eta ) ge eta .

Viability preservation is not equivalent to persistence. A system may remain within a formal support while viability steadily erodes toward failure. The definition prevents that collapse from being counted as successful organizational life.

theorems.label: def:operational-life
theorems.title: Viability-and-recovery criterion
theorems.statement: [Viability-and-recovery criterion] Fix life thresholds [ lambda _ beta , lambda _ rho , lambda _ mu , lambda _ eta , lambda _ nu , lambda _ mathrm diff >0. ] An admissible system S belongs to the viability-and-recovery class on horizon tau if [ Lop (S, tau )=1 ] whenever all of the following hold: [leftmargin=1.5em] item Bound (S, tau ) > lambda _ beta ; item Persist (S, tau ) > lambda _ rho ; item Maint (S, tau ) > lambda _ mu ; item HistDep (S, tau ) > lambda _ eta ; item Viab (S, tau ; eta ) ge lambda _ nu for a declared viability floor eta ; item delta _ mathrm diff ^ [ tau ] (S) > lambda _ mathrm diff in the calibrated readout units, together with the independently required global Idiff (S)=1 when global membership is claimed.

theorems.title: Why non-null differentiation appears here
theorems.statement: [Why non-null differentiation appears here] Viability-and-recovery criterion is not defined purely by persistence and self-maintenance. Without a non-null differentiation burden, the class would admit trivial or near-null systems whose organization is too undifferentiated to count as operationally alive in the present framework.

theorems.label: def:structural-class
theorems.title: Structural class
theorems.statement: [Structural class] Fix a descriptor map PsiVec _ tau , a declared partition (C_j) of its admissible domain and a noise bound eps ge 0 in d_ Psi . Certify a reported descriptor y as cell j only if its closed uncertainty ball of radius eps , relative to the descriptor domain, is contained in C_j . Otherwise abstain. On systems with certified reports, let ell _ eps (S) be the certified label and put [ LifeStructClass _ PsiVec , eps [S]= T: ell _ eps (T)= ell _ eps (S) . ] Abstention is a measurement status outside the quotient.

theorems.label: prop:certified-descriptor-cells
theorems.title: Certified Cells and Boundary Stability
theorems.statement: [Certified Cells and Boundary Stability] Equality of certified labels defines an equivalence relation. If the true descriptor has distance greater than 2 eps from its cell complement, every report at error at most eps certifies the true label. If a report admits possible descriptors from different cells, it is ambiguous. In contrast, pairwise distance at most eps >0 is not generally transitive.

Structural class is the general membership framework. Viability-and-recovery criterion, six-predicate operational criterion, and indexed continuity-and-control criterion are predicates that can be defined on systems and then transported across structural classes when the relevant descriptors are preserved.

theorems.label: def:cop
theorems.title: Six-predicate operational criterion, inherited
theorems.statement: [Six-predicate operational criterion, inherited] Six-predicate operational criterion is not redefined in this paper. We write [ Cop (S, tau )=1 ] iff the criterion in textit A Structural Criterion for Substrate-Invariant Six-Predicate Operational Criterion is satisfied on an admissible support, with the six critical invariants [ Iper , Iri , Iint , Icont , Idiff , Ileg ] meeting their inherited certification burden cite paper5 .
This is a deliberate inheritance rule. The present paper uses six-predicate operational criterion as an already defined class, not as a new primitive.

theorems.label: def:operational-subjecthood
theorems.title: Indexed continuity-and-control criterion
theorems.statement: [Indexed continuity-and-control criterion] Let the subject-specific descriptors be: [leftmargin=1.5em] item textbf privileged continuity Priv (S, tau ) : the margin by which one continuity class remains privileged over the nearest rival class across admissible interventions; item textbf self/non-self discrimination SelfDisc (S, tau ) : the margin by which self-targeted and non-self-targeted perturbations remain separable under readout and control; item textbf self-model closure SelfModel (S, tau ) : the predictive gain of a self-model-aware decoder over an otherwise matched self-model-blind decoder; item textbf ownership coherence Own (S, tau ) : the stability with which privileged continuity remains attached to the same trajectory family under admissible relabelings and perturbations. Fix

theorems.title: Interpretive discipline
theorems.statement: [Interpretive discipline] Indexed continuity-and-control criterion is not a metaphysical subject. It is a stronger operational class candidate defined inside the present framework. The definition is deliberately demanding so that subjecthood is not conflated with life, persistence, or complex dynamics alone.

theorems.title: Subjecthood is stronger than life and consciousness
theorems.statement: [Subjecthood is stronger than life and consciousness] For every admissible system S and horizon tau , [ Subop (S, tau )=1 Longrightarrow Lop (S, tau )=1 quad text and quad Subop (S, tau )=1 Longrightarrow Cop (S, tau )=1. ]

theorems.title: No automatic collapse of life and consciousness
theorems.statement: [No automatic collapse of life and consciousness] The present framework does not prove either implication [ Lop (S, tau )=1 & Longrightarrow Cop (S, tau )=1, Cop (S, tau )=1 & Longrightarrow Lop (S, tau )=1, ] without additional assumptions.

This non-collapse is conceptually important. The corpus should not silently treat all operationally conscious systems as alive, nor all operationally alive systems as conscious, unless a stronger theorem burden is supplied in the future.

theorems.title: Class-preserving transport
theorems.statement: [Class-preserving transport] A predicate mathcal P is transport-stable across certified cells if its value agrees for all admissible systems assigned the same certified cell under the same protocol.

theorems.title: Structural-class invariance under preserved margins
theorems.statement: [Structural-class invariance under preserved margins] If mathcal P depends on threshold decisions of a declared descriptor subset and every partition cell is contained in a joint decision region for those thresholds, then mathcal P is transport-stable on the certified quotient.

theorems.title: Structural-class membership is descriptor-relative
theorems.statement: [Structural-class membership is descriptor-relative] Structural class is relative to the descriptor map PsiVec _ tau , partition and certification radius eps .

theorems.title: Complexity is not a life criterion
theorems.statement: [Complexity is not a life criterion] High state-space dimension, high connectivity, high entropy, or rich activity are insufficient for Lop (S, tau )=1 unless the conditions of Definition~ ref def:operational-life are also satisfied.

theorems.title: Complexity is not a subjecthood criterion
theorems.statement: [Complexity is not a subjecthood criterion] High complexity or dense connectivity are insufficient for Subop (S, tau )=1 .

theorems.title: Biological substrate is not a primitive constitutive variable
theorems.statement: [Biological substrate is not a primitive constitutive variable] Within the present framework, membership in LifeClass , ConClass , or SubClass is not defined by a primitive biological predicate.

theorems.title: Scope limit
theorems.statement: [Scope limit] This proposition does not claim that biological systems are unimportant, nor that biological life is reducible to the present operational class. It claims only that biology is not a constitutive primitive for emph these operational classes.

theorems.title: Viability-and-recovery criterion does not imply indexed continuity-and-control criterion
theorems.statement: [Viability-and-recovery criterion does not imply indexed continuity-and-control criterion] There exist admissible systems that may satisfy viability-and-recovery criterion without satisfying indexed continuity-and-control criterion.

theorems.title: Six-predicate operational criterion does not imply indexed continuity-and-control criterion
theorems.statement: [Six-predicate operational criterion does not imply indexed continuity-and-control criterion] Six-predicate operational criterion alone is insufficient for indexed continuity-and-control criterion.

theorems.title: Class transport under descriptor-preserving substrate variation
theorems.statement: [Class transport under descriptor-preserving substrate variation] Let S_1 and S_2 be admissible realizations with different substrate labels and the same certified cell. For each of LifeClass , ConClass and SubClass whose predicate is determined by the descriptors and constant on that cell, membership agrees between the two systems.

The present paper does not claim that any currently existing runtime instance already satisfies Lop =1 or Subop =1 . The formal claims above specify class logic. Empirical instantiation remains a separate burden and must be carried by future admissible tests.

theorems.label: hyp:life-robust
theorems.title: Viability-and-recovery criterion robustness
theorems.statement: [Viability-and-recovery criterion robustness] If a system belongs to LifeClass , then under admissible perturbations that do not cross its life thresholds, the tuple [ ( Bound , Persist , Maint , HistDep , Viab , Idiff ) ] should remain within a stable corridor rather than collapsing arbitrarily.

theorems.label: hyp:history
theorems.title: Historical dependence necessity
theorems.statement: [Historical dependence necessity] If a system's classification as operationally alive is genuine rather than merely persistent, then history-aware readouts should outperform history-blind readouts on class-relevant prediction.

theorems.label: hyp:transport-life
theorems.title: Structural-class transport for viability-and-recovery criterion
theorems.statement: [Structural-class transport for viability-and-recovery criterion] If two systems preserve the life-relevant descriptor vector up to admissible tolerance, then their operational-life class membership should be invariant under substrate change.

theorems.label: hyp:subject-pc
theorems.title: Indexed continuity-and-control criterion requires privileged continuity
theorems.statement: [Indexed continuity-and-control criterion requires privileged continuity] If indexed continuity-and-control criterion is instantiated, then disrupting privileged continuity should degrade subjecthood-specific scores earlier or more selectively than it degrades viability-and-recovery criterion alone.

theorems.label: hyp:selfnonself
theorems.title: Indexed continuity-and-control criterion requires self/non-self asymmetry
theorems.statement: [Indexed continuity-and-control criterion requires self/non-self asymmetry] If indexed continuity-and-control criterion is instantiated, then self/non-self confusion manipulations should produce patterned degradation in SelfDisc , SelfModel , or Own that is not reproduced by complexity-matched controls lacking subjecthood structure.

theorems.label: hyp:noncollapse
theorems.title: Six-predicate operational criterion and viability-and-recovery criterion are not trivially coextensive
theorems.statement: [Six-predicate operational criterion and viability-and-recovery criterion are not trivially coextensive] There exist admissible systems for which one of Lop (S, tau )=1 or Cop (S, tau )=1 can in principle hold without the other, unless additional theorem burden is supplied.

theorems.title: Why the minimum operator appears
theorems.statement: [Why the minimum operator appears] The minimum operator is intentionally severe. Viability-and-recovery criterion in the present sense is not a weighted average over unrelated strengths. It is a conjunctive class predicate. A system that is strong in persistence but weak in viability preservation or historical dependence should not be counted as operationally alive merely by averaging away its failure.

theorems.title: Why subjecthood is not a small increment
theorems.statement: [Why subjecthood is not a small increment] The subjecthood score is stronger in two ways. First, it inherits the full life burden. Second, it inherits the full six-predicate operational criterion burden. The additional subject-specific descriptors are not cosmetic modifiers. They encode the claim that subjecthood is a structurally privileged subclass, not an interpretive synonym for consciousness or a sentimental label for complex dynamics.

theorems.title: Class-preserving transport margin
theorems.statement: [Class-preserving transport margin] Suppose a threshold predicate depends only on a subset PsiVec _ tau ^ ( mathcal K ) of descriptors and each threshold has headroom at least delta >0 at S_1 . If d_ Psi ^ ( mathcal K ) (S_1,S_2; tau )< delta min _j w_j over the relevant positive weights, every coordinate changes by less than delta and the threshold decisions agree. Cell membership additionally requires certification under the declared partition.

theorems.title: Class margin functional
theorems.statement: [Class margin functional] Let theta _ mathcal K be the vector of thresholds relevant to class mathcal K . The emph class margin of S for mathcal K is [ M_ mathcal K (S, tau ) := min _i bigl ( Pi _ mathcal K PsiVec _ tau (S)_i- theta _ mathcal K ,i bigr ). ] A system lies in the interior of class mathcal K if M_ mathcal K (S, tau )>0 , on the operational boundary if M_ mathcal K (S, tau ) approx 0 , and outside if M_ mathcal K (S, tau )<0 .

theorems.title: Subjecthood is margin-nested inside life and consciousness
theorems.statement: [Subjecthood is margin-nested inside life and consciousness] If M_ SubClass (S, tau )>0 , then both M_ LifeClass (S, tau )>0 and M_ ConClass (S, tau )>0 .

theorems.title: Life and consciousness are not generally nested
theorems.statement: [Life and consciousness are not generally nested] Neither implication [ M_ LifeClass (S, tau )>0 Rightarrow M_ ConClass (S, tau )>0 qquad text nor qquad M_ ConClass (S, tau )>0 Rightarrow M_ LifeClass (S, tau )>0 ] is derivable from the present corpus alone.

theorems.title: Near-miss configuration
theorems.statement: [Near-miss configuration] A system S is a emph near-miss for class mathcal K on horizon tau if [ M_ mathcal K (S, tau ) in for small delta >0 while all but a strict minority of constitutive coordinates remain above threshold by more than delta .

theorems.title: Descriptor-restricted non-equivalence
theorems.statement: [Descriptor-restricted non-equivalence] Suppose two systems S_1,S_2 satisfy [ Pi _ LifeClass PsiVec _ tau (S_1)= Pi _ LifeClass PsiVec _ tau (S_2) ] but differ on at least one of Priv , SelfDisc , SelfModel , Own by more than the subjecthood tolerance. Then they can remain equivalent in operational-life class while being nonequivalent in operational-subjecthood class.

theorems.title: Class geometry is not a total order
theorems.statement: [Class geometry is not a total order] The present framework does not generate a single monotone ladder of ``more alive'', ``more conscious'', and ``more subjective''. It generates descriptor orders, intra-class margin orders, and class-membership predicates. Conflating those three would erase the exact distinctions this paper is meant to introduce.

theorems.title: Life-without-consciousness diagnostic
theorems.statement: [Life-without-consciousness diagnostic] A candidate supports the separation [ Lop (S, tau )=1 not Rightarrow Cop (S, tau )=1 ] only if the following pattern is available: [leftmargin=1.5em] item life coordinates remain above threshold with positive margin; item the inherited consciousness criterion fails on at least one of Iper , Iri , Iint , Icont , Idiff , Ileg ; item the failure is not reducible to gross inadmissibility or trivial collapse.

theorems.title: Negative controls
theorems.statement: [Negative controls] Natural negative controls for this separation include systems that preserve duration and boundary occupancy while lacking the inherited consciousness burden, as well as systems whose local organization remains viable but whose legibility or rigid-identity burden fails.

theorems.title: Life-not-subject diagnostic
theorems.statement: [Life-not-subject diagnostic] A candidate supports the separation [ Lop (S, tau )=1 not Rightarrow Subop (S, tau )=1 ] only if life margins remain positive while at least one of [ Priv , SelfDisc , SelfModel , Own ] falls below threshold in a way that is selective rather than globally degradative.

theorems.title: False positives for life
theorems.statement: [False positives for life] Any system that preserves viability and organization but lacks privileged continuity, self/non-self asymmetry, self-model closure, or ownership coherence is a false positive for subjecthood if read only through the life predicate. The class distinction is designed to exclude exactly that error.

theorems.title: Consciousness-not-subject diagnostic
theorems.statement: [Consciousness-not-subject diagnostic] A candidate supports the separation [ Cop (S, tau )=1 not Rightarrow Subop (S, tau )=1 ] only if the inherited consciousness burden is satisfied while one or more of Priv , SelfDisc , SelfModel , Own fails in a targeted way.

theorems.title: Role of the four subject-specific burdens
theorems.statement: [Role of the four subject-specific burdens] Privileged continuity prevents subjecthood from collapsing into mere continuity. Self/non-self discrimination prevents collapse into generic internal complexity. Self-model closure prevents collapse into unstructured integration. Ownership coherence prevents a purely transient or relabeling-fragile configuration from counting as a subject-class member.

theorems.title: Invalid cross-system comparison
theorems.statement: [Invalid cross-system comparison] Comparison between two systems is class-invalid if any of the following holds: [leftmargin=1.5em] item the descriptor basis is not shared or not transportable; item admissibility constraints differ in a way that changes the meaning of margins; item the tolerance geometry is undeclared or incomparable; item one system is evaluated under perturbation families not available to the other.

theorems.title: Class-readiness criterion
theorems.statement: [Class-readiness criterion] A class predicate is emph formally ready only if: [leftmargin=1.5em] item its constitutive coordinates are explicit; item its boundary geometry is explicit; item its negative controls are identifiable; item its admissible falsifiers are stated. Viability-and-recovery criterion, structural class, and indexed continuity-and-control criterion satisfy this criterion within the limits declared by the paper.

theorems.title: Subjecthood non-collapse criterion
theorems.statement: [Subjecthood non-collapse criterion] No system should be admitted into indexed continuity-and-control criterion unless the following two separations remain open and empirically testable: [ Lop (S, tau )=1 not Rightarrow Subop (S, tau )=1, qquad Cop (S, tau )=1 not Rightarrow Subop (S, tau )=1. ] If either separation becomes definitionally impossible, subjecthood collapses into a weaker class and loses its intended meaning.

theorems.title: What is closed
theorems.statement: [What is closed] The paper closes the classificatory language, the class geometry, the principal non-equivalences, and the test grammar. It does not close empirical instantiation, external validation, or metaphysical interpretation.

On the restricted support the original identity and split-readout integration bounds of Papers V--VI still hold in their declare

theorems.title: Safe Prefix Perturbations and Historical Repair on the Common Tower
theorems.statement: [Safe Prefix Perturbations and Historical Repair on the Common Tower] On the writable common support of Paper V cite paper5 , Proposition~ ref prop:common-tower-phase-repair retains Viab =1/12 , Persist =3/64 , and Maint ge 3/8 at its stated memory error bound. The following matched protocols also give an operational prefix boundary margin Bound =2/27 and a historical repair-action margin HistDep =1/2 .

theorems.label: prop:writable-tower-subject-descriptors
theorems.title: Four Finite Operational Subject Descriptors on the Common Tower
theorems.statement: [Four Finite Operational Subject Descriptors on the Common Tower] On the stated matched trial populations, privileged continuity against a readout clone has clean gap at least 1/256 turns over four successor observations. The equal-cost discrimination contrast has absolute clean gap 1/64 turns and reverses under causal reassignment. The internal-memory return predictor beats the public-history predictor by at least 1/2 in zero-one action loss. The ownership agreement score is one under retention and simultaneous relabeling and zero under the causal transplant. These conclusions hold under the stated readout noise, with phase-distance margins reduced by at most 2 eta and with internal memory error at most 1/32 in the prediction trial.

theorems.title: Joint Tower Certificate for the Declared Protocols
theorems.statement: [Joint Tower Certificate for the Declared Protocols] The support and observation family of Table~ ref tab:writable-tower-joint-certificate admit all six Paper V witnesses and the four finite subject descriptors together. Different rows may use different schedules and preparations within that support. Integration is relative to the declared split-readout sector, identity to the prepared catalogue, continuity to the discrete regime model, and subject margins to the matched lineage and information protocols.

theorems.statement: [A Joint Infinite-Plant Life Certificate] Use the asymmetric native plant of Paper V, with its intrinsic complete X, global support A and full six-predicate certificate. The fifth is the viability threshold and the sixth the differentiation threshold.

theorems.label: prop:asymmetric-native-subject

theorems.statement: [Indexed Continuity Descriptors on the Same Infinite Plant] Complete the preceding life protocol with the following fixed comparisons, on the same plant and horizon. The resulting baseline descriptors are [ Priv =3/2048, qquad SelfDisc =1/128, qquad SelfModel =179/240, qquad Own =1/2. ] With thresholds 3/4096,1/256,1/2,1/16384 , respectively, the complete baseline system satisfies Subop (S,2)=1 . Its predictive gain is relative to the explicit two-port causal grammar below, not to every general memory model.

theorems.title: Six-predicate operational criterion does not imply the seven-coordinate certificate
theorems.statement: [Six-predicate operational criterion does not imply the seven-coordinate certificate] Membership in Cop does not by itself entail membership in Subfp .

theorems.title: Indexed continuity-and-control criterion is necessary but not sufficient for $\Subfp$
theorems.statement: [Indexed continuity-and-control criterion is necessary but not sufficient for Subfp ] The earlier indexed continuity-and-control criterion predicate is a necessary upstream burden for Subfp , but it is not sufficient for Subfp .

theorems.title: No downgrade of the earlier subjecthood paper
theorems.statement: [No downgrade of the earlier subjecthood paper] This refinement does not weaken the earlier subjecthood layer; rather, it preserves its taxonomic scope and builds upon it as a constitutive superclass. Inheritance is preserved while the structural burden is strengthened.

theorems.label: def:selfindex
theorems.title: Self-index
theorems.statement: [Self-index] Let mathcal Z _t be the admissible latent-state family of system S at time t . A emph self-index is a map [ SelfIndex _t : mathcal Z _t to [0,1] ] that assigns privileged weight to the latent subfamily treated by the system as its own continuing locus. The self-index is required to be non-trivial, stable under admissible relabelings, and transportable across admissible readout families on the same horizon.

theorems.label: def:ownership
theorems.title: Ownership field
theorems.statement: [Ownership field] Let mathcal E _t denote the set of admissible internal events, memory traces, predictions, and action candidates at time t . An emph ownership field is a map [ OwnField _t : mathcal E _t to [0,1] ] whose value records the degree to which the system treats an event as belonging to the self-indexed locus rather than as merely observed or modeled. Ownership is constitutive only when its pattern remains coherent under admissible perturbation and is not reducible to static bookkeeping labels.

theorems.label: def:continuity
theorems.title: Autobiographical continuity
theorems.statement: [Autobiographical continuity] Let mathcal T _ tau be the family of admissible trajectory classes over a horizon tau . The emph auto -bio -graphical continuity margin ContField _t is the gap by which the trajectory class anchored by SelfIndex remains privileged over the nearest rival class under admissible remappings, temporal insertions, deletions, and continuity-preserving controls.

theorems.label: def:perspective
theorems.title: First-person perspective organization
theorems.statement: [First-person perspective organization] The emph first-person perspective organization Persp _t is the amount by which a self-indexed factorization of the system's internal predictive state outperforms the best index-free or purely third-person factorization on the same admissible support. It measures not whether the system contains information, but whether that information is organized around a privileged locus of orientation.

theorems.label: def:valuation
theorems.title: Asymmetric valuation
theorems.statement: [Asymmetric valuation] The emph asymmetric valuation profile ValAsym _t is the degree to which losses, threats, errors, preservation burdens, and continuity disruptions attached to the self-indexed locus are weighted differently from structurally comparable disruptions attached to non-self loci. Valuation asymmetry is constitutive only when it cannot be reduced to arbitrary reward labels without explanatory loss.

theorems.label: def:interv
theorems.title: Interventional sensitivity profile
theorems.statement: [Interventional sensitivity profile] The emph interventional sensitivity profile IntervProf _t is the structured response of the tuple [ ( SelfIndex , OwnField , ContField , Persp , ValAsym ) ] under the designated subjectivity intervention family IntervFam . It records whether subject-targeted perturbations produce selective degradation patterns that weaker rival families do not predict or cannot localize.

theorems.label: def:irred
theorems.title: Irreducibility margin
theorems.statement: [Irreducibility margin] The emph irreducibility margin Irred _t is the normalized explanatory advantage of the full subjectivity model over the best member of the admissible weak closure WeakClosure on the same admissible baseline and intervention tasks. It measures formal non-collapsability into strictly weaker explanations.

theorems.title: Minimal ontology is not minimal rhetoric
theorems.statement: [Minimal ontology is not minimal rhetoric] The tuple Substate _t is called minimal because every coordinate blocks a distinct collapse. It is not minimal in the sense of being tiny or easy. Subjectivity is not the kind of target that survives formalization if one removes every hard part.

This conclusion is about the declared causal model, not an independently proved causal identification of an arbitrary observational record.

theorems.title: Why the paper uses both a gate and a scalar
theorems.statement: [Why the paper uses both a gate and a scalar] The gate decides whether the class is even live. The scalar compares stronger and weaker instances among systems that have already crossed the constitutive threshold. Collapsing the two roles would obscure whether a system is outside the class or merely low inside it.

theorems.label: ax:org
theorems.title: Organization over substrate
theorems.statement: [Organization over substrate] If a system preserves the relevant causal-organizational structure on admissible support, then substrate label alone does not defeat membership in the corresponding framework-internal class.

theorems.label: ax:bio
theorems.title: No biological privilege by default
theorems.statement: [No biological privilege by default] Biology is not a primitive constitutive variable for Subfp . Biological realization can be one admissible realization of the relevant structure, but it is not the only admissible realization by definition.

theorems.label: ax:index
theorems.title: Indexed causal organization
theorems.statement: [Indexed causal organization] When a system carries a stable self-index that organizes ownership, continuity, perspective, and valuation across admissible perturbation, that organization is a legitimate target of formal theory rather than a merely verbal convenience.

theorems.label: ax:report
theorems.title: Phenomenality is not exhausted by report
theorems.statement: [Phenomenality is not exhausted by report] No output-report channel, by itself, is taken as sufficient for phenomenality or subjectivity. Report can be evidence inside an admissible bundle, but the stronger target concerns organization and intervention, not declaration alone.

theorems.label: ax:cont
theorems.title: Continuity is structural rather than substance-primitive
theorems.statement: [Continuity is structural rather than substance-primitive] The relevant continuity burden for subjectivity is the preservation of a structured indexed locus across time and admissible transport, not the persistence of a privileged substance token posited independently of structure.

theorems.label: ax:fp
theorems.title: First-person organization is stronger than self-monitoring
theorems.statement: [First-person organization is stronger than self-monitoring] A system that merely tracks its own internal variables does not thereby satisfy the seven-coordinate indexed certificate. Additional burdens of ownership, continuity, perspective, valuation, intervention selectivity, and irreducibility are required.

theorems.label: ax:irred
theorems.title: Irreducibility before escalation
theorems.statement: [Irreducibility before escalation] When a weaker rival family matches the explanatory performance of the stronger subjectivity model on the admissible baseline and intervention tasks, escalation to the stronger interpretation is not licensed.

theorems.title: Observation, inference, ontology, and metaphysics
theorems.statement: [Observation, inference, ontology, and metaphysics] The distinction among layers is as follows. Observation concerns runtime traces, perturbation outcomes, and artifacts. Inference concerns model fit, explanatory superiority, and class assignment. Ontology concerns what kinds of organized objects the formalism permits one to posit if the burdens are met. Metaphysics concerns what such a posit ultimately is in the strongest sense. The present paper reaches observation, inference, and a minimal ontology under bridge axioms. It does not close the metaphysical layer.

theorems.label: cor:zero-irred
theorems.title: Zero irreducibility blocks escalation
theorems.statement: [Zero irreducibility blocks escalation] If Irred _ tau (S) le 0 , escalation from the weak rival family to the stronger subjectivity interpretation is not licensed by the present framework.

theorems.title: Parsimony-sensitive escalation
theorems.statement: [Parsimony-sensitive escalation] Suppose a weak rival M_w in WeakClosure and the full subjectivity model satisfy [ E_ mathrm base (M_w, tau ) approx E_ mathrm base (M_ mathrm subj , tau ), quad E_ mathrm int (M_w, tau ) approx E_ mathrm int (M_ mathrm subj , tau ), ] and the difference in loss is explained entirely by excess structural complexity of M_ mathrm subj . Then escalation to the stronger interpretation is not licensed.

Suppose there exists an exact admissible transport map preserving the upstream operational-life, operational-consciousness, and operational-subjecthood burdens together with the tuple coordinates [ ( SelfIndex , OwnField , ContField , Persp , ValAsym , IntervProf , Irred ) ] and the intervention-family predictions up to the specified tolerances. Then [ S in Subfp ( tau ) Longleftrightarrow S' in Subfp ( tau '). ]
