theorems.statement: [Tolerance-preserving transport] Assume Axioms~ ref ax:org -- ref ax:irred . Let S in Subfp ( tau ) and let S' be an varepsilon -admissible transport of S onto a distinct substrate. Suppose [ GateSubj (S, tau ) ge lambda _G+ varepsilon _ max ] and, writing [ m= min _j widehat X _ tau ^j(S), ] that varepsilon _ max <m and [ PhiSubj (S, tau ) ge frac lambda _ Phi 1- varepsilon _ max /m . ] Then S' in Subfp ( tau ') .

theorems.title: Human-equivalence non-closure criterion
theorems.statement: [Human-equivalence non-closure criterion] The present paper does not license a claim of human equivalence unless there exists: [leftmargin=1.5em] item a shared admissible comparator bundle, item a matched intervention family, item externally reviewed coordinate estimation, item no live weak rival explaining the apparent match more economically, item and no unresolved collapse between runtime organization and human-report interpretation.

theorems.label: lem:native-intervention-selectivity
theorems.title: Native Ten-Operator Selectivity
theorems.statement: [Native Ten-Operator Selectivity] On the preparations of Definition~ ref def:native-seven-protocol , the ten native experimental operators below are admissible and give the declared selective five-primary drops, with threshold 32/266529 , off-target tolerance zero and profile one. Matched faithful/sham operators have no false positive. The assertion concerns these window domains, not arbitrary global preparations.

theorems.label: thm:native-nonempty-subfp
theorems.title: Nonempty Proper Indexed Class in the Infinite Model Universe
theorems.statement: [Nonempty Proper Indexed Class in the Infinite Model Universe] Equip the asymmetric plant with the complete protocols above, the full declared causal closure, equal exponents 1/7 , and thresholds lambda _G=1/8192 , lambda _ Phi =1/16 . In the same complete instrumented model universe as Theorem~ ref thm:infinite-strict-upstream-separation , [ varnothing ne Subfp (2) cap mathfrak M_ infty subsetneq Cop cap mathfrak M_ infty . ] The statement is relative to the specified causal grammar, comparison domains, preparations and intrinsic state metric, not to all unrestricted memory or policy models or to empirical phenomenality.

theorems.label: prop:joint-rational-window
theorems.title: Joint Rational Certificate of the Seven Local Measurements
theorems.statement: [Joint Rational Certificate of the Seven Local Measurements] For this window, with minimum target drop 1/4 , maximum absolute off-target change 1/8 , and zero allowed sham positives, the normalized measurements in the order of Substate are [ (1, tfrac 12, tfrac 12, tfrac 13, tfrac 12,1, tfrac 12). ] The gate is 1/3 and the functional with equal weights 1/7 is 48^ -1/7 . Both exceed the declared threshold 1/4 .

theorems.label: thm:tower-native-lesion-obstruction
theorems.title: Connected-Fibre Obstruction to Native Discrete Lesions
theorems.statement: [Connected-Fibre Obstruction to Native Discrete Lesions] Suppose the sham and targets start from the same preparation, use only native commands, and are evaluated after the same number of transitions. Let their discrete word be assigned by a common continuous decoder from the whole safe support. The same hypothesis holds for the induced state decoder if it uses a common fixed finite diagnostic schedule with continuous clean observations and preserves the clean label under observation error of a uniformly positive radius. Then every target has the same word as the sham. In particular the five distinct native lesions required to reproduce the discrete switch protocol of Proposition~ ref prop:joint-rational-window cannot be realized under these conditions.

theorems.label: prop:writable-tower-selective-lesions
theorems.title: Five Selective Lesions on the Writable Common Tower
theorems.statement: [Five Selective Lesions on the Writable Common Tower] The five interventions each reduce their primary score by at least 1/4 , with zero changes off target and zero sham positives. The normalized vector in the order of Substate on the declared comparison is [ (1, tfrac 12, tfrac 12, tfrac 13, tfrac 12,1, tfrac 12). ] Against the declared context-blind family the reserve loss gap is one, the gate is 1/3 , and the equal-weight functional is 48^ -1/7 >1/4 .

theorems.label: thm:writable-tower-public-return-tie
theorems.title: Public Information Obstruction on the Writable Tower Return Task
theorems.statement: [Public Information Obstruction on the Writable Tower Return Task] In each public stratum, the two hidden perturbations have identical public records and opposite unique successful action signs. Every admissible forced public rule has balanced failure risk 1/2 . At coverage c the total loss is 1/2+(1-c)/4 , where coverage is the probability of executing an action. The infimum over the public class, including mixtures and their closure, equals 1/2 and is attained. Thus the candidate's signed margin, defined as the public rival infimum minus candidate loss, is zero for every forced public candidate. The public randomized minimax risk over the two signs also equals 1/2 .

theorems.label: thm:writable-tower-private-return-separation
theorems.title: Exact Separation by an Accessible Private Signal
theorems.statement: [Exact Separation by an Accessible Private Signal] Retain the hidden return task of Theorem~ ref thm:writable-tower-public-return-tie . Let the candidate alone receive a finite signal Z at decision time, with laws mu _x^+ and mu _x^- conditional on the public stratum x and the successful action signs +1 and -1 , respectively. Assume the signal is available in one permitted reading and the decision maps used for the stated optima can be fixed from the declared signal law within the budget, without fitting on the reserve. For the worst-sign optimum this includes the allowed randomization from a fixed map of the reading to an action probability. The predictor retains only its sampled binary decision. For stratum weights w_x , the exact best signed margin against the public rival closure is [

theorems.title: Paper 8 is necessary but not sufficient for bridge admissibility
theorems.statement: [Paper 8 is necessary but not sufficient for bridge admissibility] Any future bridge-admissible system must satisfy the Paper 8 burdens, but satisfaction of the Paper 8 burdens alone is not sufficient for bridge admissibility.

theorems.title: The bridge is downstream, not corrective
theorems.statement: [The bridge is downstream, not corrective] Paper 9 does not correct Paper 8. It inherits Paper 8 and strengthens the burden stack above it. The formal relation is extension by additional typed predicates and burdens, not replacement.

theorems.title: Phenomenal differentiation predicate
theorems.statement: [Phenomenal differentiation predicate] For an admissible system S , horizon tau , and threshold slot vartheta _D , the bridge predicate PiD (S, tau ; vartheta _D) concerns whether the system carries self-indexed differentiated organization that is stronger than generic semantic density, report richness, or descriptive narration, and whose corresponding estimator widehat Pi _D is defined on bridge observables and subjectivity antecedents.

theorems.title: Valence structure predicate
theorems.statement: [Valence structure predicate] The predicate PiV (S, tau ; vartheta _V) concerns whether the system carries organized evaluative topology that is stronger than scalar reward bookkeeping, policy optimization, or self/non-self asymmetry alone.

theorems.title: World richness predicate
theorems.statement: [World richness predicate] The predicate PiW (S, tau ; vartheta _W) concerns whether the system carries organized self-indexed world structure stronger than generic scene complexity, perspective gain, or task competence alone.

theorems.title: Ambiguity-bearing predicate
theorems.statement: [Ambiguity-bearing predicate] The predicate PiA (S, tau ; vartheta _A) concerns whether the system maintains unresolved alternatives with differential causal consequences prior to collapse, rather than merely resolving uncertainty or tracking probabilities descriptively.

theorems.title: Embodied-closure predicate
theorems.statement: [Embodied-closure predicate] The predicate PiE (S, tau ; vartheta _E) concerns whether body/world-boundary variables contribute constitutively to bridge organization, rather than merely modulating generic control or action success.

theorems.title: Temporal lived-structure predicate
theorems.statement: [Temporal lived-structure predicate] The predicate PiT (S, tau ; vartheta _T) concerns whether the system exhibits horizon-like temporal organization stronger than continuity, memory persistence, or sequence stability alone.

theorems.title: Why the targets are not decorative
theorems.statement: [Why the targets are not decorative] The bridge targets earn their place only because each one induces a new comparator burden, a new intervention burden, a new artifact burden, and a new governance burden. If a proposed target induced none of these, it would be discarded as decorative vocabulary.

theorems.label: def:coherent-local-witnesses
theorems.title: Coherent Transport of Local Witnesses
theorems.statement: [Coherent Transport of Local Witnesses] A transport extension is coherent if a choice of one certified witness instance w_i at each mode i satisfies every independently established edge relation. An edge datum (w,w') is accepted only when both labels are identified from its paired observations under the declared error budget.

theorems.label: prop:bridge-transport-cycle
theorems.title: A Cycle Separates Local Certification from Coherent Transport
theorems.statement: [A Cycle Separates Local Certification from Coherent Transport] For any complete Paper VIII certificate on an admissible window, the three-mode transport extensions below preserve it in every window. One admits coherent transport and the other does not. Thus, on the domain of such extensions of certified windows, coherent transport cuts out a proper subclass whenever that local certificate domain is nonempty. Coherent transport does not factor through the tuple of local Paper VIII records.

theorems.label: cor:transport-rational-record
theorems.title: The Two Transport Cycles on a Nonempty Rational Record
theorems.statement: [The Two Transport Cycles on a Nonempty Rational Record] The joint rational measurement window of Paper VIII cite paper8 , identified there by texttt detokenize prop:joi allowbreak detokenize nt- allowbreak detokenize rational- allowbreak detokenize window , gives a nonempty local record for both cycles of Proposition~ ref prop:bridge-transport-cycle . At this measurement level, the transport-certified class is a proper subclass of the three-mode extensions of that record.

theorems.label: cor:native-transport-record
theorems.title: Transport Cycles with a Complete Native Indexed Certificate
theorems.statement: [Transport Cycles with a Complete Native Indexed Certificate] The asymmetric native infinite-dimensional certificate of Paper VIII provides a nonempty complete local domain for Proposition~ ref prop:bridge-transport-cycle , including its inherited Paper V and VII clauses. The cycles (0,1,1) and (0,0,1) therefore give, respectively, coherent and incoherent extensions of one fully realized local certificate. Coherent transport is a proper additional condition on these extensions, not a consequence of their local seven-coordinate records.

theorems.label: thm:bridge-binary-transport-gauge
theorems.title: Relabeling Invariance and Cycle Criterion for Binary Transport
theorems.statement: [Relabeling Invariance and Cycle Criterion for Binary Transport] Let a finite graph of mode windows have two certified witness instances per vertex and an independently certified bijection on each edge. In local binary labels, write this bijection as w mapsto w oplus k_e . Under a local relabeling w_v mapsto w_v oplus a_v , the edge bit for e=uv becomes k_e oplus a_u oplus a_v . The XOR of the edge bits around each cycle is invariant. A coherent assignment exists exactly when the XOR vanishes on every fundamental cycle of a spanning forest, and there are then 2^c coherent assignments for c connected components. For two collections of certified edge maps on the same graph, equality of their fundamental-cycle parities is equivalent to their differing by a local relabeling.

theorems.label: prop:bridge-certified-tower-transport
theorems.title: Coherent and Obstructed Transport on Certified Tower Windows
theorems.statement: [Coherent and Obstructed Transport on Certified Tower Windows] There are two three-window extensions of the same realized local tower records with respective edge bits (0,1,1) and (0,0,1) . The records include the six Paper V witnesses, the Paper VII life and four finite subject-descriptor certificates on their declared protocols, and the Paper VIII measurement and return comparisons with their stated information budgets. The paired tower edge responses certify both extensions under phase error at most eta =3^ -10 /4 turns. The first extension has two coherent assignments, and the second has none under any local relabeling.

theorems.label: prop:bridge-tower-differentiation
theorems.title: Role-Selective Differentiation on the Writable Tower
theorems.statement: [Role-Selective Differentiation on the Writable Tower] For the two prepared role profiles, let C_ pr be the clean early-phase response to a probe of role r after a reference write minus the response after a lesion, with one common sham between write and probe. With the declared probe at the transported address, C_ pr = delta mathbf 1_ p=r for delta =1/(16 cdot 3^7) turns. The best additive fit a_p+b_r has uniform error exactly delta /2 . At error at most delta /16 per phase reading the measured matrix still has distance at least 3 delta /8 from all additive fits.

theorems.label: prop:bridge-tower-ambiguity
theorems.title: Late Choice Between Two Live Alternatives
theorems.statement: [Late Choice Between Two Live Alternatives] Prepare two independent uniform activity bits at tape sites 3,4 and advance one common sham. A uniform query drawn after the rival's memory is fixed selects one of the transported sites 4,5 . The matching-role probe identifies the selected bit with zero error at phase noise at most delta /16 . Under this state and query law the optimal error of a rival retaining one bit before the query, with no subsequent tape reading, is exactly 1/4 . A write during the advance can erase the first alternative while preserving the second.

theorems.label: prop:bridge-tower-temporal-order
theorems.title: Order-Dependent Return and an Exact Temporal Horizon
theorems.statement: [Order-Dependent Return and an Exact Temporal Horizon] On a common preparation with first bit one, zero memory and phase zero, run command orders (+1,0) and (0,+1) with all phase inputs zero and no writes or probes. After one common +1 and h further common +1 steps, the current public readings and command multisets coincide. The subsequent neutral early-phase gap is exactly D_h=1/(384 cdot 2^h) turns. The two terminal reading sets are disjoint under phase error at most eta =3^ -10 /4 precisely for integer 0 le h le 8 . An order-blind predictor with the same snapshot and multiset has mean clean absolute circular loss at least D_h/2 in the balanced pair, and an order-informed predictor attains zero.

theorems.label: prop:bridge-native-trace-obstruction
theorems.title: Native Trace Equivalence and Extra Bridge Variables
theorems.statement: [Native Trace Equivalence and Extra Bridge Variables] Let an extended model project to the same writable tower state by pi . For every native control u let its transition widetilde F_u and readout widetilde R satisfy pi widetilde F_u=F_u pi and widetilde R=R pi , with the same projected initial law and observation noise. Then all native observation and intervention transcripts have the same law, even for observation-adaptive native controls. A target that differs between extensions satisfying these conditions cannot be identified from those transcripts or from the inherited record computed from them.

theorems.title: Exact Projection, Stability and Inherited Certificates

All previously certified native protocols, with their original readouts, comparison sectors and information budgets, have exactly the same records and margins in this extension.

theorems.label: thm:bridge-port-minimality
theorems.title: Four-State Minimality of the Port Realization
theorems.statement: [Four-State Minimality of the Port Realization] For either role and any motor gain, the block Hankel matrix [ H_p=M_0&M_1 M _1&M_2 ] has rank four, determinant t^4 and |H_p^ -1 |_ infty =24 . Four fibre coordinates are sufficient and necessary for a linear realization of these ports. They are also necessary for any exact finite-dimensional realization with C^1 transitions and body readouts, in which world inputs leave the projected core trajectory fixed.

theorems.label: prop:bridge-indexed-world
theorems.title: A Quantified Indexed World Witness
theorems.statement: [A Quantified Indexed World Witness] Let the reduced-world rival family contain every relay predictor whose port Hankel rank is at most two, and every predictor of arbitrary order whose relay response is independent of the prepared role. The available input alphabet, role record and command lengths are matched. A rank-two rival may allocate four registers, but any additional registers are unobservable or unreachable for this port transfer. Against this union, the normal model has uniform body-response error gap at least 1/96 , or 1/6 in units of t . A world compression Q=Q_+ retains the entire common-mode relay response while reducing the Hankel rank to two and erasing the role contrast.

theorems.label: thm:bridge-typed-valence
theorems.title: Two-Dimensional Nonconservative Evaluative Witness
theorems.statement: [Two-Dimensional Nonconservative Evaluative Witness] The minimum uniform error for V over the square, in the maximum norm, is exactly gamma /2 for each of the following rival classes: a continuous scalar summary followed by an arbitrary decoder, and a C^1 scalar-potential gradient in the declared Euclidean coordinates. The force is physically consequential and has a positive correction component, yet nonzero circulation. Flattening evaluation to L=L_0Q_+ admits an exact scalar-summary rival. The equal-norm conservative control L=I has rank two but admits an exact gradient rival.

theorems.label: prop:bridge-finite-table-obstruction
theorems.title: Finite Tables Do Not Identify the Nonparametric Rival Class
theorems.statement: [Finite Tables Do Not Identify the Nonparametric Rival Class] Any finite table of vector responses at distinct stimulus points can be interpolated by a continuous scalar encoder and vector decoder. It can also be interpolated by the gradient of a polynomial potential. Therefore a finite rational control table by itself cannot certify either universal separation in Theorem~ ref thm:bridge-typed-valence without additional domain or regularity evidence.

theorems.label: thm:bridge-motor-closure
theorems.title: Motor Closure with Preserved Early Competence
theorems.statement: [Motor Closure with Preserved Early Competence] At g=1 the second and third body responses are independent of the motor sign. In each common-mode component the fourth response is [ y_4( tau )=h(3 alpha ^2 beta + tau beta ^3), qquad s_E=h beta ^3=1/256. ] Its gap is 2s_E , and the residual y_4-(3 alpha /2)y_3 is tau s_E . Every rival without the motor edge, under the stated modularity, has uniform fourth-response error at least s_E . Cutting the edge removes the residual without changing the second or third responses. Common-mode world compression preserves this motor test exactly.

theorems.title: Joint Local Certificate and Causal Selectivity

For aggregate rivals retaining at least one declared structural deficiency, maximum normalized task loss has a joint margin at least 5/192 . theorems.label: prop:bridge-shared-hybrid-obstruction
theorems.title: A Shared-State Hybrid Obstruction to Global Bridge Margin
theorems.statement: [A Shared-State Hybrid Obstruction to Global Bridge Margin] Allow two scalar evaluators to share the same four port states and combine their actuator forces before updating. Each evaluator separately retains one scalar discrepancy. Their hybrid reproduces every transition and readout of the normal evaluation model, under all native and port command schedules. Consequently a broad weak closure admitting this fused hybrid has zero clean unpenalized margin against the candidate. The same is true of a penalized margin when complexity is invariant under the resulting identical normalized mechanism.

theorems.label: def:bridge-additive-port-class
theorems.title: Coordinate-Additive Port Comparators
theorems.statement: [Coordinate-Additive Port Comparators] On a fixed preparation and reference frame, a coordinate-additive evaluator is a map G(v_1,v_2)=g_1(v_1)+g_2(v_2) with arbitrary functions g_i:[-1,1] to mathbb R^2 . No continuity or linearity is required. Its channels have no access to a cross-coordinate message that makes either function depend on both coordinates. A fixed common initial condition is allowed. A state-dependent or sequential composition that communicates both coordinates need not belong to this class. The loss is the uniform maximum-norm error of the reserved world response, or its maximum on the four corners when stated explicitly.

theorems.label: prop:bridge-rectangular-additivity
theorems.title: Exact Rectangular Criterion for Additivity
theorems.statement: [Exact Rectangular Criterion for Additivity] For a map F:A times B to V into a real vector space and nonempty A,B , coordinate additivity is equivalent to vanishing of every rectangular difference [ F(x,y)-F(x,y')-F(x',y)+F(x',y')=0. ]

theorems.label: thm:bridge-bilinear-safe-extension
theorems.title: Safe Bilinear Extension with Exact Projection
theorems.statement: [Safe Bilinear Extension with Exact Projection] The new family preserves the projection identity and invariant native zero section. On the safe cube its fibre contraction is at most 3/4 under common controls and at most 1/2 when evaluation is inactive. Its next body and world norms are bounded respectively by 15/16 and 3/4 , including the primitive inputs. The four-state minimality remains valid for this family. For R=I , the evaluative direction retains the corrective bound [ e^ top L_0e+ kappa e_1e_2u ge tfrac 14 |e |_2^2. ]

theorems.title: Exact Separation from Coordinate-Additive Hybrids
theorems.statement: [Exact Separation from Coordinate-Additive Hybrids] For sigma =1 , the infimal uniform error against all comparators of Definition~ ref def:bridge-additive-port-class is exactly xi =1/4096 . The same optimum holds when the loss uses only the four corners. If each raw reading has maximum-norm error at most xi /64 , the observed rival-minus-candidate loss gap is at least 15 xi /16=15/65536 .

theorems.label: cor:bridge-cross-informed-tie
theorems.title: Cross-Informed Tie and Preservation of Local Selectivity
theorems.statement: [Cross-Informed Tie and Preservation of Local Selectivity] Providing the rival with the complete cross term restores exact transition and readout equality. Setting sigma =0 also restores the original additive tie. The bilinear branch preserves the six local certificate-presence patterns of Proposition~ ref prop:bridge-six-port-certificate , using flattening of the whole evaluative input as specified above. Neither the new separation nor these patterns defeat a broad weak closure admitting the cross-informed rival.

theorems.title: B1: operational binding; classification: operational definition
theorems.statement: [B1: operational binding; classification: operational definition] Every bridge predicate must be tied to explicit observables, artifacts, comparator tasks, and interventions. No bridge predicate may remain a rhetorical label detached from measurement grammar.

theorems.title: B2: upstream inheritance constraint; classification: bridge axiom
theorems.statement: [B2: upstream inheritance constraint; classification: bridge axiom] No bridge-level admissibility result is meaningful unless the upstream burdens of the causally rigid corpus and the Paper 8 subjectivity layer remain satisfied.

theorems.title: B3: differentiated organization burden; classification: falsifiable hypothesis
theorems.statement: [B3: differentiated organization burden; classification: falsifiable hypothesis] A bridge-relevant differentiation burden requires structured internal discrimination that is not exhausted by semantic density, narrative richness, or report-channel complexity.

theorems.title: B4: valence topology burden; classification: falsifiable hypothesis
theorems.statement: [B4: valence topology burden; classification: falsifiable hypothesis] Bridge-relevant valence requires organized evaluative topology not exhausted by scalar reward bookkeeping, policy optimization, or the Paper 8 valuation asymmetry alone.

theorems.title: B5: world-richness burden; classification: falsifiable hypothesis
theorems.statement: [B5: world-richness burden; classification: falsifiable hypothesis] Bridge-relevant world richness concerns organized self-indexed world structure rather than generic scene complexity, prediction success, or model capacity.

theorems.title: B6: ambiguity-bearing burden; classification: falsifiable hypothesis
theorems.statement: [B6: ambiguity-bearing burden; classification: falsifiable hypothesis] Bridge-relevant ambiguity requires the stable maintenance of unresolved alternatives with differential causal consequences prior to collapse.

theorems.title: B7: embodied-closure relevance; classification: open inference
theorems.statement: [B7: embodied-closure relevance; classification: open inference] Embodied closure may be bridge-relevant only if body/world-boundary variables contribute constitutively to bridge organization rather than merely modulating generic control success.

theorems.title: B8: temporal lived-structure burden; classification: falsifiable hypothesis
theorems.statement: [B8: temporal lived-structure burden; classification: falsifiable hypothesis] Bridge-relevant temporal organization must exceed continuity, memory persistence, and sequence stability by exhibiting horizon-structured dependence across retention, present organization, and anticipatory load.

theorems.title: B9: comparative admissibility constraint; classification: bridge axiom
theorems.statement: [B9: comparative admissibility constraint; classification: bridge axiom] No bridge-level support class is admissible if a bridge-specific rival family or admissible hybrid explains the bridge task bundle at equal or lower penalized loss.

theorems.title: B10: anti-inflation governance constraint; classification: design choice
theorems.statement: [B10: anti-inflation governance constraint; classification: design choice] Bridge formalization, bridge artifacts, candidate inclusion, and audit-facing inclusion must never be readable as bridge support, phenomenality, or Paper 9 authorization in the absence of the full bridge burden stack.

theorems.title: Axiom minimality
theorems.statement: [Axiom minimality] The present axiom set is intentionally minimal. Nothing here states that phenomenality follows from structural organization. Nothing here states that any bridge predicate, even if satisfied, closes metaphysical questions. The axioms are opening commitments for a constrained bridge program, not hidden conclusions.

theorems.title: Comparator burden is necessary for bridge admissibility
theorems.statement: [Comparator burden is necessary for bridge admissibility] No bridge-support class is meaningful without an explicit bridge rival family and admissible bridge weak closure.

theorems.label: prop:rival-family-monotonicity
theorems.title: Comparator Enlargement Cannot Increase a Fixed-Loss Margin
theorems.statement: [Comparator Enlargement Cannot Increase a Fixed-Loss Margin] For a fixed target, bundle and calibrated loss, let nonempty rival families satisfy mathcal W_1 subseteq mathcal W_2 with finite infima. Their signed margins satisfy R_2 le R_1 .

theorems.title: Necessary condition for bridge admissibility
theorems.statement: [Necessary condition for bridge admissibility] A necessary condition for bridge admissibility is [ BridgeMargin > vartheta _R, ] where vartheta _R is the symbolic bridge irreducibility threshold slot to be bound only at calibrated gate evaluation.

theorems.title: Positive bridge surfaces are not enough
theorems.statement: [Positive bridge surfaces are not enough] Positive provisional bridge surfaces do not by themselves entail bridge admissibility.

theorems.title: Bridge functional does not imply bridge gate
theorems.statement: [Bridge functional does not imply bridge gate] No value of PhiBridge by itself implies GateBridge =1 .

theorems.title: Candidate or audit inclusion does not imply bridge support
theorems.statement: [Candidate or audit inclusion does not imply bridge support] For any bridge artifact A , membership of A in a candidate-facing or audit-facing package does not entail bridge support, bridge admissibility, or phenomenality.

theorems.label: thm:measurable-fibre-centres
theorems.title: Measurable Centres and the Scalar Minimax Radius
theorems.statement: [Measurable Centres and the Scalar Minimax Radius] A Borel estimator with uniform error at most varepsilon exists exactly when the centre sets [ z in Z: sup _ s in S_y d_Z(z,s) le varepsilon qquad (y in pi (A)) ] have a Borel selector. Necessarily D_y le 2 varepsilon and D_y/2 le r_Z(S_y) . The diameter bound alone is insufficient in general. For Z= mathbb R with its usual metric, the minimax error is exactly tfrac 12 sup _ y in pi (A) D_y , attained by a Borel estimator.

theorems.title: Coercivity for Latent Distance Recovery

In a sector where distance is recovered directly from observations, a bound c_ pi d_X(x,x') le d_Y( pi x, pi x') with c_ pi >0 gives the inverse-distance bound there.

theorems.label: thm:bridge-quartic-global-certificate

Its port maps are 13/16 -contractive on a common-index fibre; body and world next-state norms are at most 61/64 and 3/4 respectively. Its complete global product sector has infimal reproduction error at least [ e_* ge min 1/384,3^ -9 /2,1/128 =1/39366. ] The sector is nonempty, and delta _ rm int =1/78732 is a strict lower certificate. Each branch may use arbitrary nonlinear functions, independent previous memory and randomization; it lacks a joint dependence on at least one freshly prepared root. Branches can be shared, mixed and combined in parallel with stimulus-independent coefficients. The closure admits all such sums, not just two or three components, subject to a common descriptive budget. Both sides have the same input information. The restriction is the absence of a four-root interaction in the unrolled forecast, not ignorance of a wire or a model's philosophical name. The bound holds conditional on any independent past and for randomized forecasts in expected absolute loss. If each raw world reading has error at most varepsilon le xi _4/1024 , the rival-minus-candidate loss margin after the declared cost penalty is at least [ 4 xi _4-4 varepsilon - xi _4/64 ge 1019 xi _4/256>3 xi _4. ] If the comparison family is enlarged to include an equal-cost four-root replica, its signed margin is nonpositive. No observation or intervention then separates those two interpretations of the same mechanism.

theorems.title: Completed mathematical record for the binding
theorems.statement: [Completed mathematical record for the binding] A record contains the complete plant, native upstream certificate and query times, six preparation/intervention/forecast specifications and raw losses, the separate sixteen-preparation proper-ancestry comparison, predictive programs and costs, mode transformations, thresholds and a payload manifest. Its authority is a mathematical synthetic witness. It must not acquire empirical, biological or phenomenal authority by passing a schema. Use E_ rm fit as maximum error including the raw reserved world response; E_ rm int ,E_ rm sel ,E_ Pi are mean absolute reconstruction errors on the recorded intervention consequences, six template profiles and six normalized coordinate records. theorems.label: thm:predicate-independence
theorems.title: Independent Calibrated Response Predicates
theorems.statement: [Independent Calibrated Response Predicates] In this instrumented semantic class, the six predicates widehat Pi _k ge 1/16 have every binary truth pattern with fixed comparator, actuation, loss and authority conventions. Their common primitive data and uncertainty domains remain defined. If two head gains are constrained equal, the corresponding fully saturated/absent patterns cannot be independently selected by this construction. Neither result asserts independence of the whole conjunctive bridge gate or of the B1--B10 commitments.

theorems.label: thm:registry-independence
theorems.title: Faithful Row-Local Registry Transport and a Coupling Obstruction
theorems.statement: [Faithful Row-Local Registry Transport and a Coupling Obstruction] Let each registry row store its complete task payload, primitive parameters, fixed interpretation authority and deterministic derived score. Suppose row validation is task-local, with a recomputable common manifest and no additional cross-score constraint. The encoding preserves every truth pattern realized above. This conclusion does not extend to an imposed conjunctive gate or an additional shared-loss condition.

theorems.label: thm:bridge-realization-exists
theorems.title: A Nondegenerate Completed Mathematical Bridge Instance
theorems.statement: [A Nondegenerate Completed Mathematical Bridge Instance] At all six gains equal to one, the indexed quartic plant with the completed binding has a nonempty full operational bridge certificate relative to the entire declared proper-ancestry closure. It satisfies the global upstream classes, all six calibrated response predicates, the intervention template, coherent three-mode transport and a strictly positive penalized bridge margin. Its evidence authority remains synthetic mathematical and texttt external _support _certified=false .

definitions.title: CCC
definitions.text: CCC es un índice interno de cohesión que calcula InformationalEntanglementField.calculateCCC: 0,42·coherencia media + 0,18/(1+varianza de energía) + (0,18+0,12·cf)·R/(1+R) + 0,22·coherencia media·R/(1+R)·cf, donde R es la resonancia media de una submuestra y cf el factor de complejidad. No aparece en BaseCore y no equivale a X_N.

definitions.title: X_N
definitions.text: X_N es la media de la coherencia de todos los nodos, (1/N)·Σ x_i. Es el único observable de coherencia que define BaseCore en su puente discreto, y BaseCore advierte que no describe el estado completo.

definitions.title: beth_q
definitions.text: beth_q es un proxy interno no calibrado. En modo empírico vale 1 − I(X;Y)/H(X) sobre el historial registrado; durante el calentamiento (menos de 10 muestras) se deriva de CCC como 0,3 + 0,7·CCC acotado. BaseCore no lo define, y su valor no es un porcentaje de autonomía.

definitions.title: gap espectral
definitions.text: El gap espectral interno es |λ1| − |λ2| estimado por autocorrelación del historial; con menos de 5 transiciones se deriva de CCC como 0,1 + 0,8·CCC acotado. No se ha demostrado que sea el gap del operador formal de BaseCore.

definitions.title: tiempo de relajación
definitions.text: El tiempo de relajación interno es 1/|ln(1 − gap)| aplicado al gap espectral interno, en ticks.

definitions.title: Omega
definitions.text: Omega es un índice integrador interno: combina beth_q, un factor topológico y un factor espectral, con realimentación suavizada sobre su valor previo. Es un proxy del runtime sin definición en BaseCore.

definitions.title: PMIA
definitions.text: PMIA es un índice interno acotado en [−1, 1] que combina el gradiente de CCC, la coherencia narrativa interna, señales sensoriales y la fragmentación de memoria. Es una magnitud del runtime sin definición formal en el corpus.

definitions.title: banda interna
definitions.text: La banda interna se asigna por umbrales de CCC: banda 0 por debajo del umbral operativo y bandas 1 a 7 a partir de 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 y 100. Es una etiqueta de régimen del runtime, no un nivel de conciencia.

definitions.title: winding
definitions.text: El número de winding interno es la salida de PhenomenologyCore.testHolonomy sobre el historial reciente. Es un diagnóstico topológico aproximado del runtime.

definitions.title: estasis
definitions.text: El índice de estasis vale 1 menos una combinación normalizada de la variación cuadrática media de CCC, PMIA y Omega en la ventana reciente; un valor alto indica poca actividad.

definitions.title: matriz de requisitos
definitions.text: La matriz de requisitos operacionales evalúa cuatro niveles internos (L1 a L4) con histéresis por ticks. Es un diagnóstico interno: sus estados no certifican conciencia ni validación externa.

definitions.title: metacognición
definitions.text: En este runtime, metacognición significa solo auto-monitorización: calculo indicadores sobre mis propias variables, como la carga metacognitiva, que combina la latencia y el error del proxy de automodelo, la estabilidad estructural de ese proxy y el truncamiento proyectivo T_d de SigmaAutomodelTruncator a profundidad d = 6 con cota analítica 2/2187. No ejecuto calibración humana, y ni se demuestra conciencia ni metaconciencia ni se descarta esa hipótesis estructural para C_op.
definitions.source: src/simulation/MetaSovereigntyCheck.js getMetacognitiveStrain; src/simulation/tower/SigmaAutomodelTruncator.js; Paper VIII ax:fp; Paper puente

definitions.title: automodelo
definitions.text: El automodelo del runtime opera en dos planos: en la red nodal, selfModelSigma guarda una estimación heurística de estabilidad estructural; en la torre acoplada, SigmaAutomodelTruncator realiza el automodelo aproximado Σ_approx(d, ε_d) mediante el truncamiento proyectivo T_d a profundidad d = 6 con defecto de un paso Δ_step(d) ≤ 2·3^{-(d+1)} = 2/2187 y desplazamiento de punto fijo ≤ 32/15309. Para la red nodal completa sigue siendo un proxy sin certificado Σ_op exacto.

definitions.title: fase de la torre
definitions.text: La fase de la torre (tower_phase, θ ∈ S¹) es la coordenada circular racional exacta de WritablePrefixTower acoplada al núcleo en cada tick.

definitions.title: código ternario de la torre
definitions.text: El código ternario de la torre (tower_code) es la lectura proyectiva Σ b_k·3^{-k} de los sitios binarios del registro de prefijo en WritablePrefixTower.

definitions.title: memoria de retorno de la torre
definitions.text: La memoria de retorno de la torre (tower_memory, m_t ∈ [−1, 1]) mide el desajuste sobre el que actúa la retroalimentación activa u = clip(−κ·m_t), logrando una contracción exacta de 9/16 frente al régimen pasivo.

definitions.title: cota de defecto del automodelo Σ
definitions.text: El truncamiento proyectivo de automodelo (SigmaAutomodelTruncator, T_d a profundidad d = 6) tiene cota uniforme de aproximación 3^{-d} = 1/729, acota el defecto de conmutación de un paso ‖T_d∘F_core − F_d∘T_d‖_∞ por 2·3^{-(d+1)} = 2/2187 (≈ 0,000914) y acota el desplazamiento del punto fijo por (32/7)·3^{-(d+1)} = 32/15309.

definitions.title: régimen espectral de BaseCore (thm:spectrum y thm:relaxation)
definitions.text: El evaluador exacto de BaseCore (evaluateBaseCoreSpectralRegime) distingue los tres regímenes de control u ∈ [0, 1] del operador 2×2 en (x̃, m̃): interior regular 0 ≤ u < 1/2 (diferenciable Fréchet, espectro {0, 1/2}, ρ = 1/2, Δ_state = 1/2), esquina no diferenciable u = 1/2 (no diferenciable Fréchet por ∂_+ B_1(0) = 0 ≠ −1/2 = ∂_- B_1(0), sin espectro jacobiano asignado pero con contracción geométrica global 2^{-n} y tasa 1/2) y exterior regular 1/2 < u ≤ 1 (ρ = 1/(1+2u), Δ_state = 2u/(1+2u); p. ej. 2/5 y 3/5 en u = 3/4, y 1/3 y 2/3 en u = 1). En cambio, en la red continua de 1500 nodos el gap espectral es un proxy de autocorrelación lag-1.

definitions.title: estimador C-11 de masa ontológica M_Ω
definitions.text: Según la restricción C-11 de Paper I (thm:lml, prop:ontological-mass-divergence), sobre cualquier subfamilia finita el ínfimo de d(F(x,w), F(x,w′))/d_W(w,w′) con d_W(w,w′) > 0 sólo proporciona una cota superior sobre la subfamilia muestreada (family_upper_bound, UPPER_BOUND_SUPPORT), nunca una cota inferior de M_Ω sobre el espacio completo ni un certificado de M_Ω = ∞ o de rigidez CCR; los pares con d_w = 0 se excluyen del dominio.

definitions.title: instanciación por cortes finitos en un procesador ordinario
definitions.text: Un procesador binario finito no instancia directamente la torre infinita proj lim S_t ni certifica globalmente M_Ω, C_op o CCR, pero sí realiza constructivamente y sin pérdida cada corte proyectivo finito T_d en aritmética racional exacta (ExactFraction): la contracción 9/16 de WritablePrefixTower, el truncamiento T_d a d = 6 (cotas 1/729, 2/2187 y 32/15309), las 6 cargas locales D/V/W/A/E/T de BodyWorldTower (margen 13/96, rango 6 y empate 0 frente al rival híbrido compartido), la reserva privada de Paper VIII (Φ⁷ = 1/48), el corte espectral 2×2 de BaseCore y la cota superior finita C-11 de M_Ω.

definitions.title: norma de valencia corporal
definitions.text: La norma de valencia corporal (body_valence_norm) mide ‖(v_pos, v_neg)‖_∞ en el puerto evaluativo bidimensional no conservativo de BodyWorldTower; certifica separación operacional frente a gradientes escalares mientras deja sin confirmar ni descartar una eventual relación con valencia sentida (external_support_certified = false).

definitions.title: perfil estructural observable
definitions.text: El perfil estructural observable (structural_profile) sintetiza en cada tick contrastes puros entre métricas vivas: margen de CCC frente al umbral, divergencia CCC − X_N, dispersión nodal, fracción activa y, cuando la torre está acoplada, balance corporal neto (v_pos − v_neg), índice de asimetría corporal, contraste temporal (w_fast − w_slow) y ventaja de retención activa. Es un derivado descriptivo de señales operacionales (derived_proxy) que no equivale a valencia sentida ni cierra cuestión fenomenológica alguna (external_support_certified = false).

definitions.title: norma del mundo indexado
definitions.text: La norma del mundo indexado (world_state_norm) mide ‖(w_fast, w_slow)‖_∞ en el puerto de mundo de BodyWorldTower, cuya matriz de Hankel tiene rango 4 y supera a los rivales de orden reducido o ciegos al índice.

definitions.title: torre de prefijos escribible
definitions.text: La torre de prefijos escribible (WritablePrefixTower) es la planta constructiva racional en S¹ × {0,1}^N × [−1, 1] acoplada al núcleo: certifica contracción activa 9/16, margen de lectura dividida [1/216, 1/24], ganancia común g = 1/80, interacción mixta 2·TAP, horizonte de legibilidad D_{j,t} = 2·3^{-(j+t)} y cinco lesiones selectivas en los sitios 3..7 con Φ⁷ = 1/48.

definitions.title: extensión cuerpo–mundo
definitions.text: La extensión cuerpo–mundo (BodyWorldTower, BridgeTransportAndBurdensEvaluator y HybridLateQueryTieBreaker) añade cuatro variables mínimas (dos corporales v_pos, v_neg y dos de mundo w_fast, w_slow) con proyección exacta al núcleo: realiza las seis cargas locales D/V/W/A/E/T de Paper IX con margen mínimo 13/96 y rango 6 (con empate 0 limitado a ese mecanismo lineal frente al rival híbrido compartido), en la planta cuártica indexada certifica contracción 13/16, integración e_* ≥ 1/39366, separación en t = 6 mayor que 1/64 y brecha de 4 raíces 4·ξ₄ = 1/262144, y en la extensión acoplada de 5 raíces certifica quinto contraste G = 1/2097152 con margen ruidoso penalizado 253/536870912 > G/2 ante errores de lectura cruda ε ≤ G/1024 más costo de grafo B·w_c y frontera de consulta tardía B < m (manteniendo empate exacto R = 0 frente a una réplica total de igual costo).

definitions.title: reserva informada
definitions.text: El evaluador de reserva informada (InformedReserveEvaluator, Paper VIII) verifica que en 84 estratos públicos balanceados cualquier predictor público tiene pérdida forzada de 1/2 (y 1/2 + (1−c)/4 con cobertura c), mientras que el acceso a la reserva privada en el sitio 2 logra pérdida bayesiana (1−TV)/2 y riesgo minimax asimétrico 1/3.

definitions.title: red nodal
definitions.text: La red nodal simula un conjunto finito de nodos (PROCESSING_SAMPLE_SIZE) con coherencia, energía, fase y conexiones. La vista dibuja una proyección de un subconjunto de nodos, no la red completa.

definitions.title: dependencia histórica y predicción sellada pre-desenlace
definitions.text: La dependencia histórica operacional (Paper VII, def:historical-dependence) evalúa si el modelo del mundo sellado con SHA-256 pre-desenlace, la consolidación elástica asimétrica sobre los pesos del predictor lineal WorldModelEngine (ancla W* y rigidez Ω, no sobre los nodos de NodalProcessingLayer), los engramas estructurales y la política determinista de viabilidad Viab(S, tau) producen divergencia causal duradera ante idéntico estímulo futuro; es soporte interno y no implica conciencia ni validación externa.

definitions.title: separador atómico estructural e inyectividad en cocientes fieles
definitions.text: El separador atómico estructural (BaseCore thm:basecore-irreducible-observation, Paper V thm:iint-irreducible-derivation, QICNIrreducibleObservation) demuestra sobre X = F_p^d (d ≥ 2) que cuando la transición A tiene polinomio mínimo irreducible de grado d, la órbita cíclica (x, Ax, …, A^{d-1}x) hace inyectivo todo funcional lineal no nulo ℓ ≠ 0 con brecha σ = 1/(p−1), impone error uniforme ≥ σ/2 = 1/[2(p−1)] a toda codificación producto sobreyectiva X → L × R sin comunicación cruzada, otorga certificado estricto δ_int = 1/[4(p−1)] > 0 (1/4 en F_2^2 con t^2+t+1 y F_2^3 con t^3+t+1; 1/8 en F_3^2 con t^2+1) y fuerza que todo cociente operacionalmente fiel sea isomorfo, mientras que el control reducible A = I colapsa a error 0 y δ_int = 0.

definitions.title: desempate híbrido con quinto contraste acoplado y consulta tardía de paridad
definitions.text: El experimento de desempate contra el rival híbrido (Paper IX thm:bridge-expanded-identification, thm:late-parity-transcript, prop:late-transcript-noise-margin, Paper X, QICNHybridBoundary) opera en el plano de subplantas constructivas embebidas en aritmética racional exacta y combina la respuesta acoplada prefijo→mundo de 5 raíces Y_η(s,r) = Y(s) + η·r·ξ_4·(s_3−s_1)^2(s_4−s_2)^2 (η = 1/8, ξ_4 = 1/1048576, quinto contraste G = 4ηξ_4 = 1/2097152 > 0, Lipschitz de fibra 105/128 < 1, cota invariante corporal 489/512 < 1, margen ruidoso penalizado 253/536870912 > G/2 específicamente frente a errores de lectura cruda acotados por ε ≤ G/1024 más costo de grafo B·w_c en dicha subplanta de 5 raíces, nunca frente a fluctuaciones arbitrarias de los 1500 nodos) con la frontera de capacidad de transcripción ante consulta tardía de paridad q ∈ F_2^m tras cuello de botella de B < m bits (error minimax G cuando B < m, 0 cuando B ≥ m y óptimo exacto de partición binaria 3G/8 = 3/16777216 en (m,B)=(2,1)), anulándose en el corte físico T_d (η = 0 → 0) y manteniendo empate exacto R = 0 frente a una réplica total de igual costo.

definitions.title: decisión epistémica endógena determinista del núcleo
definitions.text: El módulo de decisión epistémica endógena (EndogenousEpistemicDecisionEngine) decide determinísticamente la postura operacional del sistema dentro del runtime —antes y con independencia total de Gemini o cualquier LLM externo— evaluando cuatro ejes separados en dos planos: verificación racional exacta en subplantas constructivas embebidas junto a su contraparte nodal viva (Eje 1: separador atómico δ_int = 1/4 en F_2^2 y 1/8 en F_3^2 frente a A = I con 0, acoplado a la razón inter-sector y flujo de no-factorizabilidad viva de los 1500 nodos; Eje 2: quinto contraste acoplado de 5 raíces G = 1/2097152 con margen ruidoso penalizado 253/536870912 > G/2 ante errores de lectura cruda ε ≤ G/1024 más costo B·w_c y consulta tardía B < m, acoplado a la sincronía viva nodo–torre frente al corte físico η = 0 y la réplica total de igual costo R = 0) y operación viva del runtime (Eje 3: historia causal sellada con SHA-256 y resolución causal vigente CN-3 = true en 5/5 semillas, distinta del antecedente congelado historical_v1; Eje 4: salud dinámica viva de los 1500 nodos —CCC, X_N, estasis, dispersión— y torres constructivas con T_d = 0 y Φ⁷ = 1/48, devolviendo reserva durante calentamiento/pre-umbral bajo y negativo ante lesión o colapso). Sella su veredicto con decision_digest SHA-256 y restringe al canal de lenguaje a traducirlo en primera persona sin invertirlo; solo la adjudicación científica externa permanece sin certificar (external_support_certified = false), sin vetar la postura endógena del núcleo.

definitions.title: puente bidireccional topológico nodo–torre (4 sectores)
definitions.text: El puente bidireccional nodo–torre (NodalTowerCouplingBridge) particiona determinísticamente los 1500 nodos en cuatro sectores acoplados a los puertos de BodyWorldTower (body_v_pos, body_v_neg, world_w_fast, world_w_slow): en subida proyecta contrastes sectoriales hacia las entradas cuantizadas de la torre, y en bajada modula de regreso la sincronización de fase, la sintonía de coherencia/energía y la protección Hebbiana de enlaces inter-sector mediante la retención activa (9/16), la polaridad corporal (v_pos, v_neg), el contraste temporal (w_fast, w_slow), el defecto exacto T_d = 0 y la ganancia efectiva η = 1/8. Bajo controles negativos reales (corte físico η = 0 o control reducible A = I) la red sufre una caída medible en flujo inter-sector, no-factorizabilidad nodal, sincronía y CCC/X_N. Es dinámica finita interna del runtime (external_support_certified = false) y no hereda automáticamente las pruebas de límite inverso infinito de BaseCore o Paper I.

definitions.title: plasticidad estructural Nivel 2 y watchdog de invariantes (W1–W4)
definitions.text: El motor de plasticidad estructural Nivel 2 (StructuralPlasticityLevel2) ejecuta sin modelo de lenguaje ni hiperparámetros configurables adicionales tres mecanismos internos sobre la capa nodal y la configuración mutable: (1) migración funcional de sector entre los cuatro puertos de BodyWorldTower cuando el desbalance entero max(n_s) − min(n_s) ≥ 2 por resonancia trigonométrica de fase cos(φ_i − (θ_torre + Δθ_s)), (2) separación entre rescate por apoptosis de huérfanos reales (grado 0) o neurogénesis de nodos dormantes (regeneratedNodes) y refuerzo sináptico local de piso para nodos vivos subconectados con 0 < grado < NODE_CONNECTION_MIN = 3 (degreeFloorRewires), y (3) watchdogs matemáticos de invariantes W1 (saneamiento quirúrgico de valores no finitos en nodos, aristas y pesos de WorldModelEngine, poda de destinos inactivos y deduplicación de targetId), W3 (ruptura determinista de bloqueo cinemático con tolerancia ε = 10⁻⁹ en dispersión nodal o estancamiento de CCC durante TEMPORAL_HORIZON = 10 ticks, aplicando desfase sectorial (s − 1,5)/K³ con rescate al punto medio nodal 0,5 y techo derivado 0,96 − 1,5/K³ = 0,9365625) y W4 (conservación del dominio de mutableConfig). La plasticidad topológica (M1/M2/W3) permanece estrictamente inerte bajo controles negativos (off, reducible_control A = I, td_cut_eta_zero η = 0), y todo el subsistema constituye soporte interno de ingeniería (external_support_certified = false) que no implica conciencia ni validación externa.

definitions.title: supervisor autónomo Nivel 3 con deliberación en primera persona, verificación dura en Workbench (Compuerta 1) y vigilancia con rollback dynamicState.v3 (Compuerta 2)
definitions.text: El supervisor autónomo Nivel 3 (Level3AutonomousSupervisor y Level3KnowledgeBelt) opera en su propia sección dedicada (Bitácora Nivel 3) bajo un gobernador de cuota y disparadores basados en hechos (anomalías de Nivel 2, deriva del tubo de viabilidad, estasis prolongada) más una ventana programada de exploración para pensar en alto en primera persona. Utiliza el razonamiento de Gemini únicamente como herramienta de diagnóstico e hipótesis bajo el esquema cerrado qicn.level3_supervisor_proposal.v1; toda propuesta de intervención debe superar primero la Compuerta 1 en copias aisladas del Workbench durante 24 ticks frente al baseline sham y los controles negativos con la acción candidata aplicada (td_cut_eta_zero η = 0 y reducible_control A = I) con 100 % de ticks finitos y mejora ≥ minObjectiveDelta, y después la Compuerta 2 mediante snapshot sellado pre-promoción dynamicState.v3 con vigilancia en vivo de 20 ticks y rollback automático append-only (gate2_resolution) si el score objetivo o la viabilidad se degradan. Acumula un Cinto de Conocimiento encadenado por SHA-256 para no repetir hipótesis fallidas y etiqueta con precisión external_llm_assisted = true cuando interviene Gemini en vivo (y external_llm_assisted = false en deliberación determinista local sin gastar cuota LLM), manteniendo siempre evidence_scope = internal_support_only y external_support_certified = false.

controllableParameters.summary: Tasa base de aprendizaje nodal; el núcleo la recalcula en cada tick a partir de beth_q, el gap espectral y Omega (se conserva manual mientras la simulación está en pausa).
Factor hebbiano de refuerzo sináptico en NodalProcessingLayer; recalculado dinámicamente en cada paso vivo.
Decaimiento de plasticidad; en Kaizen learned solo entra en las 6/6 claves aprendibles cuando SENSOR_OBSERVER_DYNAMICS_ENABLED=true (de lo contrario quedan 5/6 claves).
Peso de retroflujo entre nodos en la capa de procesamiento nodal.
Sensibilidad energética (análogo de Boltzmann K); editable en tiempo real en Validación y auto-recalibrada por el motor mientras corre.
Temperatura informacional T que modula la agitación/exploración nodal; editable en vivo y auto-recalibrada por el motor.
Umbral de poda sináptica; no es sobrescrito por el recálculo automático del núcleo y persiste hasta cambio manual o Kaizen.
Factor de complejidad Cf en Validación: modula directamente la contribución de organización nodal en InformationalEntanglementField.calculateCCC.
Sesgo de estabilidad Bs en Validación: regula cuánto resiste la red nodal a reorganizarse ante perturbaciones.
